Grammis is one of IDS’s most widely used online resources and is aimed at students, teachers, and anyone interested in linguistics.

relatedItems.label: grammis - Systematische Grammatik
relatedItems.description:
Systematische Grammatik bietet eine wissenschaftlich fundierte Beschreibung der deutschen Grammatik aus syntaktischer, semantischer und kommunikativ-funktionaler Perspektive. Ausdruckseinheiten wie Wörter, Phrasen sowie einfache und komplexe Sätze werden syntaktisch nach ihren Funktionen und semantisch nach ihrer Bedeutung beschrieben. Zudem werden die syntagmatischen und paradigmatischen Beziehungen zwischen diesen Einheiten dokumentiert und die sprachlichen Mittel vorgestellt, die zur Bewältigung verschiedener kommunikativer Aufgaben dienen. Damit liefert Systematische Grammatik eine umfassende, empirisch gestützte Darstellung der deutschen Gegenwartssprache für Forschung und Lehre.

---

The Systematic Grammar provides a scholarly description of German grammar from syntactic, semantic, and communicative-functional perspectives. Units of expression such as words, phrases, and simple and complex sentences are described syntactically in terms of their functions and semantically in terms of their meanings. The description also documents the syntagmatic and paradigmatic relations between these units and presents the linguistic resources used to accomplish various communicative tasks. In this way, The Systematic Grammar offers a comprehensive, empirically grounded account of contemporary German for research and teaching.

relatedItems.label: grammis - Valenzwörterbuch
relatedItems.description:
Das Wörterbuch zur Verbvalenz enthält grammatisch relevante Informationen zu knapp 700 ausgewählten deutschen Verben. Für jedes Verb werden Strukturbeispiele (Anzahl und Semantik der Komplemente), Satzbaupläne (Komplementstrukturen) und Belegungsregeln (grammatische Realisierung der Komplemente) übersichtlich dargestellt. Zudem liefert es Angaben zur Konjugationsklasse, Passivfähigkeit, Bedeutung, Stilebene und Aussprache. Jeder Eintrag beginnt mit einem Artikelkopf, der allgemeine Informationen zu Aussprache, Stammformen und Konjugation bietet, gefolgt von einer anklickbaren Liste unterschiedlicher Lesarten. Das integrierte Suchformular ermöglicht die gezielte Recherche über verschiedene Filteroptionen.

---

The Verb Valency Dictionary provides grammatically relevant information for nearly 700 selected German verbs. For each verb, structure examples (number and semantics of complements), sentence-frame plans (complement structures), and assignment rules (grammatical realization of complements) are clearly presented. In addition, the dictionary gives information on conjugation class, passive capability, meaning, stylistic register, and pronunciation. Each entry begins with a header providing general information on pronunciation, stem forms, and conjugation, followed by a clickable list of different readings. The integrated search form allows for targeted queries using various filter options.

relatedItems.label: OpenArchaeo - Semantic web plateform for archaeological data
relatedItems.description:
MASA (Mémoire des Archéologues et des Sites Archéologiques), a consortium of the TGIR Huma-Num, in partnership with the SPARNA company, specialized in semantic web, and the Laboratoire d’Informatique Fondamentale et Appliquée de Tours (LIFAT), has developed the OpenArchaeo semantic web platform. Exploiting the archaeological triplestores paired with the CIDOC in a federated way, OpenArchaeo has been designed with two distinct interfaces.
The Explorer, resolutely user-friendly, is based on a system of icons and concepts well understood by archaeologists (Stratigraphic Unit, Artifact, Feature, Site...). In order to produce a SPARQL query from the natural language, OpenArchaeo has been the subject of the development of the SPARNATURAL component, which is modular and reusable. This system enables to generate a SPARQL query intuitively, without knowledge of the SPARQL language, but with knowledge of the main concepts of archaeology.
The SPARQL endpoint is a query service to write federated queries to multiple sources in SPARQL language (query language dedicated to the semantic web). This interface is associated with web services to exploit the MASA Triplestore. Its purpose is to be operated by machines and is therefore more accessible to computer specialists.

relatedItems.label: TextGrid - Import Workflow for Data aka The Fluffy Import
relatedItems.description:
How do I import textual research data in the TextGrid Repository?

Researchers repeatedly articulate their need for well-usable tools and infrastructures for the easy creation and publication of text-based research data. This also applies to Text+ and is exemplified by the Text+ User Stories. The partners involved in Text+, including SUB Göttingen, GWDG, and TU Dresden, contribute to this—for example, with the new developments tested at the 2024 Code Sprint for Humanities Data.

Thanks to its extensive, searchable, and reusable collection of texts and images, TextGridRep is an important and relevant repository for humanities research data.

For researchers, it offers a sustainable, permanent, and secure means of citable publication of their research data and a clear description of the same through necessary and extended metadata so that the publication in TextGridRep can be presented and reused. Results were achieved on various levels, which were presented and used on the occasion of the Code Sprint. TextGridRep was further developed in terms of authentication, the presentation of unpublished projects, and data intake. A new tool was developed for generating the required TextGrid metadata files, which detects the metadata in the teiHeader elements of the input files and also allows the manual setting of values and rules for their discovery. A web-based tool enabling convenient workflow operation was implemented as a Jupyter Notebook. For easy use of this tool, the Text+ JupyterHub is available. It was also adapted on this occasion so that the mentioned tools are already installed and can be used without further ado.

This workflow describes the new fluffy import in the TextGrid Repository.

relatedItems.label: Deposit in HAL
relatedItems.description:
Carry out your deposit on hal.science — the French national open archive — under the document type "Software". In the "Automatic extraction" subsection, paste the SWHID obtained in Step 2 into the designated field; HAL will extract the metadata from your codemeta.json file and pre-populate the form automatically. This automation is not merely a time-saving convenience: it ensures consistency between the metadata declared in HAL and those archived in Software Heritage, a condition essential to the interoperability of both systems.
Verify and complete the mandatory fields — software name, thematic domain, licence information, and author list with at least one institutional affiliation. These elements form the minimum basis of any scientifically valid record. The optional fields — keywords, production date, programming language, development status, ANR or European project reference, link to the code repository — are far from incidental: they directly determine the visibility and citability of your software across academic information retrieval systems.
At the final stage of your deposit, accept the transfer to Software Heritage. This step is what enables the SWHID to be inscribed in your HAL record and in citation exports, ensuring the long-term traceability of your contribution. Your deposit then enters a moderation phase.

concept.label: PNG
concept.definition: Portable Network Graphics (PNG, pronounced PEE-en-JEE or PING) is a raster graphics file format that supports lossless data compression. PNG was created as an improved, non-patented replacement for Graphics Interchange Format (GIF), and is the most widely used lossless image compression format on the Internet. PNG supports palette-based images (with palettes of 24-bit RGB or 32-bit RGBA colors), grayscale images (with or without alpha channel for transparency), and full-color non-palette-based RGB/RGBA images (with or without alpha channel). PNG was designed for transferring images on the Internet, not for professional-quality print graphics, and therefore does not support non-RGB color spaces such as CMYK. A PNG file contains a single image in an extensible structure of "chunks", encoding the basic pixels and other information such as textual comments and integrity checks documented in RFC 2083. PNG files nearly always use file extension PNG or png and are assigned MIME media type image/png. PNG was published as informational RFC 2083 in March 1997 and as an ISO/IEC standard in 2004.

relatedItems.label: HedgeDoc - GWDG Pad
relatedItems.description:
Online tool for collaborative text editing to work together on the same texts at the same time.

The HedgeDoc-pad is an open-source-based web editor that allows multiple users to work on a single text simultaneously from different locations. Users can work collaboratively on the same document at the same time without having to send files back and forth.

With the export function, the pad can be saved in different formats and an import from existing files is also possible. The TimeSlider can also be used to restore different processing conditions.

The 'Share this pad' function allows the URL to be shared with other users (also those who are not signed in). It is possible to manage and change the access permission of a note.
For each pad a registration with the DARIAH account or with your home institution data is required. See for more information the data privacy note.

To access the service you need to login via the Academic Cloud (https://academiccloud.de/home): either with a registered e-mail adress (if your academic home institution is based in Niedersachsen, Germany) or via the federated login with your DARIAH account or your instutional account. Please note, that regardless of which account you choose here, you should always make the same selection for all subsequent logins, as your profile and thus, also your data and your entries will be linked to this identity.

This resource is supported by Text+. In case of questions you may get in touch with the Text+ helpdesk at textplus-support@gwdg.de.

label: Heimdall
description:
**HEIMDALL** is a tool for converting more easily one or more databases from one format to another.

If, for example, you find yourself in one of the following situations…

- you need to **access** data, but it is not stored in a format compatible with your favorite software…
- you’d prefer to **merge** several heterogeneous databases into a single corpus, easier to analyze…
- you’re considering which format to use for your software or database…
- you want to make data more **accessible** and **interoperable**…

… then HEIMDALL can offer you an exchange format, and abstract the details of data implementation: yours, but also those of others.
Thanks to HEIMDALL, you can also switch from one technology to another in a matter of moments, as and when you need to, without ever losing, disorganizing or corrupting your data –or even by improving them over time, documenting them and linking them to current standards in your field.

In a nutshell, HEIMDALL is your **H**igh-**E**nd **I**nteroperability **M**odule when **D**ata is **ALL** over the place. It’s a bridge between scattered islands of data. ⚔️🌉🌈

relatedItems.label: Interoperability of Scientific Databases: a Facade of Sobriety
relatedItems.description:
Any task is more sustainable if it consumes fewer resources, over its entire lifecycle. Some of the challenges of Digital Humanities are tasks related to interoperability between databases, such as documentation, alignment, migration and publication. Often requiring specialized knowledge, these tasks can quickly become time-consuming. After reviewing the context in which these tasks are generally undertaken, this article will propose solutions for reducing their consumption of resources, of human resources in particular. Finally, it will discuss the benefits and limitations of these solutions.


This article is in French.

label: Hermetic Word Frequency Counter
description: This software scans a Word DOCX file or a text file (including HTML and XML files) with text encoded via ANSI or UTF-8 and counts the frequencies of different words. The words which are found and displayed can be ordered alphabetically or by frequency. Characters which can appear in words can be specified, so the program can be told to allow or disallow words with numerals, hyphens, apostrophes, underscores or colons, to ignore words which are short or which occur infrequently, to treat upper/lower case as significant or not, and to ignore words (e.g., common words such as 'this', a.k.a. stop words) contained in a specified file. This software may be used with text in most European languages. The language of the text is detected automatically and (if supported) the corresponding stop words file is optionally loaded. Results can be exported to Excel for further processing. There is also an Advanced Version with greater functionality.

The program can be told to allow or disallow words with numerals, hyphens, apostrophes, underscores or colons, to ignore words which are short or which occur infrequently, and to ignore words (e.g., common words such as 'the', a.k.a. stop words) contained in a specified file. It can also count only words or phrases in a specified list (optionally with pattern-matching). Results can be exported to Excel for further processing. label: Heurist
description:
HEURIST is a unique, researcher-friendly Open Source solution to the data management needs of a broad range of Humanities researchers. Heurist is discipline agnostic, from archaeological and historical data, through literature and art, to contemporary cultural research. Developed since 2005, it is an extremely comprehensive system which supports hundreds of diverse projects and data-generated websites, ranging from individual doctoral research to large projects such as ERC, ANR, AHRC and ARC projects. It supports thousands of users and provides a free service through servers supported by public research infrastructure in Europe and Australia. 

Heurist is a truly research-led Humanities data management infrastructure that has evolved through feedback from hundreds of projects over two decades to give researchers, of all stripes, without the need for programmers or consultants, the ability to design, populate, explore and publish their own richly-structured, heterogeneous database(s)  through a simple web interface. It puts the control of the data back in the hands of researchers rather than chaining them to the availability, time schedules and miscommunications of dealing with external developers.

Heurist supports incremental database design, allowing database structure to be modified on the fly as needs or understanding evolve; entity types, fields and connections can be added and modified freely without corrupting existing data. Database structure can be published and used in a new database. It has a rich range of field types to handle text, numeric, classifications, dates (including fuzzy dates), spatial information, images, audio, video and 3D. Building relationships is as simple as defining a pointer field and specifying what entity types(s) it should point to, what relationship types to allow, and whether you can set up multiple connections eg. to Authors or a single connection eg. to findspot. Data can be imported, verified and normalised from external sources such as spreadsheets and legacy databases, or looked up in reference collections.

Heurist has all functions available from the start: data driven websites, layered workgroup control to manage access to data, sophisticated searching including wizard setup of facet searches,  simple descriptvie tables, mapping and timelines, network diagrams, custom reporting, and multiple export formats including archival formats. Software updates are automatic and seamless, and there is a responsive help desk and user forum. Development is very active with more than 1000 program commits per year (2024). 

Heurist can also leverage the work of developers by fast-tracking a database and providing complete data management solutions within hours to days rather than weeks or months. The source code to set up a local service is available on gitHub or through installation scripts on the Heurist web site (recommended method), but most projects/users should use one of the free servers provided by the public research infrastructure partners, for which the development team provide direct support.

In terms of sustainability, Heurist uses widely used Open Source components - MySQL, PHP, Javascript - and builds well-structured MySQL relational databases while hiding the complexity of the structure from the user. As long as a server and the Heurist code on it are maintained, all databases and websites created on that serve should remain operational. For peace of mind, archival downloads are available with a few clicks, so that data is not locked into Heurist. The archival files are comprehensive and in easily interpreted formats (SQL, XML, CSV files, original uploaded files, and include extensive documentation), and allow the transfer of a database to a new server or to a completely different data system.

label: Historical documents page classifier - archival scans categorization by content type
description:
Sorts scanned pages of archival documents into 11 content categories, so that each page goes to the processing it needs: OCR or HTR of typed, printed or handwritten text, table extraction, or extraction of drawings and photos. The categories (DRAW, DRAW_L, LINE_HW, LINE_P, LINE_T, PHOTO, PHOTO_L, TEXT, TEXT_HW, TEXT_P, TEXT_T) were formed from archival documents of 1920–2020.

Fine-tuned ViT, RegNetY and EfficientNetV2 models, usable singly or as an averaged ensemble (`--best`), are published on the Hugging Face Hub and were trained on 48,499 manually annotated pages released at LINDAT. The tool covers PDF-to-PNG preparation, top-N predictions for single images or directories, CSV summary tables, training and evaluation, with a paradata JSON log per run.

Command-line tool or REST API container image (`ghcr.io/ufal/atrium-page-classification-api`: `/predict_image` for JPG/PNG, `/predict_document` for PDF).

relatedItems.label: ALTO XMLs post-processing and quality control (text lines categorization)
relatedItems.description:
Turns OCR output into clean, classified text lines. The pipeline splits documents into pages, builds page statistics tables, extracts text in reading order (LayoutReader by default; alto-tools, GLM-4v, JSON-key and plain-text readers as alternatives) and labels every line by language and OCR quality: Clear, Noisy, Trash, Non-text or Empty. The quality score combines structural detectors, perplexity (Qwen2.5-0.5B or distilgpt2) and character-level metrics; the language comes from FastText.

Input: ALTO XML, generic OCR JSON, or any text-bearing file (PDF, DOCX, TXT, HTML, TEI, PAGE XML and more). Output: per-line CSV tables, page statistics, plain text and the ATRIUM document record (JSON), with a paradata JSON log per run.

Command-line pipeline or REST API container image (`ghcr.io/ufal/atrium-alto-postprocess-api`, `/process`).

relatedItems.label: Semi-automated extraction of information from textual documents in a domain-specific repository
relatedItems.description:
The workflow addresses the **machine processing and enhancement of archaeological textual documents** (e.g., grey literature, excavation reports, field forms) held in a domain-specific repository. It processes both **scanned documents**, through automatic text recognition, and **born-digital documents** (PDF, DOCX) that already carry a text layer. The goal is an integrated solution for **legacy data and new uploads within the selected repository system**: better search and reuse of the documents, and fewer manual steps in archiving and annotation.

The workflow chains **independent tools available as services through APIs**. Each tool performs one step: page classification, OCR quality control, linguistic annotation and named entity recognition, keyword extraction against the domain vocabularies, and translation. Each tool can also be used on its own. The repository calls the services asynchronously and stores every result as an **alternative distribution of the original file**, with a **paradata** record describing the run that produced it (tool version, parameters, licence).

The results of all steps also accumulate in **one JSON record per document** (the ATRIUM document record). Its blocks each have one producing tool, so any step can be re-run alone. The record carries the provenance of every contribution, and the licence of the combined result is derived from the most restrictive licence among them. It can later be exported as an RO-Crate.

The enriched data support:

* full-text and faceted search by page types, named entities and vocabulary keywords,
* assessment of OCR quality before further processing,
* linking of documents to controlled vocabularies and to each other,
* international access through English translations of metadata and texts,
* corpora for natural language processing, including the training and evaluation of models.

The tools were developed in the [ATRIUM project](https://atrium-research.eu/) by the Institute of Formal and Applied Linguistics (Charles University) with the Institutes of Archaeology of the Czech Academy of Sciences in Prague and Brno. They are open source, published as container images, and are described in their own Marketplace records. Their integration into [Galaxy](https://galaxyproject.org/) is being prepared with DARIAH.

The [Archaeological Map of the Czech Republic (AMCR)](https://digiarchiv.aiscr.cz/) repository serves as the **demonstrator** of the workflow.

**Diagram caption**: *Users and data curators work with a data repository (AMCR) that stores each document with its metadata, original file, ALTO XML, document record, enrichments and paradata, and the AMCR vocabularies. A processing orchestration (step 2) passes documents between the repository, a separate automatic text recognition workflow (step 4) and the ATRIUM tool services: page classification (3), ALTO post-processing and quality control (5), NLP enrichment with UDPipe and NameTag to TEITOK (7), vocabulary keywords by LLM (8) and XML translation (10). A dashed born-digital branch (6) replaces steps 4 and 5. NLP enrichment and translation call the LINDAT services; the vocabularies feed keyword extraction and translation. Annotators and data engineers train a custom NameTag model (9). A discovery service (11) serves users and feeds the OAI-PMH and File API, which feeds the ARIADNE Portal.*

label: Historisches Grundbuch der Stadt Basel Nested NER
description:
Tagger for Historical Texts, mainly 15th to 18th century German.

Developed by Ismail Prada Ziegler.

A model for historical German developed as part of the project Economies of Space. Practices, Discourses, and Actors on the Basel Real Estate Market (1400-1700) at the University of Basel and the Digital Humanities Bern. This Model was created to annotate nested document structures. It can be used to annotate flat text (such as in the example), but may perform slightly worse than models trained only for that task. 
Dataset
Not yet published dataset created from the Historical Land Registry of the city of Basel. Timeframe: 1400-1700. Language: Early New High German. 661 documents in train, 83 in dev. Language model based on the full HLRB corpus until 1800, appr. 120k documents.

The documents were annotated according to the BeNASch annotation guidelines. For this model, a simplified tagset was used.

The training data was prepared in a special way to accommodate nested annotation. See the linked paper for more information.

Citation
If you publish works using this model, please cite:

Prada Ziegler, I. (2024, May 30). What's in an entity? Exploring Nested Named Entity Recognition in the Historical Land Register of Basel (1400-1700). DH Benelux 2024, Leuven, Belgium. Zenodo. https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.11394453

description:
History of Slovenia - Sistory portal represents the main research infrastructure for historical resources and rare historical literature in Slovenia. It also hosts digital archive for all main Slovenian historian magazines. It has bilingual interface and storages over 40000 different publications, mostly text in pdf format. 

Beyond its once primary goal to serve as a digital library for history related research is also a main source for TEI-XML annotated text databases in constant development, based on the diverse digitised and digital material - such as stenographic minutes of the Slovenian parliament (1945-2018), it also hosts the database of the population censuses from 1830 to 1937, most of them transcribed and accessible for the researchers in machine readable format, the database of the death-toll of WW II for Slovenia and TEI - XML based list of losses in the WW I for Slovenia, not to mention smaller scale databases, which are mostly the result of digitally enabled research. 

Its advanced archival system allows long-time preservation for all collected data, available in Open Access.

label: HRČAK - Portal of Croatian Scientific and Professional Journals
description:
HRČAK is the central portal for Croatian scientific and professional journals, serving as the national platform for facilitating Open Access publishing.  It provides access to over 540 Open Access journals and more than 299,000 full-text articles. The journals featured on the portal encompass a wide array of scientific disciplines and languages, and submissions are accepted from authors across the globe. 

HRČAK has been a community-driven idea, and the community contributes to the development of HRČAK through the Advisory Board. The portal is developed and maintained by SRCE – University of Zagreb University Computing Centre. 

Since its beginnings in 2006, HRČAK has been promoting and supporting Open Access and good publishing practices. Journal editors and publishers are offered tools to publish and enhance the openness and visibility of their journals, while offering the public a centralised platform to access the content from all available journals. Journal editors can also utilise the maintained instance of Open Journal Systems to oversee and streamline the editorial process. HRČAK prioritises interoperability ensuring that its content is discoverable through search services such as Google Scholar and OpenAIRE (data provider since 2015).

relatedItems.label: JATS XML Converter Service
relatedItems.description:
JATS XML Converter Service enables users to convert full-text Open Office (.docx) files to JATS XML (Journal Publishing v1.1). It is part of a service of Portal of Croatian scientific and professional journals HRČAK, developed and maintained by SRCE - University of Zagreb University Computing Centre.

JATS (Journal Article Tag Suite) is a set of elements and attributes used to describe scientific literature in XML format. It is open standard that enables content and reference mining, more sophisticated searching and access to articles, interactive interface and easier data exchange. JATS XML is an open format for publishing scientific and professional articles, offering numerous advantages such as easier content mining, enhanced data exchange, improved searchability and visibility of articles, and interactive content usage on user interfaces. Its importance is also emphasized in Plan S, which strongly recommends the use of machine-readable formats like JATS XML.

label: HT-Bookworm
description:
Bookworm is a tool that visualizes language usage trends in repositories of digitized texts in a simple and powerful way. It is a tool for culturomic exploration through the observation of chronological trends for words and phrases in large digitized collections of textual documents with metadata facets.



The world's great research libraries have, over time, carefully assembled a rich body of metadata pertaining to the books in their collections. Since the HTRC has access to volume-level metadata as well as volume-level content, we have constructed a Bookworm of the HathiTrust Non-Google-digitized public domain (NGPD) corpus. We felt that setting up Bookworm with a HathiTrust corpus would provides scholarly researchers with the means of exploring trends.



This tool enables scholars to discover new textual use patterns across the entire corpus. In the future, we plan to ingest the entire HathiTrust corpus and continue to identify appropriate metadata to use for the faceted browsing. This tool will be particularly useful to scholars interested in books that are still under copyright - which is the case for most books published after 1923. Although these books will not be available for reading or downloading online, working with individual words and phrases and tracking their occurrences through time will be useful to academic researchers, especially historians, sociologists and literary scholars.



John Unsworth has noted that a fundamental goal of the humanities is appreciation: "by paying attention to an object of interest, we can explore it, find new dimensions within it, notice things about it that have never been noticed before, and increase its value" (2004). Shifting from traditional close reading to a large-scale view of text presents a profound discomfort for humanities scholars, due to the difficulty in retaining the same sensitivity to what is actually contained in the works being studied. HTRC-Bookworm will function as a link between quantitative analysis (distant reading) and close reading. According to Frederick Gibbs and Daniel Cohen, "any robust digital research methodology must allow the scholar to move easily between distant and close reading, between the bird's eye view and the ground level of the texts themselves" (2011). This is what HTRC-Bookworm intends to accomplish (within the limitations of applicable copyright laws.)



Current limitations and future improvements:



The current instantiation (the alpha version) of the HTRC-Bookworm is set up to work with only 250,000 out-of-copyright volumes from the HathiTrust NGPD corpus. Overall the HathiTrust has more than 11,000,000 volumes in all their corpus, consisting of 420 billion pages.



As a demonstration we have selected some metadata for use with this smaller corpus, but we are open to feedback on improvements to this metadata.



Our plan is to ingest the larger HathiTrust corpus and to allow facets to be selected based on HTRC worksets.

concept.label: ASCII
concept.definition: ASCII abbreviated from American Standard Code for Information Interchange, is a character encoding standard for electronic communication. ASCII codes represent text in computers, telecommunications equipment, and other devices. Most modern character-encoding schemes are based on ASCII, although they support many additional characters. ASCII is the traditional name for the encoding system.

concept.label: JPEG
concept.definition: JPEG ( JAY-peg) is a commonly used method of lossy compression for digital images, particularly for those images produced by digital photography. The degree of compression can be adjusted, allowing a selectable tradeoff between storage size and image quality. JPEG typically achieves 10:1 compression with little perceptible loss in image quality. JPEG compression is used in a number of image file formats. JPEG/Exif is the most common image format used by digital cameras and other photographic image capture devices; along with JPEG/JFIF, it is the most common format for storing and transmitting photographic images on the World Wide Web. These format variations are often not distinguished, and are simply called JPEG. The term "JPEG" is an initialism/acronym for the Joint Photographic Experts Group, which created the standard. The MIME media type for JPEG is image/jpeg, except in older Internet Explorer versions, which provides a MIME type of image/pjpeg when uploading JPEG images. JPEG files usually have a filename extension of .jpg or .jpeg. JPEG/JFIF supports a maximum image size of 65,53565,535 pixels, hence up to 4 gigapixels for an aspect ratio of 1:1.

concept.label: PNG
concept.definition: Portable Network Graphics (PNG, pronounced PEE-en-JEE or PING) is a raster graphics file format that supports lossless data compression. PNG was created as an improved, non-patented replacement for Graphics Interchange Format (GIF), and is the most widely used lossless image compression format on the Internet. PNG supports palette-based images (with palettes of 24-bit RGB or 32-bit RGBA colors), grayscale images (with or without alpha channel for transparency), and full-color non-palette-based RGB/RGBA images (with or without alpha channel). PNG was designed for transferring images on the Internet, not for professional-quality print graphics, and therefore does not support non-RGB color spaces such as CMYK. A PNG file contains a single image in an extensible structure of "chunks", encoding the basic pixels and other information such as textual comments and integrity checks documented in RFC 2083. PNG files nearly always use file extension PNG or png and are assigned MIME media type image/png. PNG was published as informational RFC 2083 in March 1997 and as an ISO/IEC standard in 2004.

concept.label: TIFF
concept.definition: Tagged Image File Format, abbreviated TIFF or TIF, is a computer file format for storing raster graphics images, popular among graphic artists, the publishing industry, and photographers. TIFF is widely supported by scanning, faxing, word processing, optical character recognition, image manipulation, desktop publishing, and page-layout applications. The format was created by Aldus Corporation for use in desktop publishing. It published the latest version 6.0 in 1992, subsequently updated with an Adobe Systems copyright after the latter acquired Aldus in 1994. Several Aldus or Adobe technical notes have been published with minor extensions to the format, and several specifications have been based on TIFF 6.0, including TIFF/EP (ISO 12234-2), TIFF/IT (ISO 12639), TIFF-F (RFC 2306) and TIFF-FX (RFC 3949).

concept.label: XML
concept.definition: Extensible Markup Language (XML) is a markup language that defines a set of rules for encoding documents in a format that is both human-readable and machine-readable.

concept.label: Apache FOP
concept.definition: Apache FOP (Formatting Objects Processor) is a print formatter driven by XSL formatting objects (XSL-FO) and an output independent formatter. It is a Java application that reads a formatting object (FO) tree and renders the resulting pages to a specified output. Output formats currently supported include PDF, PS, PCL, AFP, XML (area tree representation), Print, AWT and PNG, and to a lesser extent, RTF and TXT. The primary output target is PDF

label: HTR-United
description:
HTR-United is a catalog of metadata on training datasets (ground truth datasets) available for the creation of transcription or segmentation models. The metadata are provided by the creators of these datasets. 
HTR-United offers a schema to homogenize descriptions of datasets, as well as recommendations on how to organize a data repository, and tools for quality control and continuous documentation. 
HTR-United is an ecosystem relying on a Github organization, transparent and open to all, using minimalistic developments to facilitate its maintenance. 
HTR-United was born from the necessity -for projects- to have access to various types of ground truth to rapidly train models on smaller corpora.

label: Hypotheses, Academic Blogs
description:
Hypotheses is an academic publishing platform that hosts several thousand blogs covering all areas of the humanities and social sciences. The texts are in open access. They are not aimed exclusively at specialists and may be of interest to a broad readership. Hypotheses publishes content in a wide range of languages. It is possible to browse the platform in the most commonly used languages on Hypotheses: French, German, Spanish and English.

The Hypotheses platform is open to the whole academic community (researchers, research teams, PhD students, information specialists, institutions, etc.) in all disciplines of the arts, humanities and social sciences.

Hypotheses aims to develop direct scientific communication. The perimeter of the platform is widely open. Many types of projects are accepted and each application is examined individually. 

However, some editorial projects will not be approved on Hypotheses. For instance, an application to open a blog that would be the publication medium for an academic journal would be refused (for more information about the platform’s editorial scope, see the view of its scientific committee) ; but a blog that aims to accompany an existing academic journal or journal project will be approved. 

To open a Hypotheses blog, you must provide a clear editorial and scientific project description, as well as an academic affiliation (research laboratory or institution, university, scholarly society, etc.).

relatedItems.label: OpenEdition
relatedItems.description:
OpenEdition is a comprehensive digital infrastructure for academic communication in the humanities and social sciences. It brings together four complementary platforms focused respectively on journals (OpenEdition Journals), book series (OpenEdition Books), research blogs (Hypotheses) and academic events (Calenda).

With its status as a national research infrastructure, OpenEdition is supported by OpenEdition Center, a CNRS Support and Research Unit (UAR 2504) associated with Aix-Marseille University, the EHESS and Avignon University.

relatedItems.label: DARIAH-DE and OPERAS-GER academic blogging with Hypotheses
relatedItems.description:
Hypotheses is a non-commercial blog portal for the humanities and social sciences. The portal provides a free service that facilitates scientific blogging and ensures greater visibility as well as archiving of content. The German branch of Hypotheses is provided by [OpenEdition](https://openedition.org/) in cooperation with the [Max Weber Foundation](https://www.maxweberstiftung.de/index.php?id=startseite). It contains contributions selected by the [community management](https://de.hypotheses.org/community-management) based at Max Weber Foundation. In a wider context, under the umbrella of OpenEdition [hypotheses.org](https://hypotheses.org/) publishes content in a wide range of languages. It is possible to browse the platform in the most commonly used languages on Hypotheses: French, German, Spanish and English.

The German branch of Hypotheses offers:
+ Technical assistance online via the [bloghaus](https://bloghaus.hypotheses.org/), by mail, as well as training offers.
+ Visibility of the posts on the homepage as well as via the social media channels of the portal
+ Archiving of content
+ Migration of already existing blogs

For further assistance please write to: blogs@maxweberstiftung.de

Check out some examples of community and research data infrastructure blogs: [Text+ Blog](https://textplus.hypotheses.org/) or [OPERAS-GER](https://operas-ger.hypotheses.org/)

This resource is supported by Text+. In case of questions you may get in touch with the Text+ helpdesk at textplus-support@gwdg.de.

label: I-Analyzer
description:
I-Analyzer is a service created by the Digital Humanities Lab of Utrecht University. I-Analyzer allows searching and exploring text corpora, visualizing trends, and downloading tables of text and metadata for further analysis. I-Analyzer is open-source software and freely available.Presently, it offers access to the following corpora:
1. Digital Library for Dutch Literature (DBNL),
2. Financial reports of Dutch companies,
3. Dutch Newspapers from the Royal Library: public dataset and full dataset (available upon request),
4. Eighteenth Century Collections Online (available for Utrecht University users),
5. Jewish Funerary Inscriptions,
6. Book reviews from Goodreads,
7. The Guardian-Observer newspaper archives (available for Utrecht University users),
8. 19th century UK Periodicals (available for Utrecht University users),
9. Dutch court rulings,
10. Times newspaper archives (available for Utrecht University users),
11. Dutch monarchs' speeches,
12. Dutch parliamentary debates.
I-analyzer does not have an option to upload your own data yet. But you can still use your data with I-analyzer by self-hosting the tool or contacting the team ([contact and self-host instructions](https://github.com/UUDigitalHumanitieslab/I-analyzer)).

label: IAT/ML
description:
IAT/ML is a methodology for discourse analysis.

By using IAT/ML, you can analyse a text jointly from four points of view: contextual (what social context produced the text), ontological (what the text refers to), argumentation (how the text justifies what it says), and agency (what beliefs, desires and intentions are represented in the text). You can connect the four types of analysis and carry out combined analytics.

IAT/ML is supported by LogosLink, a suite of software tools that you can use to carry out IAT/ML analyses. LogosLink also has some corpus management and analysis features, so you can benefit from an integrated and seamless workflow for your discourse analysis project. LogosLink is free to download and use.

label: ICE (Integrated Content Environment)
description:
Integrated Content Environment (ICE) was an open source project of the Learning Resources Development (LRD) unit at the University of Southern Queensland. The content management system allowed users to convert content authored in Microsoft Word or OpenOffice.org Writer into self-contained course websites using the IMS format.

The ICE authoring environment enabled:

Basic generic formatting of a document using styles for headings and other structural elements

Pedagogical elements such as learning outcomes, lists of readings and activities

Piece-by-piece course construction with immediate feedback about the web and print views

Modular collaborative and distributed authoring

Revision control

Content reuse

Basic print and web/CD publishing under author control

Common/generic content
ICE is no longer running.

label: ICON Ontology
description:
The ICON ontology defines classes and properties to express artistic interpretations of figurative artworks' subject matter (i.e., iconographies) and meanings (i.e., symbols, iconological aspects). It was developed by conceptualizing authoritative knowledge and notions from art historians' theoretical approaches. The ontology creation is motivated by the need to provide a comprehensive description of the content of the artwork, thereby attributing subjectivity, responsibility, and sources to each statement while representing both iconographical and iconological aspects. This allows for the representation and integration of complex domain-specific knowledge into the context of the semantic web. 

ICON is a domain-specific ontology intended to be used by 1) museums aiming at describing thoroughly the content of the artworks, 2) art historians conducting research with the aim of quantitative approaches, and 3) developers using computer vision to associate a content description to portions of artworks.

relatedItems.label: Enrichir le candidat avec des alignements et des images
relatedItems.description:
Ajouter un alignement : il s’agit de créer une relation d’équivalence plus ou moins exacte entre le mot-clé Pactols et un item correspondant dans un autre référentiel du web. Pactols a fait le choix de préférer les relations exactes (skos:exactMatch). Les alignements ne sont possibles qu’avec des référentiels fournissant un identifiant pérenne à ses items (DOI, ARK,...) ou une adresse web stable (URI).

Les principaux référentiels des alignements Pactols sont : Wikidata, les thésaurus du ministère français de la Culture (http://data.culture.fr/thesaurus/), IdRef (oeuvres, personnes), le Art and Architecture Thesaurus de la Fondation Getty, Bibracte_thesaurus, Bnf, Pleiades (lieux anciens), Geonames (lieux), Insee (lieux de France). 

Deux modes d’alignement sont possibles : 
1. alignement : faites une recherche préalable dans le réservoir puis donnez l’URI distante de l’item et le nom du référentiel dans le formulaire.
Ex. URI distante : https://www.wikidata.org/wiki/Q6934696
      Nom de la source : Wikidata
2. alignement automatique : Opentheso opère une recherche sur le libellé dans les référentiels pré-enregistrés : Bibracte_thesaurus, Bnf, GeoNames, Wikidata. Selon le réservoir, la réponse peut être faussement négative sur le libellé en français, par exemple avec Wikidata dont les items peuvent ne pas avoir d’équivalent dans la langue de la recherche. Écrivez de préférence le terme de la requête dans la langue du référentiel visé. Sélectionnez la meilleure réponse affichée. La possibilité de rapatrier des métadonnées supplémentaires (traductions, images, définition) peut être un avantage mais nécessitera une relecture voire une correction après alignement. 

Image : Certains concepts, difficiles à définir, peuvent être illustrés avec profit d’une ou de plusieurs images. Celles-ci doivent être représentatives du concept et se positionner autant que possible dans le champ de l’archéologie sinon de l’histoire ancienne. Elles doivent impérativement être libres de droit (sélectionnez les réservoirs ad hoc, notamment Wikimedia Commons, et citables (avec une URI comme adresse web stable, un PID identifiant pérenne de type ARK, DOI, etc.).

Pour ajouter une image depuis Wikimedia Commons : sélectionnez l'image choisie, cliquez sur l'onglet "use this file" et recopiez le champ "File URL:". Remplissez les 4 champs de l'onglet Image de Pactols : l'URI, la légende de l'image (libellé), son auteur et la source. 
Ex. pour amphore attique : URI : https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/0/01/Amphore_attique_%C3%A0_figures_noires._Peintre_de_Rycroft_-_btv1b101044967_%282_of_2%29.jpg ; libellé : Amphore attique à figures noires. Peintre de Rycroft ; auteur : Bibliothèque nationale de France ; source : Wikimédia.

relatedItems.label: Consult and Digitize Sources
relatedItems.description:
Access to primary sources is a prerequisite for any critical edition and must be addressed before encoding begins. Where sources have not yet been digitized, the editor should follow the IIIF (International Image Interoperability Framework) protocol, which enables standardized sharing, annotation, and long-term preservation of high-resolution images. IIIF allows any rectangular fragment of a manuscript to be directly addressed via a URL, and supports comparative visualization across multiple sources and collections. 

Where digitizations already exist in institutional repositories (libraries, archives), the editor should link to them rather than duplicate them, while verifying the legal conditions of their reuse. Two access modalities are available: a hyperlink to an externally hosted digitized resource, or an IIIF viewer integrated directly into the digital edition interface. 

The availability of digitized sources is particularly crucial for early music, where the faithful transcription of ligatures, mensuration signs, tablature systems, and other notational features requires direct visual reference to the manuscript.

label: ILSP Neural NLP Toolkit
description:
The ILSP Neural NLP toolkit for Greek currently integrates modules for segmentation, POS tagging, lemmatization, dependency parsing, chunking, named entity recognition and text classification. The toolkit is based on language resources including web crawled corpora, word embeddings, large lexica, and corpora manually annotated at different levels of linguistic analysis.

You can use this service to process any TXT document in UTF-8 encoding and obtain the output in either JSON format or in CSV file format.

According to the processing steps followed by the service, the output includes annotations on the level of sentence (Sentence ID, Sentence), token (Token ID, Token, Token Start, Token End), lemma, part of speech (Upos and Features according to Universal PoS & Features Tagset, Xpos according to XPoS ILSP Tagset), dependency relation (Relation and Head ID) according to Universal Dependency Relations Tagset, named entity (Named Entity, Named Entity Type according to ILSP Neural NER Tagset, Named Entity Score), chunks (Chunk and Chunk Type according to ILSP Neural Toolkit Chunk Tagset) and the thematic category in which the whole text is classified into (Text Classification according to ILSP Neural Text Classification Tagset). See the Output Annotation Schema field below for more information on the respective tagsets.

For technical reasons, the file submitted for processing may be split into smaller files, and so will the output.

This service is seamlessly integrated into the CLARIN:EL infrastructure's workflows, providing users with convenient and easy access as a web service. You can use this service by clicking the "Use" button on this page or by accessing it through the CLARIN:EL processing services page.

concept.label: IIIF
concept.definition: The International Image Interoperability Framework (IIIF) is a set of shared application programming interface (API) specifications for interoperable functionality in digital image repositories. The IIIF is comprised of and driven by a community of libraries, museums, archives, software companies, and other organizations working together to create, test, refine, implement and promote the IIIF specifications. Using JSON-LD, linked data, and standard W3C web protocols such as Web Annotation, IIIF makes it easy to parse and share digital image data, migrate across technology systems, and provide enhanced image access for scholars and researchers. In short, IIIF enables better, faster and cheaper image delivery. It lets you leverage interoperability and the fabric of the Web to access new possibilities and new users for your image-based resources, while reducing long term maintenance and technological lock in. label: INCEpTION
description:
**INCEpTION** is an open-source, web-based platform for annotating text. It supports annotations of any span of text, from single words to whole documents, relations between annotations, coreference chains and document-level labels, on documents in formats such as plain text, PDF, HTML and TEI. INCEpTION is the successor of WebAnno and can import WebAnno projects.

* **Collaborative Annotation:** Multiple annotators can work on the same documents, with different workflow management schemes, built-in inter-annotator agreement measures, and curation of the individual annotations into a gold standard.
* **Customizable Annotation Layers:** Users define their own layers, features and tagsets in the browser, tailored to the needs of their project.
* **Knowledge Base Integration:** Annotations can be linked to knowledge bases and authority files such as Wikidata, the GND and SNOMED CT, to other resources in RDF, OWL, OBO or SKOS, and to remote SPARQL endpoints.
* **Machine Learning Integration:** Built-in recommenders learn from the annotations as users work and suggest new ones, active learning focuses attention on uncertain cases, and projects can connect their own models as external recommenders.
* **Interoperability:** It imports and exports a range of formats, including TEI, CoNLL-U and other CoNLL variants, WebAnno TSV, WebLicht TCF and UIMA XMI, and offers a REST API for integration into processing pipelines.
* **Flexible Deployment:** It runs on a single computer or on an institutional server with single sign-on. Hosted instances are offered through CLARIN:EL and CLARIN-IT.

These features make INCEpTION a comprehensive solution for building and managing annotated corpora.

label: Indico Event Management
description:
The open source software Indico developed by Cern is a web application. Lectures, meetings and conferences can be created using Indico.
Three different event types (lecture, meeting and conference) can be created in Indico.

**Lecture**: A lecture can contain a presentation and be given with several speakers or one speaker.

**Meeting**: Usually a meeting consists of several presentations. The duration of a meeting can vary: a meeting can last one day or several days, with a meeting often taking place on one day. It is possible that contributions are organized in meetings. Minutes can also be added to a meeting.

**Conference**: A conference usually lasts a few days and several meetings can be held at the same time. Conferences also have the advantage that they enable flexible workflows for the processing of abstracts and documents.

Participants can be managed for all three types of events. Registrations, the use of collaborative tools and surveys are also possible. Reminder emails can also be used for events.

To access the service you need to login via the Academic Cloud (https://academiccloud.de/home): either with a registered e-mail adress (if your academic home institution is based in Niedersachsen, Germany) or via the federated login with your DARIAH account or your instutional account. Please note, that regardless of which account you choose here, you should always make the same selection for all subsequent logins, as your profile and thus, also your data and your entries will be linked to this identity.

The Indico service is is widespread use in the National Research Data Infrastructure (NFDI), for instance in Text+.

This resource is supported by Text+. In case of questions you may get in touch with the Text+ helpdesk at textplus-support@gwdg.de.

concept.label: JPEG
concept.definition: JPEG ( JAY-peg) is a commonly used method of lossy compression for digital images, particularly for those images produced by digital photography. The degree of compression can be adjusted, allowing a selectable tradeoff between storage size and image quality. JPEG typically achieves 10:1 compression with little perceptible loss in image quality. JPEG compression is used in a number of image file formats. JPEG/Exif is the most common image format used by digital cameras and other photographic image capture devices; along with JPEG/JFIF, it is the most common format for storing and transmitting photographic images on the World Wide Web. These format variations are often not distinguished, and are simply called JPEG. The term "JPEG" is an initialism/acronym for the Joint Photographic Experts Group, which created the standard. The MIME media type for JPEG is image/jpeg, except in older Internet Explorer versions, which provides a MIME type of image/pjpeg when uploading JPEG images. JPEG files usually have a filename extension of .jpg or .jpeg. JPEG/JFIF supports a maximum image size of 65,53565,535 pixels, hence up to 4 gigapixels for an aspect ratio of 1:1.

label: INEL Dolgan Corpus - Web Search
description:
The corpus contains audio recordings with time-aligned transcriptions of Dolgan, as well as additional descriptions such as annotations and glosses. In the updated version 2.0, the corpus, which was created as part of the INEL subproject Dolgan (September 2016–August 2019, January 2022-June 2022), is available under open access conditions. The corpus enables typologically based grammatical research into the Dolgan language. At the same time, it makes a further contribution to the documentation of the hitherto little-described indigenous languages of Northern Eurasia. The INEL Dolgan corpus is composed of materials from the following sources:

* Published folkloric texts from an anthology (“Fol'klor Dolgan,” P.E. Efremov 2000)
* Transcripts of recordings from the House of Cultures of the Peoples of the Taimyr Peninsula (TDNT) in Dudinka
* Transcripts from the collection of Dr. Eugénie Stapert, whose recordings were made during several field trips between 2007 and 2010
* Transcripts of recordings made during a field trip in 2017.

The materials listed under 1. and parts of 3. have already been transcribed and translated, while the rest of the recordings were transcribed and translated as part of the INEL project. All texts in the corpus contain morphological glosses, translations into English, Russian, and German, as well as annotations for borrowings from Russian. Some texts also have annotations for syntactic functions, semantic roles, and information structure/information status.

The database is an open access resource, freely accessible online, that was developed with the aim to support other specialists within the heritage science field that work with XRF, infrared (ATR-FTIR) or Raman spectroscopic techniques.The INFRA-ART Spectral Library follows the European Commission’s recommendation on access to scientific information as well as the FAIR Guiding Principles on research data that result from publicly funded research. This resource supports cross-disciplinary research and reliable re-use of research data for research, innovation, and educational purposes. The INFRA-ART database is targeted to the cultural heritage research community as well as to other specialists in the field of art history, conservation, and materials science.# Key features**» Wide selection of materials**: INFRA-ART covers a wide selection of materials, including materials not represented in other databases, as far as we know, such as an impressive number of earth pigments from different geological sources, special effect pigments (such as metal effect pigments, pearlescent pigments or daylight fluorescent pigments), or traditional Japanese painting materials such as iwa-enogu.**» Ongoing compilation of spectra**: New reference samples will be integrated within the database on an ongoing basis as new materials are being analyzed.**» Complementary spectral data**: The INFRA-ART database includes data provided by XRF, FTIR and Raman techniques offering thus information at both elemental and molecular level.**» Accessible spectroscopic techniques**: The employed techniques (handheld XRF, ATR-FTIR, and fiber-optic Raman) are affordable scientific tools, widely used for the technical examination of works of art, both in-laboratory and on-site applications.**» Rich metadata**: Detailed information for each reference material is included (sample source, origin, description, alternative names, chemical information, and history of use) as well as on the employed techniques and data acquisition conditions.**» Search engine**: For greater functionality and access, an advanced search engine was incorporated within the INFRA-ART database which allows users to search by keywords, material class or data type.**» Spectra viewer**: An interactive spectra-viewer tool was integrated within the webpage in order to allow the user to interact with the loaded spectral data - pick points, label peaks, zoom in and out, pan, and also save the spectrum as image, on local disk.

concept.label: JPEG
concept.definition: JPEG ( JAY-peg) is a commonly used method of lossy compression for digital images, particularly for those images produced by digital photography. The degree of compression can be adjusted, allowing a selectable tradeoff between storage size and image quality. JPEG typically achieves 10:1 compression with little perceptible loss in image quality. JPEG compression is used in a number of image file formats. JPEG/Exif is the most common image format used by digital cameras and other photographic image capture devices; along with JPEG/JFIF, it is the most common format for storing and transmitting photographic images on the World Wide Web. These format variations are often not distinguished, and are simply called JPEG. The term "JPEG" is an initialism/acronym for the Joint Photographic Experts Group, which created the standard. The MIME media type for JPEG is image/jpeg, except in older Internet Explorer versions, which provides a MIME type of image/pjpeg when uploading JPEG images. JPEG files usually have a filename extension of .jpg or .jpeg. JPEG/JFIF supports a maximum image size of 65,53565,535 pixels, hence up to 4 gigapixels for an aspect ratio of 1:1.

label: INL BlackLab
description:
**From the official BlackLab site:** "BlackLab is a corpus retrieval engine built on top of Apache Lucene. It allows fast, complex searches with accurate hit highlighting on large, tagged and annotated, bodies of text. It was developed at the Institute of Dutch Lexicology (INL) to provide a fast and feature-rich search interface on our historical and contemporary text corpora.

BlackLab is licensed under the Apache License 2.0."

BlackLab is not an end-user application, but an extension to Apache Lucene. It requires programming experience to use. Several sites have so far been built using BlackLab. The BlackLab FAQ at https://github.com/INL/BlackLab/wiki/Frequently-Asked-Questions lists several of these.

BlackLab is very useful as search engine for morphologically adorned corpora. The principal search language syntax is similar to that of traditional corpus search engine tools such as the Corpus Workbench or the Sketch Engine.

relatedItems.label: Enrichir le candidat avec des alignements et des images
relatedItems.description:
Ajouter un alignement : il s’agit de créer une relation d’équivalence plus ou moins exacte entre le mot-clé Pactols et un item correspondant dans un autre référentiel du web. Pactols a fait le choix de préférer les relations exactes (skos:exactMatch). Les alignements ne sont possibles qu’avec des référentiels fournissant un identifiant pérenne à ses items (DOI, ARK,...) ou une adresse web stable (URI).

Les principaux référentiels des alignements Pactols sont : Wikidata, les thésaurus du ministère français de la Culture (http://data.culture.fr/thesaurus/), IdRef (oeuvres, personnes), le Art and Architecture Thesaurus de la Fondation Getty, Bibracte_thesaurus, Bnf, Pleiades (lieux anciens), Geonames (lieux), Insee (lieux de France). 

Deux modes d’alignement sont possibles : 
1. alignement : faites une recherche préalable dans le réservoir puis donnez l’URI distante de l’item et le nom du référentiel dans le formulaire.
Ex. URI distante : https://www.wikidata.org/wiki/Q6934696
      Nom de la source : Wikidata
2. alignement automatique : Opentheso opère une recherche sur le libellé dans les référentiels pré-enregistrés : Bibracte_thesaurus, Bnf, GeoNames, Wikidata. Selon le réservoir, la réponse peut être faussement négative sur le libellé en français, par exemple avec Wikidata dont les items peuvent ne pas avoir d’équivalent dans la langue de la recherche. Écrivez de préférence le terme de la requête dans la langue du référentiel visé. Sélectionnez la meilleure réponse affichée. La possibilité de rapatrier des métadonnées supplémentaires (traductions, images, définition) peut être un avantage mais nécessitera une relecture voire une correction après alignement. 

Image : Certains concepts, difficiles à définir, peuvent être illustrés avec profit d’une ou de plusieurs images. Celles-ci doivent être représentatives du concept et se positionner autant que possible dans le champ de l’archéologie sinon de l’histoire ancienne. Elles doivent impérativement être libres de droit (sélectionnez les réservoirs ad hoc, notamment Wikimedia Commons, et citables (avec une URI comme adresse web stable, un PID identifiant pérenne de type ARK, DOI, etc.).

Pour ajouter une image depuis Wikimedia Commons : sélectionnez l'image choisie, cliquez sur l'onglet "use this file" et recopiez le champ "File URL:". Remplissez les 4 champs de l'onglet Image de Pactols : l'URI, la légende de l'image (libellé), son auteur et la source. 
Ex. pour amphore attique : URI : https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/0/01/Amphore_attique_%C3%A0_figures_noires._Peintre_de_Rycroft_-_btv1b101044967_%282_of_2%29.jpg ; libellé : Amphore attique à figures noires. label: Integrated Authority File (GND)
description:
The Integrated Authority File (GND) is a service facilitating the collaborative use and administration of authority data. These authority data represent and describe entities, i.e. persons, corporate bodies, conferences and events, geographic entities, topics and works relating to cultural and academic collections. Authority data make cataloguing easier, offer definitive search entries and forge links between different information resources.

It is operated cooperatively by the German National Library, all German-speaking library networks and the associated libraries, the German Union Catalogue of Serials (ZDB) and numerous other institutions. Contributions to the GND are made either via the networks or in direct agreement with the German National Library.

The Common Authority File (GND) is a service for the cooperative use and management of authority data. This authority data represents and describes entities, i.e. persons, corporate bodies, conferences, geographies, subject headings and works that are related to cultural and scientific collections. Standardised data facilitates indexing, provides clear search access points and links different information resources.
