relatedItems.label: Hypotheses, Academic Blogs
relatedItems.description:
Hypotheses is an academic publishing platform that hosts several thousand blogs covering all areas of the humanities and social sciences. The texts are in open access. They are not aimed exclusively at specialists and may be of interest to a broad readership. Hypotheses publishes content in a wide range of languages. It is possible to browse the platform in the most commonly used languages on Hypotheses: French, German, Spanish and English.

The Hypotheses platform is open to the whole academic community (researchers, research teams, PhD students, information specialists, institutions, etc.) in all disciplines of the arts, humanities and social sciences.

Hypotheses aims to develop direct scientific communication. The perimeter of the platform is widely open. Many types of projects are accepted and each application is examined individually. 

However, some editorial projects will not be approved on Hypotheses. For instance, an application to open a blog that would be the publication medium for an academic journal would be refused (for more information about the platform’s editorial scope, see the view of its scientific committee) ; but a blog that aims to accompany an existing academic journal or journal project will be approved. 

To open a Hypotheses blog, you must provide a clear editorial and scientific project description, as well as an academic affiliation (research laboratory or institution, university, scholarly society, etc.).

relatedItems.label: Open Conference Systems
relatedItems.description:
Open Conference Systems (OCS) is a free Web publishing tool that can create a complete Web presence for scholarly conferences. It is a highly flexible management and publishing system that can be downloaded for free and installed on a local Web server. It has been designed to reduce the time and energy devoted to the clerical and managerial tasks associated with managing a conference, while improving the record-keeping and efficiency of editorial processes. It seeks to improve the scholarly and public quality of conference publishing through a number of innovation, from making policies more transparent to improving indexing.

Features:

- create a conference Web site

- Manage conferences that occur more than once (e.g., yearly)

- compose and send a call for papers

- electronically accept paper and abstract submissions

- allow paper submitters to edit their work

- Conduct peer reviews

- post conference proceedings and papers in a searchable format

- Schedule a Conference

- post the original data sets

- register participants, including accepting payments

- integrate post-conference online discussions

- utilize an e-mail template system

- support multiple languages with localization files

- Take advantage of more customizable, scalable and secure code

System Requirements:

A server environment meeting the following requirements is recommended:

- PHP \>= 4.2.x (including PHP 5.x); Microsoft IIS requires PHP 5.x

- MySQL \>= 3.23.23 (including MySQL 4.x) or PostgreSQL \>= 7.1 (including

- PostgreSQL 8.x)

label: OpenITI Regex Search Explorer (ReSearchITI) (v1.0)
description:
ReSearchITI is a Python-based research tool designed for the systematic exploration of Arabic textual corpora, particularly focused on the OpenITI corpus. The software enables users to perform context-aware searches based on a primary search pattern combined with optional contextual filters, extract relevant text fragments with configurable context windows, and organize the results into a structured Excel file enriched with metadata.
Key features include: 1) Regex-based primary and contextual search patterns. 2) Configurable context extraction by number of lines. 3) Optional cleaning of OpenITI mARkdown structural and semantic tags. 4) Automatic grouping and deduplication of results by author and work. 5) Optional automatic translation of extracted fragments into a target language. 6) Optional word alignment-based or manual highlighting in both source text and translation. 7) Rich-text Excel output with color-coded highlights and metadata columns.
The software is intended as an exploratory and research-oriented tool for philological, historical, linguistic, and textual analysis. It is under active development and may evolve with additional features and refinements.

relatedItems.label: Arabic Similarity Search Tool for the OpenITI Corpus (SimilArITI) (v1.0)
relatedItems.description:
SimilArITI is a Python-based tool designed to identify textually similar passages across a corpus of Arabic works, mainly the OpenITI Corpus. It operates in two distinct phases: 1) an indexing phase, in which texts are preprocessed, segmented into fragments, and represented using TF-IDF vectorization at the fragment level; and 2) a search phase, in which a user-defined reference text is compared against the indexed fragments using cosine similarity.
The software is particularly intended for digital humanities research on Arabic textual traditions, enabling the detection of parallels, thematic echoes, and reused narrative material across works. A set of preprocessed works is provided to allow immediate use, while the indexing script enables users to extend the corpus with additional texts. The current version represents a functional first release, with future refinements planned for fragment segmentation strategies and similarity modeling.

relatedItems.label: Introduction
relatedItems.description:
[Zotero](https://zotero.org) is a free and open source reference and bibliography management software. It [ingests structured publication metadata](https://www.zotero.org/support/adding_items_to_zotero) from files in various formats, and through a set of translators also by scraping from websites.

[Wikibase](https://wikiba.se) is a free and open source software solution for storing, editing, and querying Linked Data. It is the software underlying Wikidata.

[Wikidata](https://www.wikidata.org) is today the largest free and open Knowledge Graph. It contains millions of entities describing, for example, scholarly publications and their authors.

ZotWb, the tool presented in this workflow, helps to migrate records from a Zotero group library to a custom Wikibase instance, and performing entity reconciliation against Wikidata and/or the own Wikibase, using [OpenRefine](https://openrefine.org).

relatedItems.label: Reconciling person name literal strings against Wikibase and Wikidata entities
relatedItems.description:
# Deduplicating and Reconciling person names in OpenRefine

This function will produce a CSV sheet to be imported into OpenRefine, containing all unreconciled (i.e., literal only) creator statements (including all creator role properties). The CSV file will be saved in your [`data/unreconciled_creators`](data/unreconciled_creators) folder.

## Deduplication (optional)

Deduplication using the [Clustering function](https://openrefine.org/docs/manual/cellediting#cluster-and-edit)

1. Starting point is the column containing the full name of persons.

2. To perform **clustering** without losing original column content, select the column menu:

	* `Edit column > Add column based on this column > value`.
    
	* Choose a column name, e.g. `fullName_clusters`.
    
3.  Clustering algorithms can be accessed with `Edit cells > Cluster and edit`.
    
4. Perform all clustering algorithms in the recommended order and manually validate the found name clusters. Different algorithms may detect different degrees and types of string similarity.
	* key collision - fingerprint
	* key collision - ngram fingerprint
	* key collision - metaphone3
	* key collision - cologne-phonetic
	* key collision - Daitch-Mokotoff
	* key collision - Beider-Morse
	* nearest neighbor - Levenshtein
	* nearest neighbor - ppm
    
	Validation of name clusters includes selecting one of the names as the normalized name variant. Within the column `fullName_clusters`, this preferred name variant will replace the various name forms previously found in the data.
    
5. To perform **merging of duplicates** for normalized person names in `fullName_clusters`, once again select the column menu: `edit column > Add column based on this column > value`. REQUIRED COLUMN NAME: `fullName_preferred`.
    
6. Before duplicates can be eliminated, sort alphabetically and re-order permanently:

	`Sort > a-z`
	`Sort > re-order rows permanently`
	`Edit cells > Blank down`

	These steps result in a list of preferred person names that appear only once in the column. Preferred full names are thus connected to preferred given names and last names.
    
## Reconciliation

**Reconciliation** will be based on the column `fullName_clusters`. If no clustering was performed, Reconciliation will be based on the raw person data in the column `fullName`.
    
1. Person names may already be included in your Wikibase. If not, they might be found in Wikidata. In both cases, the [Reconciliation function](https://openrefine.org/docs/manual/reconciling) searches for matches in the specified dataset.

	For each reconciliation process, create a separate column based on `fullName_clusters` (or `fullName`) column using `edit column > Add column based on this column > value`.

	REQUIRED COLUMN NAMES:
	fullName_recon_Wikidata
	fullName_recon_Wikibase
    
2. For each recon column, invoke the reconciliation process using `Reconcile > Start reconciling`. From the list of reconciliation services, pick the appropriate one, leading to your Wikibase or to Wikidata. If not already selected, select an entity type such as `human` (Q5) to restrict possible reconciliation targets. Be careful with the function `automatically match candidates with high confidence`; that is risky, since it is not at all unlikely that there exist several persons with the same or similar name on Wikidata, and only one (or none) of these is the one you want to link to.
    
3. Validate reconciliation candidates. Approved reconciled person names are now linked to their corresponding person item in Wikibase/Wikidata. 
4. Now create a new column containing the person item identifier from Wikibase/Wikidata using `Reconcile > Add entity identifiers column`
    
    Specify the new column's name as REQUIRED: 
     * `Wikidata_Qid`
     * `Wikibase_Qid`
5. Export as comma seperated value (csv) to your `data/reconciled_creators` folder using `Export > comma separated values`

relatedItems.label: Producing Structured Visual Data from Illustrated Heritage Corpora
relatedItems.description:
Illustrated heritage corpora bring together digitised pages, plates, photographs, prints, drawings, captions, inscriptions, handwritten notes, and catalogue records at different levels of granularity. This workflow provides a method for turning these heterogeneous sources into visual units that can be located, described, compared, and reused while preserving their connection to the original documents and collections.

Starting from a research question, the workflow guides the selection of a representative corpus, the preparation of images and metadata, and the definition of the visual and textual units to be identified. A reference sample establishes the expected structure and quality of the results. Automatic or semi-automatic processing can then be used to extract images and associated text, followed by expert review, correction, and evaluation. The validated results are converted into structured data that can support cataloguing, quantitative analysis, visual exploration, or the study of relationships between images, texts, people, places, and objects.

The workflow preserves source identifiers, processing history, uncertainty, and validation status throughout the process. Its outputs may include extracted image regions, annotations, transcriptions, structured metadata, authority links, similarity results, and documented datasets. These elements provide a reproducible basis for further research and enable the resulting data, methods, and evaluation criteria to be shared and adapted across heritage collections.

This process is particularly relevant to researchers working with visual or illustrated corpora; research engineers and data stewards; libraries, archives, museums and heritage institutions; digital humanities projects preparing training, evaluation or exploration datasets; and teaching and training teams introducing computer vision methods for cultural heritage.

label: Open Research Knowledge Graph
description:
Research is a fundamental pillar of societal progress. Yet, scientific communities face great difficulties in sharing their findings. With approximately 2.5 million newly published scientific articles per year, it is impossible to keep track of all relevant knowledge. Even in small fields, researchers often find themselves drowning in a publication flood, contributing to major scientific crises such as the reproducibility crisis, the deficiency of peer-review and ultimately the loss of knowledge.

The underlying problem is that we never updated our methods of scholarly communication to exploit the possibilities of digitalization. This is where the Open Research Knowledge Graph comes into play!

The ORKG makes scientific knowledge human- and machine-actionable and thus enables completely new ways of machine assistance. This will help researchers find relevant contributions to their field and create state-of-the-art comparisons and reviews. With the ORKG, scientists can explore knowledge in entirely new ways and share results even across different disciplines.

label: Open Science Framework
description:
The Open Science Framework (OSF) is a free, open source tool designed to help researchers manage the entire research workflow: planning, execution, reporting, archiving and discovery. It is part collaboration software and part version control system. The OSF can be used to manage individual projects or large collaborative ones. Privacy and sharing settings allow for fine-grained control over access to files and materials stored on the platform - share privately with collaborators or publicly with the community at large. Each project, contributor, and file on the OSF is given a persistent unique identifier, making all research products citable. The platform also mints DOIs and ARKs through DataCite. A collaborative wiki allows contributors to work on writing materials simultaneously.

API connections with other services (Github, Dropbox, Box, Dataverse, Google Drive, figshare, Zotero, Mendeley, Amazon S3) allow researchers to connect other services they already use in order to see all their materials in one place. The OSF also offers a registry for preregistering research projects and/or analysis plans.

label: Opentheso
description:
Opentheso is a web-based thesaurus management tool dedicated to the management of vocabularies.

It is developed at the CNRS (National Center for Scientific Research - France), financed by GDS FRANTIQ (https://www.frantiq.fr/), la MOM (https://www.mom.fr/) and IR* Huma-Num (https://www.huma-num.fr/) with Consortium (MASA) Mémoire des archéologues et des sites archéologiques (https://masa.hypotheses.org/). 


OpenTheso is used by a network of 39 research libraries (FRANTIQ. Archaeology, 32 000 concepts. Contact : Blandine Nouvel), research units (Zoomatia, archaelogical research project), les Hospices civils de Lyon (medicine, 60000 concepts), l’Institut des Sciences de l’Homme (part of Rameau vocabulary)…

Ses fonctionnalités actuelles :
- Gestion avancée des termes et des branches
- Drag and Drop
- Gestion collaborative avec 4 niveaux d'authentification (Superadmin, Admin, User et Traducteur)
- Interopérable : génération automatique d'identifiants Handle et ARK (ce service est assuré par le PSIR de la MOM)
- WebServices REST
- import : SKOS, Turtle, JsonLD
- export : SKOS, Turtle, JsonLD, CSV et PDF



OpenTheso is released under the terms of the CeCILL_C license, fully compatible with the GNU GPL.

relatedItems.label: Textual typology : a thesaurus of textual genres
relatedItems.description:
With the emergence and subsequent rise of digital editions, a polyphonic situation arises, posing a problem: the identification of resources using automated tools can be hindered due to the lack of a common framework for the typological description of textual resources. This observation prompted some members of the Consortium-HN CAHIER (Huma-Num) to create a "Textual typology" working group, aimed at developing a thesaurus for describing various types of literary texts.
This consortium, which encompassed over sixty projects of digital edition and digitization of authorial corpora from various periods and intellectual backgrounds, exhibited significant heterogeneity in its productions, accompanied by highly enriched metadata. However, the keywords used to describe these objects (whether through Dublin Core in Omeka or in the headers - teiHeaders - of XML/TEI files) lack uniformity.

The "Textual Typology" working group undertook the development of a reference thesaurus for genres and types of texts, drawing from the terms used in the projects and conducting a systematic review of various lists of literary concepts. The construction of the "Textual Typology" thesaurus thus proceeded in several stages, aiming to provide a conceptually, lexically, and semantically rich tool to meet the needs of our knowledge domains.

relatedItems.label: ANAMNESIS - Metadata and paradata management platform for Cultural and Heritage Sciences
relatedItems.description: ANAMNESIS is an open-source web platform designed to document, structure, and preserve digitization workflows in Cultural Heritage (CH) and Heritage Science (HS). Built on the W7 semantic framework (What, Why, Who, Where, When, How, Which), it enables fine-grained metadata and paradata documentation for HS imaging and measurments activities—from data acquisition to processing and analysis—while ensuring traceability, reproducibility, and FAIR compliance.

relatedItems.label: The Pactols Thesaurus
relatedItems.description:
Controlled, standardized and multilingual vocabulary for archaeology, from prehistory to the contemporary period and for the sciences of antiquity in all their aspects.

Pactols is a reservoir of controlled and multilingual keywords.

If it serves historically the indexing of the CCI (Frantiq's indexed collective catalog), its richness and its scalability seduced other communities. For several years, it has been used as a thematic repository for diversified resources (academic journals, scientific databases, heritage enhancement programs).

It was created by Frantiq (Federation and Resources on Antiquity constituted as a CNRS Service Group no. 3378), which brings together around fifty units CNRS, services of the Ministry of Culture, archaeological museums, local authorities and other public establishments.

It was developed with the support of MASA consortium, Memory of archaeologists and archaeological sites.

relatedItems.label: Proposer un nouveau mot-clé (candidat) au thésaurus Pactols
relatedItems.description:
Pactols rassemble des mots-clés spécialisés (concepts) pour décrire sans ambiguïté le contenu de ressources documentaires et de jeux de données en archéologie, depuis la Préhistoire jusqu’à l’époque contemporaine, et tous les aspects des sciences de l’Antiquité. Le thésaurus est normalisé et multilingue : sa langue par défaut est le français et il est traduit en 5 langues. Il est libre d’accès et son évolution se fait dans un cadre contrôlé. Toute proposition de nouveaux termes suit donc une procédure bien définie. 

C’est ce processus de proposition/création de nouveau terme qui est présenté ici.

relatedItems.label: Se connecter à Pactols et au module « Candidats »
relatedItems.description:
Le thésaurus Pactols fonctionne avec le logiciel de gestion de thésaurus Opentheso. La possibilité de proposer un nouveau concept/mot-clé nécessite d’avoir un compte avec un niveau d’autorisation au moins égal à « contributeur ». 

Pour obtenir un compte Pactols, adressez une demande à pactols@services.cnrs.fr en précisant votre identité, votre appartenance institutionnelle et la raison de la demande. Vous recevrez votre login par mail et à la première connexion, vous validerez le compte en créant votre mot de passe.

Une fois connecté, sélectionnez le thésaurus Pactols (« Lieux » ou « Sujets » ) pour accéder au module Candidats (signe + dans le menu de gauche).

relatedItems.label: Bibracte_Thesaurus
relatedItems.description:
Bibracte_Thesaurus is a specialised thesaurus developed for the archaeological research and documentation of Bibracte. It provides a structured vocabulary reflecting the terminology used by the scientific partners involved in research at the site, covering areas such as archaeological excavation and prospection, artefacts, chronology, research methods, conservation-restoration and dissemination. Managed through Opentheso, it supports the standardised description, organisation and interoperability of archaeological data.

FR:

Bibracte_Thesaurus est un thésaurus spécialisé développé pour la recherche et la documentation archéologiques de Bibracte. Il propose un vocabulaire structuré reflétant la terminologie utilisée par les partenaires scientifiques impliqués dans les recherches sur le site, couvrant notamment la prospection et la fouille archéologiques, les artefacts, la chronologie, les méthodes de recherche, la conservation-restauration et la valorisation. Géré avec Opentheso, il favorise la description et l'organisation normalisées des données archéologiques ainsi que leur interopérabilité.

relatedItems.label: [3] Opening to external users
relatedItems.description:
More than an active step per se, **opening** the schema corresponds rather to the question of display and communication related to the schema’s progress as it moves to version 1.0.  The schema documentation covers both the schema *data* (sections, structure, formatting, translations) and *metadata*, as well as example sheets illustrating how the schema is used. Once these key points have been validated, the schema can be shared and used on a large scale, ensuring consistency in completion across users. A small **internal** communication can also be considered within the platform. This step marks the end of the internal schema creation process on ANAMNESIS.

The following sub-steps should be viewed as **optional**, value-adding steps that allow you to capitalise on the initial investment made in creating the schema. We propose three approaches and pathways within this framework: **generalisation, external publication, and external documentation**. All three pathways are based on the idea that the metadata schema has value in itself as an object of knowledge and that, in this sense, it can be manipulated as such.    
- In a process of increasing **generality**, it is possible to carry out retrospective **curation** of schemas to align the qualities of one schema with another that has emerged after or in parallel with the established path. This **fine-tuning** stage offers a form of enrichment based on the pooling of practices and the potential contributions of other tools, however distant. It is also possible to move towards generic schemas starting from a schema specific to a particular technique. By adopting an abstract approach, we believe it is possible to explore a higher-level approach, yet one based on **bottom-up** developments. 

- The outsourcing of **documentation** is a significant step, even if it is not mandatory. In fact, we have concluded that **outsourcing** helps to overcome certain limitations of Anamnesis while clearly illustrating the evolution of a schema for those outside the Anamnesis practice, thereby confirming the ability to project a schema beyond its purely utilitarian existence within the platform. The steps identified here are divided into three parts: the use of an **external thesaurus manager** to standardise terms with persistent identifiers, without needing to be an administrator on Anamnesis. As it is not yet possible to automate the transfer process, curation is carried out manually, using the various methods permitted by Opentheso.    
The second part of the external documentation involves creating a **graphical representation** based on the current version of the schema, as, building on the practicality of a visual approach to schema design, it is quite useful to be able to present a schema through a visual representation. Whether this is done automatically from the schema’s .json file or manually from the structure on Anamnesis, this step offers a real benefit.    
Finally, the third step involves drafting a **summary sheet**, again outside of Anamnesis (in our case, on the wiki referenced in the workflow’s metadata) which allows us to document information that has already been structured as schema metadata (see step 2), but also enriched it with a range of information that can help to better **understand** the schema. A template is provided in the full workflow documentation.

- And to complete this workflow, a **publication** stage still needs to be developed. At present, we have identified the HSportal tool as a potential platform for publishing the schema and making it available within the context of alignment with **ontologies**, thereby taking it to an even higher level. We hope to be able to enhance this workflow in the future, taking into account the capabilities available and feedback regarding the specific benefits of this publication stage for the schema itself.

concept.label: IIIF
concept.definition: The International Image Interoperability Framework (IIIF) is a set of shared application programming interface (API) specifications for interoperable functionality in digital image repositories. The IIIF is comprised of and driven by a community of libraries, museums, archives, software companies, and other organizations working together to create, test, refine, implement and promote the IIIF specifications. Using JSON-LD, linked data, and standard W3C web protocols such as Web Annotation, IIIF makes it easy to parse and share digital image data, migrate across technology systems, and provide enhanced image access for scholars and researchers. In short, IIIF enables better, faster and cheaper image delivery. It lets you leverage interoperability and the fabric of the Web to access new possibilities and new users for your image-based resources, while reducing long term maintenance and technological lock in. IIIF gives users a rich set of baseline functionality for viewing, zooming, and assembling the best mix of resources and tools to view, compare, manipulate and work with images on the Web, an experience made portableshareable, citable, and embeddable. (source: https://iiif.io/community/faq/)

concept.label: JPEG
concept.definition: JPEG ( JAY-peg) is a commonly used method of lossy compression for digital images, particularly for those images produced by digital photography. The degree of compression can be adjusted, allowing a selectable tradeoff between storage size and image quality. JPEG typically achieves 10:1 compression with little perceptible loss in image quality. JPEG compression is used in a number of image file formats. JPEG/Exif is the most common image format used by digital cameras and other photographic image capture devices; along with JPEG/JFIF, it is the most common format for storing and transmitting photographic images on the World Wide Web. These format variations are often not distinguished, and are simply called JPEG. The term "JPEG" is an initialism/acronym for the Joint Photographic Experts Group, which created the standard. The MIME media type for JPEG is image/jpeg, except in older Internet Explorer versions, which provides a MIME type of image/pjpeg when uploading JPEG images. JPEG files usually have a filename extension of .jpg or .jpeg. JPEG/JFIF supports a maximum image size of 65,53565,535 pixels, hence up to 4 gigapixels for an aspect ratio of 1:1.

concept.label: TIFF
concept.definition: Tagged Image File Format, abbreviated TIFF or TIF, is a computer file format for storing raster graphics images, popular among graphic artists, the publishing industry, and photographers. TIFF is widely supported by scanning, faxing, word processing, optical character recognition, image manipulation, desktop publishing, and page-layout applications. The format was created by Aldus Corporation for use in desktop publishing. It published the latest version 6.0 in 1992, subsequently updated with an Adobe Systems copyright after the latter acquired Aldus in 1994. OHMS is an open source, web-based application designed to improve the user experience you provide for oral history, no matter what CMS or repository you use. There are 2 main components of the OHMS system

OHMS Application: The OHMS application is where the work is done. This is the back-end, web-based application where interviews are imported, and metadata is created. In the OHMS application transcripts are time-coded and/or interviews are indexed. Upon completion, the interview record (including the synchronized transcript and/or time-coded index) are exported as an XML file. When located on a web server, the OHMS XML file is what interfaces with your content management system through the OHMS Viewer.

OHMS Viewer: The OHMS viewer is the user interface of ohms. When an interview is called by the repository, the OHMS viewer loads, calling select interview level metadata and the intra interview level metadata created in the OHMS Application from the corresponding xml file.

Rather than replacing the recording with a transcription, this process structures the resource into titled, synopsised, and keyworded segments, enabling users to navigate directly to specific points in the interview and locate content by person, place, or institution. By preserving the double voice of interviewer and interviewee at segment level and by using indexing — rather than transcription — as the primary access tool, the workflow supports listening to the original recording as the main mode of engagement with the source, in line with the stated aim of guiding and educating listening. This kind of indexing can be carried out either through OHMS (Oral History Metadata Synchronizer) or without the support of any dedicated application. The output is a reviewed, structured index suitable for publication.

relatedItems.label: Research Design and Methodological Planning
relatedItems.description:
The treatment of oral sources begins with a carefully structured phase of research design and methodological planning, which shapes the quality of the data collected as well as its legal validity, long-term preservation, and future reuse. This phase brings together methodological reflection, technical, and ethical choices, legal awareness, and archival foresight.

At its core lies a solid grounding in the principles and practices of linguistics and oral history. Researchers—and, where applicable, collaborators—should develop a clear awareness of the legal, ethical, and deontological implications of working with oral testimonies. This includes familiarity with relevant international and national guidelines, such as those of the Oral History Society (OHS) and the Associazione Italiana di Storia Orale (AISO), and an understanding of the responsibilities linked to the collection, processing, and preservation of personal narratives. At this stage, the focus is on building awareness within the research team, rather than formally informing participants.

Methodological planning also involves defining the research framework, including research questions, scope, and participant selection. Interviews should be conceived as co-constructed communicative events; therefore, flexible interview guides are preferable to rigid questionnaires, allowing space for digressions that may open new lines of inquiry.

Researchers must also anticipate the conditions of the recording, including the choice of environment and the establishment of a relationship of trust with participants, which directly affects the quality and interpretability of the testimonies.

Technical planning is equally essential. Decisions regarding recording formats (audio or audio-video) and equipment should be made in relation to research objectives and future uses of the data. These choices are methodological as much as technical, as they shape the nature and reusability of the sources.

Finally, this phase includes preparing the documentation resources that will support the workflow, such as interview guides, information sheets, consent and authorization forms, and recording sheets for contextual data. Anticipating legal requirements, preservation strategies, and future access conditions ensures coherence across the process and supports the sustainable reuse of oral sources.

label: OrlandoVision (OVis)
description:
An application for visualizing a specific collection of authors, and the links or associations between them. Links are determined by co-occurrence in the Orlando dataset. The current dataset consists of authors, other people associated with them, and the text entries upon which these associations are based. The application is designed in such a way that it could be extended to use other datasets as well.  

The display can be customized in the several ways. Node colours, shapes and sizes can be altered. More significantly, the layout of the graph can be chosen from amongst several different algorithms.  

As the collection is quite large, there are many filtering options available. In terms of author, the following categories can be specified: gender, author/non-author, and author nationality. The user can create complex search queries of the authors and the text, and specify a date restriction for the authors' life span.  

Each association in the text has been tagged with one or more semantic attributes, i.e. the type or meaning of the relation between the people. These tags have been organized into a tree, moving from general to more specific relations. Each tag in the tree can be checked/unchecked, further filtering the results.  

Finally, a data set and customizations can be saved as a session which can then be loaded at a later time. In addition, screenshots of the current layout can be saved to an image file.

relatedItems.description:
Produce a transcription of the recorded interview in order to enable analysis, indexing, and long-term accessibility. Transcription constitutes a key stage in the enrichment of the oral source, transforming an audio or audiovisual document into a textual resource that can be searched, annotated, and reused.

Define the level of transcription according to the objectives of the research. This may range from verbatim transcription (including hesitations, pauses, and non-verbal elements) to a more edited version that improves readability while preserving the meaning of the discourse. Where relevant, adopt established transcription conventions and ensure consistency across the corpus.

If required, integrate time-coding to align the transcription with the original recording, facilitating navigation between text and audio/video. Consider also the need for translation, particularly in multilingual research contexts.

During transcription, pay attention to the treatment of personal data and sensitive information. Anonymisation or pseudonymisation may be necessary, especially when preparing the material for dissemination or public access. Any modifications should be documented to ensure transparency and reproducibility.

The transcription should be treated as a distinct but related document within the oral source corpus. It must therefore be documented through a dedicated record, including its relationship to the original recording, the tools and methods used, and the identity of the transcriber.

This step may be carried out prior to, or in parallel with, the description and metadata creation phase, depending on the research design and available resources. In all cases, it significantly enhances the findability, accessibility, and reusability of the oral source in line with FAIR principles.

description:
Overview is a free, web-based tool for document mining. Developed by and for journalists, Overview is also broadly applicable to other corpus-based research applications. Aside from providing [advanced search features](http://overview.ap.org/about/overview.ap.org/blog/2013/12/advanced-search-quoted-phrases-boolean-operators-fuzzy-matching-and-more/) such as regular expressions and fuzzy matching, Overview automatically [sorts documents according to topic](http://overview.ap.org/blog/2013/04/how-overview-can-organize-thousands-of-documents-for-a-reporter/) and provides a fast visualization and reading interface. You can apply tags to search results, individual documents, or entire topics to track what you've found, then export the entire document set with its tags to perform further processing or create visualization. It's been used for qualitative research, social media conversation analysis, legal document review, digital humanities, and more.  
Overview can be run via the web interface (max 200 000 documents) or downloaded and installed. The system can import documents in PDF or CSV format and currently supports analysis in 9 languages. The code is open source and there is a plugin API to extend Overview's analysis and visualization capability.

relatedItems.label: OWID – elexiko
relatedItems.description:
elexiko ist ein Online-Informationssystem zur deutschen Gegenwartssprache, das den Wortschatz anhand aktueller Sprachdaten bis 2013 dokumentiert, erklärt und wissenschaftlich kommentiert. Der Schwerpunkt liegt auf dem Modul Lexikon zum öffentlichen Sprachgebrauch, das hochfrequente Stichwörter ausführlich in Bedeutung und Verwendung beschreibt. Für weniger häufige Wörter enthält das System Angaben zur Orthografie und zur Belegung im elexiko-Korpus. In Wortgruppenartikeln werden Stichwörter aus Themenfeldern, Wortfeldern oder sinnrelationalen Gruppen vergleichend dargestellt. Das Projekt wurde 2017 abgeschlossen und ist online über OWID verfügbar.

---

Its focus is on the Lexicon of Public Use module, which provides detailed descriptions of high-frequency entries regarding meaning and usage. relatedItems.label: OWID – Paronymwörterbuch
relatedItems.description:
„Paronyme – Dynamisch im Kontrast“ ist ein neues und neuartiges Nachschlagewerk für sprachliche Zweifelsfälle und Unsicherheiten. Erstmals werden lautlich, orthografisch und/oder semantisch ähnliche Wörter (z. B. farbig–farblich, kindlich–kindisch, universal–universell, Mehrheit–Mehrzahl) korpusbasiert in ihrem aktuellen Gebrauch untersucht und dokumentiert. Nutzer:innen können sich über die Bedeutung jedes Ausdrucks in zahlreichen Angaben und Verwendungsbeispielen informieren. Dies erfolgt kontrastiv und dynamisch in selbst wählbaren Ausschnitts- oder Vergleichsansichten, im Überblick oder im Detail.

---

“Paronyms – Dynamic in Contrast” is a new and innovative reference work for linguistic uncertainties and doubtful cases. For the first time, phonetically, orthographically, and/or semantically similar words (e.g., farbig–farblich, kindlich–kindisch, universal–universell, Mehrheit–Mehrzahl) are examined and documented based on corpus data in their current usage. Users can explore the meaning of each expression through numerous notes and usage examples. This is done contrastively and dynamically in user-selectable snippet or comparison views, either in overview or in detail.

relatedItems.label: OWID – Sprichwörterbuch
relatedItems.description:
Wer kennt nicht diese Sprüche aus der Kindheit? "Morgenstund hat Gold im Mund" wollte man ebenso wenig hören wie "Ordnung ist das halbe Leben".
Aber diese Sprichwörter drücken ebenso Lebenserfahrungen aus wie "Den Mutigen gehört die Welt" oder "Der Glaube versetzt Berge". Sprichwörter helfen, komplexe Sachverhalte prägnant auf den Punkt zu bringen, Situationen und Verhaltensweisen plastisch zu kommentieren und manchmal etwas „durch die Blume“ zu sagen. Diese festen Sätze gehören zum Kulturgut einer Sprachgemeinschaft und werden als Weisheiten von Generation zu Generation weitergetragen. Gleichzeitig unterliegen Sprichwörter einem stetigen Wandel. Im OWID-Sprichwörterbuch kann man sich ein Bild davon machen, wie lebendig und variabel Sprichwörter auch noch im 21. Jahrhundert sind, wozu Sprecher sie benutzen und auf welche Weise neue entstehen, z. B. in der Werbung.

---

Who doesn't know these sayings from childhood? “The early bird catches the worm” was just as unwelcome as “Tidiness is half the battle.”
But these proverbs express life experiences just as much as “fortune favors the brave” or “faith can move mountains.” Proverbs help to succinctly summarize complex issues, vividly comment on situations and behaviors, and sometimes say something “in a roundabout way.” These fixed phrases are part of the cultural heritage of a language community and are passed on from generation to generation as words of wisdom. At the same time, proverbs are subject to constant change. The OWID proverb dictionary gives an idea of how lively and variable proverbs still are in the 21st century, how speakers use them, and how new ones are created, e.g., in advertising.

relatedItems.label: OWID – Sprichwörterbuch
relatedItems.description:
Wer kennt nicht diese Sprüche aus der Kindheit? "Morgenstund hat Gold im Mund" wollte man ebenso wenig hören wie "Ordnung ist das halbe Leben".
Aber diese Sprichwörter drücken ebenso Lebenserfahrungen aus wie "Den Mutigen gehört die Welt" oder "Der Glaube versetzt Berge". Sprichwörter helfen, komplexe Sachverhalte prägnant auf den Punkt zu bringen, Situationen und Verhaltensweisen plastisch zu kommentieren und manchmal etwas „durch die Blume“ zu sagen. Diese festen Sätze gehören zum Kulturgut einer Sprachgemeinschaft und werden als Weisheiten von Generation zu Generation weitergetragen. Gleichzeitig unterliegen Sprichwörter einem stetigen Wandel. Im OWID-Sprichwörterbuch kann man sich ein Bild davon machen, wie lebendig und variabel Sprichwörter auch noch im 21. Jahrhundert sind, wozu Sprecher sie benutzen und auf welche Weise neue entstehen, z. B. in der Werbung.

---

Who doesn't know these sayings from childhood? “The early bird catches the worm” was just as unwelcome as “Tidiness is half the battle.”
But these proverbs express life experiences just as much as “fortune favors the brave” or “faith can move mountains.” Proverbs help to succinctly summarize complex issues, vividly comment on situations and behaviors, and sometimes say something “in a roundabout way.” These fixed phrases are part of the cultural heritage of a language community and are passed on from generation to generation as words of wisdom. At the same time, proverbs are subject to constant change. The OWID proverb dictionary gives an idea of how lively and variable proverbs still are in the 21st century, how speakers use them, and how new ones are created, e.g., in advertising.

label: OWID – elexiko

relatedItems.label: OWID - Schlüsselwörter der Wendezeit
relatedItems.description:
Die „Schlüsselwörter der Wendezeit“ wurden in den Jahren 1993–1996 am IDS mit dem Ziel erarbeitet, den öffentlichen Sprachgebrauch der Wendezeit in der DDR und in der Bundesrepublik konsequent korpusbezogen und textdokumentativ darzustellen. Es handelt sich um ein auf der Basis eines definierten Textkorpus des Wendekorpus erarbeitetes Buch, das den öffentlichen Gebrauch ausgewählter Lexeme in einem bestimmten Zeitraum der Wendezeit darstellt, erläutert und dokumentiert. Anlässlich des 25-jährigen Jubiläums der Ereignisse der Wendezeit wurde das Wörterbuch für eine Onlinefassung aufbereitet und in OWID integriert.

---

The “Key Words of the Reunification Period” were created between 1993 and 1996 at the IDS with the aim of documenting public language use during the reunification period in East and West Germany in a corpus-based and text-documentary manner. It is a book based on a defined text corpus of the Reunification Corpus that presents, explains, and documents the public use of selected lexemes during a specific period of the reunification. On the occasion of the 25th anniversary of the reunification events, the book was prepared as an online version and integrated into OWID.

relatedItems.description:
OWIDplus ist eine experimentelle Plattform für multilinguale lexikalisch-lexikografische Daten, für quantitative lexikalische Auswertungen und für interaktive lexikalische Anwendungen, die in einzelnen unverbundenen Rubriken präsentiert werden. OWIDplus richtet sich an Fachkolleginnen und Studierende und wird kontinuierlich erweitert.

---

OWIDplus is an experimental platform for multilingual lexical-lexicographic data, for quantitative lexical analyses and for interactive lexical applications which are presented in individual, unconnected sections. OWIDplus addresses an academic audience and is under active development.

relatedItems.label: OWID – Paronymwörterbuch
relatedItems.description:
„Paronyme – Dynamisch im Kontrast“ ist ein neues und neuartiges Nachschlagewerk für sprachliche Zweifelsfälle und Unsicherheiten. Erstmals werden lautlich, orthografisch und/oder semantisch ähnliche Wörter (z. B. farbig–farblich, kindlich–kindisch, universal–universell, Mehrheit–Mehrzahl) korpusbasiert in ihrem aktuellen Gebrauch untersucht und dokumentiert. Nutzer:innen können sich über die Bedeutung jedes Ausdrucks in zahlreichen Angaben und Verwendungsbeispielen informieren. Dies erfolgt kontrastiv und dynamisch in selbst wählbaren Ausschnitts- oder Vergleichsansichten, im Überblick oder im Detail.

---

“Paronyms – Dynamic in Contrast” is a new and innovative reference work for linguistic uncertainties and doubtful cases. For the first time, phonetically, orthographically, and/or semantically similar words (e.g., farbig–farblich, kindlich–kindisch, universal–universell, Mehrheit–Mehrzahl) are examined and documented based on corpus data in their current usage. Users can explore the meaning of each expression through numerous notes and usage examples. This is done contrastively and dynamically in user-selectable snippet or comparison views, either in overview or in detail.

relatedItems.label: OWID – Sprichwörterbuch
relatedItems.description:
Wer kennt nicht diese Sprüche aus der Kindheit? "Morgenstund hat Gold im Mund" wollte man ebenso wenig hören wie "Ordnung ist das halbe Leben".
Aber diese Sprichwörter drücken ebenso Lebenserfahrungen aus wie "Den Mutigen gehört die Welt" oder "Der Glaube versetzt Berge". Sprichwörter helfen, komplexe Sachverhalte prägnant auf den Punkt zu bringen, Situationen und Verhaltensweisen plastisch zu kommentieren und manchmal etwas „durch die Blume“ zu sagen. Diese festen Sätze gehören zum Kulturgut einer Sprachgemeinschaft und werden als Weisheiten von Generation zu Generation weitergetragen. Gleichzeitig unterliegen Sprichwörter einem stetigen Wandel. Im OWID-Sprichwörterbuch kann man sich ein Bild davon machen, wie lebendig und variabel Sprichwörter auch noch im 21. Jahrhundert sind, wozu Sprecher sie benutzen und auf welche Weise neue entstehen, z. B. in der Werbung.

---

Who doesn't know these sayings from childhood? “The early bird catches the worm” was just as unwelcome as “Tidiness is half the battle.”
But these proverbs express life experiences just as much as “fortune favors the brave” or “faith can move mountains.” Proverbs help to succinctly summarize complex issues, vividly comment on situations and behaviors, and sometimes say something “in a roundabout way.” These fixed phrases are part of the cultural heritage of a language community and are passed on from generation to generation as words of wisdom. At the same time, proverbs are subject to constant change. The OWID proverb dictionary gives an idea of how lively and variable proverbs still are in the 21st century, how speakers use them, and how new ones are created, e.g., in advertising.

relatedItems.label: OWID - Schlüsselwörter der Wendezeit
relatedItems.description:
Die „Schlüsselwörter der Wendezeit“ wurden in den Jahren 1993–1996 am IDS mit dem Ziel erarbeitet, den öffentlichen Sprachgebrauch der Wendezeit in der DDR und in der Bundesrepublik konsequent korpusbezogen und textdokumentativ darzustellen. Es handelt sich um ein auf der Basis eines definierten Textkorpus des Wendekorpus erarbeitetes Buch, das den öffentlichen Gebrauch ausgewählter Lexeme in einem bestimmten Zeitraum der Wendezeit darstellt, erläutert und dokumentiert. Anlässlich des 25-jährigen Jubiläums der Ereignisse der Wendezeit wurde das Wörterbuch für eine Onlinefassung aufbereitet und in OWID integriert.

---

The “Key Words of the Reunification Period” were created between 1993 and 1996 at the IDS with the aim of documenting public language use during the reunification period in East and West Germany in a corpus-based and text-documentary manner. It is a book based on a defined text corpus of the Reunification Corpus that presents, explains, and documents the public use of selected lexemes during a specific period of the reunification. On the occasion of the 25th anniversary of the reunification events, the book was prepared as an online version and integrated into OWID.

OWIDplus is an experimental platform for multilingual lexical-lexicographic data, for quantitative lexical analyses and for interactive lexical applications which are presented in individual, unconnected sections. OWIDplus addresses an academic audience and is under active development.

relatedItems.label: OWID – elexiko
relatedItems.description:
elexiko ist ein Online-Informationssystem zur deutschen Gegenwartssprache, das den Wortschatz anhand aktueller Sprachdaten bis 2013 dokumentiert, erklärt und wissenschaftlich kommentiert. Der Schwerpunkt liegt auf dem Modul Lexikon zum öffentlichen Sprachgebrauch, das hochfrequente Stichwörter ausführlich in Bedeutung und Verwendung beschreibt. Für weniger häufige Wörter enthält das System Angaben zur Orthografie und zur Belegung im elexiko-Korpus. In Wortgruppenartikeln werden Stichwörter aus Themenfeldern, Wortfeldern oder sinnrelationalen Gruppen vergleichend dargestellt. Das Projekt wurde 2017 abgeschlossen und ist online über OWID verfügbar.

---

elexiko is an online information system for contemporary German that documents, explains, and scientifically comments on the vocabulary based on current language data up to 2013. Its focus is on the Lexicon of Public Use module, which provides detailed descriptions of high-frequency entries regarding meaning and usage. Less frequent words include information on orthography and occurrence in the elexiko corpus. Word group articles present entries from thematic fields, word fields, or semantic groups in a comparative manner. The project was completed in 2017 and is available online via OWID.

relatedItems.label: OWID – Paronymwörterbuch
relatedItems.description:
„Paronyme – Dynamisch im Kontrast“ ist ein neues und neuartiges Nachschlagewerk für sprachliche Zweifelsfälle und Unsicherheiten. Erstmals werden lautlich, orthografisch und/oder semantisch ähnliche Wörter (z. B. farbig–farblich, kindlich–kindisch, universal–universell, Mehrheit–Mehrzahl) korpusbasiert in ihrem aktuellen Gebrauch untersucht und dokumentiert. Nutzer:innen können sich über die Bedeutung jedes Ausdrucks in zahlreichen Angaben und Verwendungsbeispielen informieren. Dies erfolgt kontrastiv und dynamisch in selbst wählbaren Ausschnitts- oder Vergleichsansichten, im Überblick oder im Detail.

---

“Paronyms – Dynamic in Contrast” is a new and innovative reference work for linguistic uncertainties and doubtful cases. For the first time, phonetically, orthographically, and/or semantically similar words (e.g., farbig–farblich, kindlich–kindisch, universal–universell, Mehrheit–Mehrzahl) are examined and documented based on corpus data in their current usage. Users can explore the meaning of each expression through numerous notes and usage examples. This is done contrastively and dynamically in user-selectable snippet or comparison views, either in overview or in detail.

Das Online‑Wortschatz‑Informationssystem Deutsch (OWID) des IDS ist eine wissenschaftliche, korpusbasierte Plattform für verschiedene lexikografische Ressourcen wie Neologismen‑, Fremd‑ und Diskurswörterbücher. Es verknüpft Forschungsergebnisse aus der Korpuslinguistik mit benutzerfreundlichen Online‑Wörterbüchern. Zudem bietet OWID eine elektronische Bibliografie zur Lexikografie (OBELEX). Die Plattform richtet sich sowohl an Sprachwissenschaftler:innen als auch an sprachinteressierte Nutzer:innen.

The Online German Lexical Information System (OWID) at IDS is a scientific, corpus-based platform providing various lexicographical resources, including dictionaries of neologisms, foreign words, and discourse vocabulary. It links findings from corpus linguistics with user-friendly online dictionaries. OWID also includes an electronic bibliography on lexicography (OBELEX). The platform is aimed at both linguists and users interested in the German language.

Die „Schlüsselwörter der Wendezeit“ wurden in den Jahren 1993–1996 am IDS mit dem Ziel erarbeitet, den öffentlichen Sprachgebrauch der Wendezeit in der DDR und in der Bundesrepublik konsequent korpusbezogen und textdokumentativ darzustellen. Es handelt sich um ein auf der Basis eines definierten Textkorpus des Wendekorpus erarbeitetes Buch, das den öffentlichen Gebrauch ausgewählter Lexeme in einem bestimmten Zeitraum der Wendezeit darstellt, erläutert und dokumentiert. Anlässlich des 25-jährigen Jubiläums der Ereignisse der Wendezeit wurde das Wörterbuch für eine Onlinefassung aufbereitet und in OWID integriert.

---

The “Key Words of the Reunification Period” were created between 1993 and 1996 at the IDS with the aim of documenting public language use during the reunification period in East and West Germany in a corpus-based and text-documentary manner. It is a book based on a defined text corpus of the Reunification Corpus that presents, explains, and documents the public use of selected lexemes during a specific period of the reunification. On the occasion of the 25th anniversary of the reunification events, the book was prepared as an online version and integrated into OWID.

relatedItems.description:
Dieses Wörterbuch ist das Nachschlagewerk zu der im Jahr 2012 erschienenen Untersuchung‚ Aspekte des Demokratiediskurses der späten 1960er Jahre.

---

This dictionary is the reference work for the study published in 2012, Aspects of the Discourse on Democracy in the Late 1960s.

relatedItems.label: OWID – Paronymwörterbuch
relatedItems.description:
„Paronyme – Dynamisch im Kontrast“ ist ein neues und neuartiges Nachschlagewerk für sprachliche Zweifelsfälle und Unsicherheiten. Erstmals werden lautlich, orthografisch und/oder semantisch ähnliche Wörter (z. B. farbig–farblich, kindlich–kindisch, universal–universell, Mehrheit–Mehrzahl) korpusbasiert in ihrem aktuellen Gebrauch untersucht und dokumentiert. Nutzer:innen können sich über die Bedeutung jedes Ausdrucks in zahlreichen Angaben und Verwendungsbeispielen informieren. Dies erfolgt kontrastiv und dynamisch in selbst wählbaren Ausschnitts- oder Vergleichsansichten, im Überblick oder im Detail.

---

“Paronyms – Dynamic in Contrast” is a new and innovative reference work for linguistic uncertainties and doubtful cases. For the first time, phonetically, orthographically, and/or semantically similar words (e.g., farbig–farblich, kindlich–kindisch, universal–universell, Mehrheit–Mehrzahl) are examined and documented based on corpus data in their current usage. Users can explore the meaning of each expression through numerous notes and usage examples. This is done contrastively and dynamically in user-selectable snippet or comparison views, either in overview or in detail.

relatedItems.label: OWID
relatedItems.description:
Das Online‑Wortschatz‑Informationssystem Deutsch (OWID) des IDS ist eine wissenschaftliche, korpusbasierte Plattform für verschiedene lexikografische Ressourcen wie Neologismen‑, Fremd‑ und Diskurswörterbücher. Es verknüpft Forschungsergebnisse aus der Korpuslinguistik mit benutzerfreundlichen Online‑Wörterbüchern. Zudem bietet OWID eine elektronische Bibliografie zur Lexikografie (OBELEX). Die Plattform richtet sich sowohl an Sprachwissenschaftler:innen als auch an sprachinteressierte Nutzer:innen.

---

The Online German Lexical Information System (OWID) at IDS is a scientific, corpus-based platform providing various lexicographical resources, including dictionaries of neologisms, foreign words, and discourse vocabulary. It links findings from corpus linguistics with user-friendly online dictionaries. OWID also includes an electronic bibliography on lexicography (OBELEX). The platform is aimed at both linguists and users interested in the German language.

relatedItems.label: OWID – Sprichwörterbuch
relatedItems.description:
Wer kennt nicht diese Sprüche aus der Kindheit? "Morgenstund hat Gold im Mund" wollte man ebenso wenig hören wie "Ordnung ist das halbe Leben".
Aber diese Sprichwörter drücken ebenso Lebenserfahrungen aus wie "Den Mutigen gehört die Welt" oder "Der Glaube versetzt Berge". Sprichwörter helfen, komplexe Sachverhalte prägnant auf den Punkt zu bringen, Situationen und Verhaltensweisen plastisch zu kommentieren und manchmal etwas „durch die Blume“ zu sagen. Diese festen Sätze gehören zum Kulturgut einer Sprachgemeinschaft und werden als Weisheiten von Generation zu Generation weitergetragen. Gleichzeitig unterliegen Sprichwörter einem stetigen Wandel. Im OWID-Sprichwörterbuch kann man sich ein Bild davon machen, wie lebendig und variabel Sprichwörter auch noch im 21. Jahrhundert sind, wozu Sprecher sie benutzen und auf welche Weise neue entstehen, z. B. in der Werbung.

---

Who doesn't know these sayings from childhood? “The early bird catches the worm” was just as unwelcome as “Tidiness is half the battle.”
But these proverbs express life experiences just as much as “fortune favors the brave” or “faith can move mountains.” Proverbs help to succinctly summarize complex issues, vividly comment on situations and behaviors, and sometimes say something “in a roundabout way.” These fixed phrases are part of the cultural heritage of a language community and are passed on from generation to generation as words of wisdom. At the same time, proverbs are subject to constant change. The OWID proverb dictionary gives an idea of how lively and variable proverbs still are in the 21st century, how speakers use them, and how new ones are created, e.g., in advertising.

relatedItems.label: OWID – elexiko
relatedItems.description:
elexiko ist ein Online-Informationssystem zur deutschen Gegenwartssprache, das den Wortschatz anhand aktueller Sprachdaten bis 2013 dokumentiert, erklärt und wissenschaftlich kommentiert. Der Schwerpunkt liegt auf dem Modul Lexikon zum öffentlichen Sprachgebrauch, das hochfrequente Stichwörter ausführlich in Bedeutung und Verwendung beschreibt. Für weniger häufige Wörter enthält das System Angaben zur Orthografie und zur Belegung im elexiko-Korpus. In Wortgruppenartikeln werden Stichwörter aus Themenfeldern, Wortfeldern oder sinnrelationalen Gruppen vergleichend dargestellt. Das Projekt wurde 2017 abgeschlossen und ist online über OWID verfügbar.

---

elexiko is an online information system for contemporary German that documents, explains, and scientifically comments on the vocabulary based on current language data up to 2013. Its focus is on the Lexicon of Public Use module, which provides detailed descriptions of high-frequency entries regarding meaning and usage. Less frequent words include information on orthography and occurrence in the elexiko corpus. Word group articles present entries from thematic fields, word fields, or semantic groups in a comparative manner. The project was completed in 2017 and is available online via OWID.

relatedItems.label: OWID - Schlüsselwörter der Wendezeit
relatedItems.description:
Die „Schlüsselwörter der Wendezeit“ wurden in den Jahren 1993–1996 am IDS mit dem Ziel erarbeitet, den öffentlichen Sprachgebrauch der Wendezeit in der DDR und in der Bundesrepublik konsequent korpusbezogen und textdokumentativ darzustellen. Es handelt sich um ein auf der Basis eines definierten Textkorpus des Wendekorpus erarbeitetes Buch, das den öffentlichen Gebrauch ausgewählter Lexeme in einem bestimmten Zeitraum der Wendezeit darstellt, erläutert und dokumentiert. Anlässlich des 25-jährigen Jubiläums der Ereignisse der Wendezeit wurde das Wörterbuch für eine Onlinefassung aufbereitet und in OWID integriert.

---

It is a book based on a defined text corpus of the Reunification Corpus that presents, explains, and documents the public use of selected lexemes during a specific period of the reunification. On the occasion of the 25th anniversary of the reunification events, the book was prepared as an online version and integrated into OWID.

OWIDplus richtet sich an Fachkolleginnen und Studierende und wird kontinuierlich erweitert.

---

OWIDplus is an experimental platform for multilingual lexical-lexicographic data, for quantitative lexical analyses and for interactive lexical applications which are presented in individual, unconnected sections. OWIDplus addresses an academic audience and is under active development.

relatedItems.label: OWID – elexiko
relatedItems.description:
elexiko ist ein Online-Informationssystem zur deutschen Gegenwartssprache, das den Wortschatz anhand aktueller Sprachdaten bis 2013 dokumentiert, erklärt und wissenschaftlich kommentiert. Der Schwerpunkt liegt auf dem Modul Lexikon zum öffentlichen Sprachgebrauch, das hochfrequente Stichwörter ausführlich in Bedeutung und Verwendung beschreibt. Für weniger häufige Wörter enthält das System Angaben zur Orthografie und zur Belegung im elexiko-Korpus. In Wortgruppenartikeln werden Stichwörter aus Themenfeldern, Wortfeldern oder sinnrelationalen Gruppen vergleichend dargestellt. Das Projekt wurde 2017 abgeschlossen und ist online über OWID verfügbar.

---

elexiko is an online information system for contemporary German that documents, explains, and scientifically comments on the vocabulary based on current language data up to 2013. Its focus is on the Lexicon of Public Use module, which provides detailed descriptions of high-frequency entries regarding meaning and usage. Less frequent words include information on orthography and occurrence in the elexiko corpus. Word group articles present entries from thematic fields, word fields, or semantic groups in a comparative manner. The project was completed in 2017 and is available online via OWID.

relatedItems.label: OWID – Paronymwörterbuch
relatedItems.description:
„Paronyme – Dynamisch im Kontrast“ ist ein neues und neuartiges Nachschlagewerk für sprachliche Zweifelsfälle und Unsicherheiten. Erstmals werden lautlich, orthografisch und/oder semantisch ähnliche Wörter (z. B. farbig–farblich, kindlich–kindisch, universal–universell, Mehrheit–Mehrzahl) korpusbasiert in ihrem aktuellen Gebrauch untersucht und dokumentiert. Nutzer:innen können sich über die Bedeutung jedes Ausdrucks in zahlreichen Angaben und Verwendungsbeispielen informieren. Dies erfolgt kontrastiv und dynamisch in selbst wählbaren Ausschnitts- oder Vergleichsansichten, im Überblick oder im Detail.

---

“Paronyms – Dynamic in Contrast” is a new and innovative reference work for linguistic uncertainties and doubtful cases. For the first time, phonetically, orthographically, and/or semantically similar words (e.g., farbig–farblich, kindlich–kindisch, universal–universell, Mehrheit–Mehrzahl) are examined and documented based on corpus data in their current usage. Users can explore the meaning of each expression through numerous notes and usage examples. This is done contrastively and dynamically in user-selectable snippet or comparison views, either in overview or in detail.

relatedItems.label: OWID

Das Online‑Wortschatz‑Informationssystem Deutsch (OWID) des IDS ist eine wissenschaftliche, korpusbasierte Plattform für verschiedene lexikografische Ressourcen wie Neologismen‑, Fremd‑ und Diskurswörterbücher. Es verknüpft Forschungsergebnisse aus der Korpuslinguistik mit benutzerfreundlichen Online‑Wörterbüchern. Zudem bietet OWID eine elektronische Bibliografie zur Lexikografie (OBELEX). Die Plattform richtet sich sowohl an Sprachwissenschaftler:innen als auch an sprachinteressierte Nutzer:innen.

The Online German Lexical Information System (OWID) at IDS is a scientific, corpus-based platform providing various lexicographical resources, including dictionaries of neologisms, foreign words, and discourse vocabulary. It links findings from corpus linguistics with user-friendly online dictionaries. OWID also includes an electronic bibliography on lexicography (OBELEX). The platform is aimed at both linguists and users interested in the German language.

relatedItems.label: OWID – Sprichwörterbuch
relatedItems.description:
Wer kennt nicht diese Sprüche aus der Kindheit? "Morgenstund hat Gold im Mund" wollte man ebenso wenig hören wie "Ordnung ist das halbe Leben".
Aber diese Sprichwörter drücken ebenso Lebenserfahrungen aus wie "Den Mutigen gehört die Welt" oder "Der Glaube versetzt Berge". Sprichwörter helfen, komplexe Sachverhalte prägnant auf den Punkt zu bringen, Situationen und Verhaltensweisen plastisch zu kommentieren und manchmal etwas „durch die Blume“ zu sagen. Diese festen Sätze gehören zum Kulturgut einer Sprachgemeinschaft und werden als Weisheiten von Generation zu Generation weitergetragen. Gleichzeitig unterliegen Sprichwörter einem stetigen Wandel. Im OWID-Sprichwörterbuch kann man sich ein Bild davon machen, wie lebendig und variabel Sprichwörter auch noch im 21. Jahrhundert sind, wozu Sprecher sie benutzen und auf welche Weise neue entstehen, z. B. in der Werbung.

---

It is a book based on a defined text corpus of the Reunification Corpus that presents, explains, and documents the public use of selected lexemes during a specific period of the reunification. On the occasion of the 25th anniversary of the reunification events, the book was prepared as an online version and integrated into OWID.

relatedItems.label: OWID – elexiko
relatedItems.description:
elexiko ist ein Online-Informationssystem zur deutschen Gegenwartssprache, das den Wortschatz anhand aktueller Sprachdaten bis 2013 dokumentiert, erklärt und wissenschaftlich kommentiert. Der Schwerpunkt liegt auf dem Modul Lexikon zum öffentlichen Sprachgebrauch, das hochfrequente Stichwörter ausführlich in Bedeutung und Verwendung beschreibt. Für weniger häufige Wörter enthält das System Angaben zur Orthografie und zur Belegung im elexiko-Korpus. In Wortgruppenartikeln werden Stichwörter aus Themenfeldern, Wortfeldern oder sinnrelationalen Gruppen vergleichend dargestellt. Das Projekt wurde 2017 abgeschlossen und ist online über OWID verfügbar.

---

elexiko is an online information system for contemporary German that documents, explains, and scientifically comments on the vocabulary based on current language data up to 2013. Its focus is on the Lexicon of Public Use module, which provides detailed descriptions of high-frequency entries regarding meaning and usage. Less frequent words include information on orthography and occurrence in the elexiko corpus. Word group articles present entries from thematic fields, word fields, or semantic groups in a comparative manner. The project was completed in 2017 and is available online via OWID.

Erstmals werden lautlich, orthografisch und/oder semantisch ähnliche Wörter (z. B. farbig–farblich, kindlich–kindisch, universal–universell, Mehrheit–Mehrzahl) korpusbasiert in ihrem aktuellen Gebrauch untersucht und dokumentiert. Nutzer:innen können sich über die Bedeutung jedes Ausdrucks in zahlreichen Angaben und Verwendungsbeispielen informieren. Dies erfolgt kontrastiv und dynamisch in selbst wählbaren Ausschnitts- oder Vergleichsansichten, im Überblick oder im Detail.

---

“Paronyms – Dynamic in Contrast” is a new and innovative reference work for linguistic uncertainties and doubtful cases. For the first time, phonetically, orthographically, and/or semantically similar words (e.g., farbig–farblich, kindlich–kindisch, universal–universell, Mehrheit–Mehrzahl) are examined and documented based on corpus data in their current usage. Users can explore the meaning of each expression through numerous notes and usage examples. This is done contrastively and dynamically in user-selectable snippet or comparison views, either in overview or in detail.

relatedItems.label: OWID – Sprichwörterbuch
relatedItems.description:
Wer kennt nicht diese Sprüche aus der Kindheit? "Morgenstund hat Gold im Mund" wollte man ebenso wenig hören wie "Ordnung ist das halbe Leben".
Aber diese Sprichwörter drücken ebenso Lebenserfahrungen aus wie "Den Mutigen gehört die Welt" oder "Der Glaube versetzt Berge". Sprichwörter helfen, komplexe Sachverhalte prägnant auf den Punkt zu bringen, Situationen und Verhaltensweisen plastisch zu kommentieren und manchmal etwas „durch die Blume“ zu sagen. Diese festen Sätze gehören zum Kulturgut einer Sprachgemeinschaft und werden als Weisheiten von Generation zu Generation weitergetragen. Gleichzeitig unterliegen Sprichwörter einem stetigen Wandel. Im OWID-Sprichwörterbuch kann man sich ein Bild davon machen, wie lebendig und variabel Sprichwörter auch noch im 21. Jahrhundert sind, wozu Sprecher sie benutzen und auf welche Weise neue entstehen, z. B. in der Werbung.

---

Who doesn't know these sayings from childhood? “The early bird catches the worm” was just as unwelcome as “Tidiness is half the battle.”
But these proverbs express life experiences just as much as “fortune favors the brave” or “faith can move mountains.” Proverbs help to succinctly summarize complex issues, vividly comment on situations and behaviors, and sometimes say something “in a roundabout way.” These fixed phrases are part of the cultural heritage of a language community and are passed on from generation to generation as words of wisdom. At the same time, proverbs are subject to constant change. The OWID proverb dictionary gives an idea of how lively and variable proverbs still are in the 21st century, how speakers use them, and how new ones are created, e.g., in advertising.

label: Panoptic
description:
Panoptic is a research-focused software designed to visualize, explore, and annotate large image corpora. It incorporates advanced image grouping algorithms based on similarity (MobileNet, average hash, SHA1), helping users efficiently sort and navigate extensive datasets. It also offers filtering, search, and annotation capabilities, enabling the creation, analysis, and export of sub-corpora.

Panoptic’s extensive features enable researchers to perform activities such as image clustering, visual similarity searches, batch or detailed annotation, associated data management, and multi-modal corpora processing.

Key Features

•	Corpus Exploration: Explore all items within an imported image corpus.

•	Automatic Image Grouping and Clustering: Organize images automatically based on visual similarity.

•	Similarity Search: Find images similar to a specific image or group of images.

•	Annotation: Add detailed properties to images, including date, URL, tags, numerical values, and other custom attributes.

•	Sorting and Filtering: Manage images by their imported or annotated properties, with flexible options for sorting, filtering, and grouping.

•	Properties Management: Import, manage, and export properties associated with images.

relatedItems.label: PANOPTIC, un outil d’exploration par similarité de vastes corpus d’images
relatedItems.description:
A French language resource that helps researchers explore large image corpora through similarity-based search. 

L’analyse de corpus d’images en SHS se heurte à différentes limites des outils numériques disponibles et des méthodologies employées. On trouve d’un côté des outils très spécifiques pour
certaines applications (détection de tel ou tel type d’objet, segmentation, classification supervisée. . .), qui manquent de souplesse. D’un autre côté, on trouve des outils très génériques,
non conçus pour les recherches en SHS (tels que des tableurs ou des outils de tri de photographies), dont les chercheurs et chercheuses se saisissent en détournant l’usage. Le présent article décrit une démarche méthodologique et technique pour tenter de combler cette lacune de l’outillage numérique. À l’occasion de différentes enquêtes sur la circulation d’images au sein des réseaux sociaux numériques, nous avons impulsé le développement d’un outil, PANOPTIC, dont l’objectif est de permettre aux chercheurs et chercheuses d’explorer et d’annoter de vastes corpus d’images associés à des métadonnées. Mobilisable au-delà de ce seul champ d’application, la solution logicielle proposée s’appuie sur des algorithmes de regroupement d’images par similarités visuelles pour aider à l’analyse.

relatedItems.label: Producing Structured Visual Data from Illustrated Heritage Corpora
relatedItems.description:
Illustrated heritage corpora bring together digitised pages, plates, photographs, prints, drawings, captions, inscriptions, handwritten notes, and catalogue records at different levels of granularity. This workflow provides a method for turning these heterogeneous sources into visual units that can be located, described, compared, and reused while preserving their connection to the original documents and collections.

Starting from a research question, the workflow guides the selection of a representative corpus, the preparation of images and metadata, and the definition of the visual and textual units to be identified. A reference sample establishes the expected structure and quality of the results. Automatic or semi-automatic processing can then be used to extract images and associated text, followed by expert review, correction, and evaluation. The validated results are converted into structured data that can support cataloguing, quantitative analysis, visual exploration, or the study of relationships between images, texts, people, places, and objects.

The workflow preserves source identifiers, processing history, uncertainty, and validation status throughout the process. Its outputs may include extracted image regions, annotations, transcriptions, structured metadata, authority links, similarity results, and documented datasets. These elements provide a reproducible basis for further research and enable the resulting data, methods, and evaluation criteria to be shared and adapted across heritage collections.

This process is particularly relevant to researchers working with visual or illustrated corpora; research engineers and data stewards; libraries, archives, museums and heritage institutions; digital humanities projects preparing training, evaluation or exploration datasets; and teaching and training teams introducing computer vision methods for cultural heritage.

relatedItems.label: Explore visual similarity (optional)
Building and Exploring a Massive Plurisemiotic Corpus from Social Media Data with Panoptic
relatedItems.description:
This workflow is intended for researchers in the social sciences and humanities who wish to build a corpus of images collected from a digital social network with their context (texts,
metadata) — here, Bluesky — and then explore it visually and semantically using the Panoptic tool. It covers the entire data lifecycle: from raw collection to the reasoned annotation of a cleaned corpus, including the technical structuring required for import into the tool.
The workflow is designed for plurisemiotic use: each image remains linked to its original text and metadata via a common identifier, which guarantees the traceability and reversibility of analytical choices.

Prerequisites: access to the Bluesky API (or data export), a scripting environment (Python mandatory) for collection and conversion, installation of Panoptic (open-source local application), spreadsheet or CSV editor.

Drive allows users to upload, store, and share any type of file (e.g., JPEG, MP4, JS, INDD, AI). The majority can be previewed, and many can be edited within Drive. Some files (e.g., DOCX, XLSX, PPTX) can be converted into compatible file types for editing, commenting, and more. Drive is the platform for Google Sheets, Docs, Slides, and many other approved applications. Files saved in Drive sync to all other devices, with an activity monitor that can be useful for version control (see what edits have been made and when, and revert back to previous instances if needed).

Offers both free and paid accounts, priced by data capacity: 15 GB (free), 100 GB ($1.99/month), 1 TB ($9.99/month), 10 TB ($99.99/month), 20 TB ($199.99/month), 30 TB ($299.99/month). Teams with more than five people can purchase unlimited storage for $10/user/month.

relatedItems.label: Formalising and bottom-up enriching the Ontology of a Generative Lexicon
relatedItems.description: This paper presents on-going research to formalise the ontology of a computational lexicon in OWL (W3C standard) as well as to enrich it by applying a bottom-up approach that extracts semantic information from the lexicon. The resource used follows the Generative Lexicon (GL) theory and therefore (1) puts a challenge to ontology design as its semantic types are multidimensional and (2) enables the acquisition of further knowledge on concepts from semantic units. The formalisation allows the ontology to be processed by Description Logics reasoners as well as to be employed in Semantic Web applications. Moreover, the lexicon-driven enrichment increases the semantic information present in the ontology making it appropriate for ontology-driven Natural Language Processing. Finally, the paper studies the application of these procedures to a subsequent GL-based biological resource.

relatedItems.label: Converting the PAROLE SIMPLE CLIPS Lexicon into RDF with lemon
relatedItems.description:
This paper describes the publication and linking of (parts of) PAROLE SIMPLE CLIPS (PSC), a large scale Italian
lexicon, to the Semantic Web and the Linked Data cloud using the lemon model. The main challenge of the conversion is
discussed, namely the reconciliation between the PSC semantic structure which contains richly encoded semantic information,
following the qualia structure of the generative lexicon theory and the lemon view of lexical sense as a reified pairing of a lexical
item and a concept in an ontology. The result is two datasets: one consists of a list of lemon lexical entries with their lexical
properties, relations and senses; the other consists of a list of OWL individuals representing the referents for the lexical senses.
These OWL individuals are linked to each other by a set of semantic relations and mapped onto the SIMPLE OWL ontology of
higher level semantic types.
