relatedItems.label: Report on Standards
relatedItems.description: This document describes mechanisms where interoperability of data is ensured with the use of standards. The standards we covered are both domain related, the archival standards in XML formats such as EAD, EAC-CPF and EAG, and transversal standards, whose use is recommended in the context of any digital project, in particular the ISO standards for the representation of language, script and countries. Interoperability of archival descriptions expressed in EAD is made possible with the specification of a specific EAD profile for EHRI. This profile is built and maintained using the TEI-ODD framework, which is explained of the first section of the report. Interoperability and reusability of EHRI resources is also ensured with the design of more consistent URLs, composed with standardised methods and using ISO reference codes. This design has to be seen as a first step through a persistent identifier system. The work initiated in WP11 and presented in this document will be continued, enhanced and developed by other EHRI work packages, WP7 Virtual Access to EHRI Virtual Observatory, WP10 Resource Identification and Integration Workflows and WP13 Research Data Infrastructures for Holocaust Material.

Pactols rassemble des mots-clés spécialisés (concepts) pour décrire sans ambiguïté le contenu de ressources documentaires et de jeux de données en archéologie, depuis la Préhistoire jusqu’à l’époque contemporaine, et tous les aspects des sciences de l’Antiquité. Le thésaurus est normalisé et multilingue : sa langue par défaut est le français et il est traduit en 5 langues. Il est libre d’accès et son évolution se fait dans un cadre contrôlé. Toute proposition de nouveaux termes suit donc une procédure bien définie. 

C’est ce processus de proposition/création de nouveau terme qui est présenté ici.

relatedItems.label: The Pactols Thesaurus
relatedItems.description:
Controlled, standardized and multilingual vocabulary for archaeology, from prehistory to the contemporary period and for the sciences of antiquity in all their aspects.

Pactols is a reservoir of controlled and multilingual keywords.

If it serves historically the indexing of the CCI (Frantiq's indexed collective catalog), its richness and its scalability seduced other communities. For several years, it has been used as a thematic repository for diversified resources (academic journals, scientific databases, heritage enhancement programs).

It was created by Frantiq (Federation and Resources on Antiquity constituted as a CNRS Service Group no. 3378), which brings together around fifty units CNRS, services of the Ministry of Culture, archaeological museums, local authorities and other public establishments.

It was developed with the support of MASA consortium, Memory of archaeologists and archaeological sites.

relatedItems.label: Opentheso
relatedItems.description:
Opentheso is a web-based thesaurus management tool dedicated to the management of vocabularies. 
It conforms to ISO 25964-1 2011 and ISO 25964-2:2012 standards (Information and documentation. Thesauri and interoperability with other vocabularies).
It is developed at the CNRS (National Center for Scientific Research - France), financed by GDS FRANTIQ (https://www.frantiq.fr/), la MOM (https://www.mom.fr/) and IR* Huma-Num (https://www.huma-num.fr/) with Consortium (MASA) Mémoire des archéologues et des sites archéologiques (https://masa.hypotheses.org/). 


OpenTheso is used by a network of 39 research libraries (FRANTIQ. Archaeology, 32 000 concepts. Contact : Blandine Nouvel), research units (Zoomatia, archaelogical research project), les Hospices civils de Lyon (medicine, 60000 concepts), l’Institut des Sciences de l’Homme (part of Rameau vocabulary)…

Ses fonctionnalités actuelles :
- Gestion avancée des termes et des branches
- Drag and Drop
- Gestion collaborative avec 4 niveaux d'authentification (Superadmin, Admin, User et Traducteur)
- Interopérable : génération automatique d'identifiants Handle et ARK (ce service est assuré par le PSIR de la MOM)
- WebServices REST
- import : SKOS, Turtle, JsonLD
- export : SKOS, Turtle, JsonLD, CSV et PDF



OpenTheso is released under the terms of the CeCILL_C license, fully compatible with the GNU GPL.

composedOf.description:
Le thésaurus Pactols fonctionne avec le logiciel de gestion de thésaurus Opentheso. La possibilité de proposer un nouveau concept/mot-clé nécessite d’avoir un compte avec un niveau d’autorisation au moins égal à « contributeur ». 

Pour obtenir un compte Pactols, adressez une demande à pactols@services.cnrs.fr en précisant votre identité, votre appartenance institutionnelle et la raison de la demande. Vous recevrez votre login par mail et à la première connexion, vous validerez le compte en créant votre mot de passe.

Une fois connecté, sélectionnez le thésaurus Pactols (« Lieux » ou « Sujets » ) pour accéder au module Candidats (signe + dans le menu de gauche).

relatedItems.label: Opentheso
relatedItems.description:
Opentheso is a web-based thesaurus management tool dedicated to the management of vocabularies. 
It conforms to ISO 25964-1 2011 and ISO 25964-2:2012 standards (Information and documentation. Thesauri and interoperability with other vocabularies).
It is developed at the CNRS (National Center for Scientific Research - France), financed by GDS FRANTIQ (https://www.frantiq.fr/), la MOM (https://www.mom.fr/) and IR* Huma-Num (https://www.huma-num.fr/) with Consortium (MASA) Mémoire des archéologues et des sites archéologiques (https://masa.hypotheses.org/). 


OpenTheso is used by a network of 39 research libraries (FRANTIQ. Archaeology, 32 000 concepts. Contact : Blandine Nouvel), research units (Zoomatia, archaelogical research project), les Hospices civils de Lyon (medicine, 60000 concepts), l’Institut des Sciences de l’Homme (part of Rameau vocabulary)…

Ses fonctionnalités actuelles :
- Gestion avancée des termes et des branches
- Drag and Drop
- Gestion collaborative avec 4 niveaux d'authentification (Superadmin, Admin, User et Traducteur)
- Interopérable : génération automatique d'identifiants Handle et ARK (ce service est assuré par le PSIR de la MOM)
- WebServices REST
- import : SKOS, Turtle, JsonLD
- export : SKOS, Turtle, JsonLD, CSV et PDF



OpenTheso is released under the terms of the CeCILL_C license, fully compatible with the GNU GPL.

composedOf.label: Créer un nouveau  « Candidat »
composedOf.description:
La fiche « Candidat » comprend plusieurs champs issus principalement du standard SKOS, Simple Knowledge Organisation System (https://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/). 

1. Renseigner dans un premier temps les deux champs obligatoires qui apparaissent (voir image 1).

Ils obéissent à des règles d’écriture précises : 

a. Intitulé (skos:prefLabel@fr) : il représente le libellé préférentiel donné au concept. C’est un substantif (mot simple ou mot composé) écrit en français, langue par défaut du thésaurus, et au singulier dans cette langue sauf usage particulier. Le libellé n’est ni un verbe ni un adjectif. Ceux-ci peuvent être substantivés pour répondre aux règles d’écriture. 
Ex. : brillance plutôt que briller ou brillant.

Le mot commence par une lettre minuscule, sauf s’il s'agit d’une entité nommée (nom de personnage, de lieu, d'œuvre, etc.).
Ex. : catacombes ; épigraphie ; arsenal naval ; grotte de Lascaux ; Les Troyennes (Sénèque).

Le libellé doit être explicite, au besoin en conservant la langue d’origine s’il n’y a pas d’équivalent en français (ou dans une autre des langues du thésaurus).
Ex. : dolium (dans toutes les langues du thésaurus).

Pour éviter toute ambiguïté, il est possible d’ajouter entre parenthèses une précision.
Ex. : Dialogues (Tacite).

b. Définition (skos:definition) : explicitation du concept en une phrase commençant par un substantif avec initiale en majuscule et qui reprend idéalement la position du concept dans l’arbre. La définition ne contient ni le terme défini ni aucun exemple et n’est pas une notice d’information. Elle est une aide pour sélectionner le mot-clé le plus juste dans l’indexation d’une ressource.
Voir les recommandations sur https://hal.inrae.fr/hal-03153824v1/document. 

La source de la définition peut être signalée entre parenthèses à la fin du texte. Elle sera de préférence issue de dictionnaires ou de publications imprimées ou numériques faisant foi.
Ex. : bouilloire (TG récipient culinaire) : Pot verseur utilisé pour chauffer de l'eau (Balfet et al. 1989, p. 19).

2. Valider la demande de création du candidat.

relatedItems.label: Controlled Vocabularies and SKOS training at DARIAH Campus
relatedItems.description: Training module about controlled vocabularies and SKOS. Presentation of how controlled vocabularies can be used for organizing and classifying data and how the resources can be queried, retrieved, analysed and linked to other relevant information objects.

composedOf.label: Enrichir le candidat avec des relations internes
composedOf.description:
A ce stade, il est toujours possible de corriger l’intitulé (modifier directement dans le champ) et la définition (utiliser le bouton « Modifier »).

Des métadonnées complémentaires apparaissent. Certaines sont fortement recommandées et sont signalées par un *. Si vous ne savez pas répondre, laissez le champ libre, il sera complété par les administrateurs.

A l’exception de l’intitulé que seul le demandeur peut corriger, les métadonnées sont modifiables par tous les gestionnaires du thésaurus. 

Les métadonnées susceptibles d’être enrichies sont les suivantes : 

- Ajouter à la collection (skos:Collection) : une collection est un groupement de concepts sur une thématique donnée. Dans Pactols, les collections reprennent les termes de tête de l’organisation hiérarchique. Elles servent notamment de filtres pour le requêtage par l’API de Opentheso.

- *Termes génériques (TG) (skos:broaderTerm) : il s’agit du libellé du concept parent qui positionnera le nouveau mot-clé dans l’arbre. Bien que la polyhiérarchie soit techniquement possible, Pactols a fait le choix d’en limiter strictement l’usage. Il est donc préférable de proposer un seul terme générique. 

- Employé pour (EP) (skos:altLabel) : il s’agit des termes rejetés ou des variantes de forme et de sens du concept. On donnera ici, si besoin, les formes latine ou grecque, les abréviations et les sigles. Il n’y a pas de limitation numérique aux variantes. Elles sont incluses dans l’index de recherche et renvoient au concept tout comme son libellé.

- Termes associés (TA) (skos:narrow) : tout autre concept déjà présent dans le thésaurus qui a un rapport avec le candidat. La relation d’association étant réciproque, un lien créé entre un concept A et un concept B est automatiquement créé entre le concept B et le concept A.
Ex : Iliade TA Homère ; tatouage TA peau ; vin TA amphore, viticulture.

composedOf.label: Enrichir le candidat avec des notes et des traductions
composedOf.description:
Notes dont *Définition et aussi Note d’application (skos:scopeNote) : il s’agit de préciser des limitations possibles ou exigées dans l’utilisation du concept (voir image 2).

 Le choix du type de Note se fait par sélection (voir image 3).

*Ajouter une traduction : l’intitulé du concept ne s’écrit qu’en français dans le module Candidat. Pactols étant multilingue, il est recommandé de le traduire ici, dans les langues de Pactols : allemand, anglais, arabe, espagnol, italien, néerlandais. Sélectionnez la langue de la traduction. Le choix des langues disponibles pour la traduction se réduit au fur et à mesure que les possibilités sont utilisées. 
NB : Il n’est pas possible à ce stade d’ajouter des variantes dans les langues traduites. Si vous en connaissez, inscrivez-les dans la zone des commentaires, elles seront ajoutées par les gestionnaires après la validation du candidat.
La recherche de traductions justes étant complexe et délicate, vous êtes invités à compléter au maximum les traductions du libellé. Pour vous aider : 
les publications scientifiques, recours essentiel ;
puis les dictionnaires spécialisés ;
L’utilisation des traductions des items de Wikidata ou des traducteurs en ligne (comme DeepL ou GoogleTrad) doit être absolument contrôlée par une interrogation d’Internet à partir de la traduction suggérée, en particulier à l'aide de Google image et Google books. Les résultats confirmeront ou pas la validité du choix ou le risque d’un faux-ami.

relatedItems.label: Google Books
relatedItems.description: Google Books provides full, free PDF scans (and web-viewable versions) of public domain books and magazines, free previews of some books and magazines under copyright, and the option to purchase digital editions of available items to save and read on Google Play, their e-reading platform. You can also find a local library based on your zip code that has the item available. Reader reviews of the items are available and you can contribute your own. Search for authors, titles, as well as keywords and Google will return results with matches in the title/text of the item. There are permalinks to available pages. Highly useful for finding items that contain your keywords in its text.

composedOf.label: Enrichir le candidat avec des alignements et des images
composedOf.description:
Ajouter un alignement : il s’agit de créer une relation d’équivalence plus ou moins exacte entre le mot-clé Pactols et un item correspondant dans un autre référentiel du web. Pactols a fait le choix de préférer les relations exactes (skos:exactMatch). Les alignements ne sont possibles qu’avec des référentiels fournissant un identifiant pérenne à ses items (DOI, ARK,...) ou une adresse web stable (URI).

Les principaux référentiels des alignements Pactols sont : Wikidata, les thésaurus du ministère français de la Culture (http://data.culture.fr/thesaurus/), IdRef (oeuvres, personnes), le Art and Architecture Thesaurus de la Fondation Getty, Bibracte_thesaurus, Bnf, Pleiades (lieux anciens), Geonames (lieux), Insee (lieux de France). 

Deux modes d’alignement sont possibles : 
1. alignement : faites une recherche préalable dans le réservoir puis donnez l’URI distante de l’item et le nom du référentiel dans le formulaire.
Ex. URI distante : https://www.wikidata.org/wiki/Q6934696
      Nom de la source : Wikidata
2. alignement automatique : Opentheso opère une recherche sur le libellé dans les référentiels pré-enregistrés : Bibracte_thesaurus, Bnf, GeoNames, Wikidata. Selon le réservoir, la réponse peut être faussement négative sur le libellé en français, par exemple avec Wikidata dont les items peuvent ne pas avoir d’équivalent dans la langue de la recherche. Écrivez de préférence le terme de la requête dans la langue du référentiel visé. Sélectionnez la meilleure réponse affichée. La possibilité de rapatrier des métadonnées supplémentaires (traductions, images, définition) peut être un avantage mais nécessitera une relecture voire une correction après alignement. 

Image : Certains concepts, difficiles à définir, peuvent être illustrés avec profit d’une ou de plusieurs images. Celles-ci doivent être représentatives du concept et se positionner autant que possible dans le champ de l’archéologie sinon de l’histoire ancienne. Elles doivent impérativement être libres de droit (sélectionnez les réservoirs ad hoc, notamment Wikimedia Commons, et citables (avec une URI comme adresse web stable, un PID identifiant pérenne de type ARK, DOI, etc.).

Pour ajouter une image depuis Wikimedia Commons : sélectionnez l'image choisie, cliquez sur l'onglet "use this file" et recopiez le champ "File URL:". Remplissez les 4 champs de l'onglet Image de Pactols : l'URI, la légende de l'image (libellé), son auteur et la source. 
Ex. pour amphore attique : URI : https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/0/01/Amphore_attique_%C3%A0_figures_noires._Peintre_de_Rycroft_-_btv1b101044967_%282_of_2%29.jpg ; libellé : Amphore attique à figures noires. Peintre de Rycroft ; auteur : Bibliothèque nationale de France ; source : Wikimédia.

relatedItems.label: Pleiades dataset
relatedItems.description: Pleiades gives scholars, students, and enthusiasts worldwide the ability to use, create, and share historical geographic information about the ancient world in digital form. At present, Pleiades has extensive coverage for the Greek and Roman world, and is expanding into Ancient Near Eastern, Byzantine, Celtic, and Early Medieval geography. JSON-formatted data is the site's "only comprehensive data dump." It contains all attributes of all place, name, and location objects in the database that have been published. Each morning, a single JSON file for all published places is written to a JSON file at http://atlantides.org/downloads/pleiades/json/. JSON is a widely used, well-known format that is popular for use in web applications and other programming tasks. We keep a week's worth of files, deleting older ones. The file named pleiades-places-latest.json.gz will always get you the most recent version. Note also that those previously published place resources that have been withdrawn and moved to the "errata" section of the site are dumped to a separate json file.

relatedItems.label: Entity Matching Tool
relatedItems.description: The EHRI Entity Matching Tool is an online utility for translating a list of textual references into a table of data from controlled vocabulary items, using fuzzy matching where appropriate. For example, if you have a list place names you want to put on a map, the tool will search the [Geonames](https://www.geonames.org) database for each reference, present the most appropriate options, and allow you to copy the result as CSV containing the Geonames IDs, latitude and longitude in a tabular format that can be imported into a spreadsheet or other system.While places were the original use-case, the tool also supports other entities in the [EHRI portal](https://portal.ehri-project.eu) database.

relatedItems.label: Getty Thesaurus of Geographic Names
relatedItems.description: The Getty Thesaurus of Geographic Names ® (TGN), The Art \& Architecture Thesaurus ® (AAT), the Union List of Artist Names ® (ULAN), the Cultural Objects Name Authority ® (CONA), and the Iconography Authority (IA) are structured resources that can be used to improve access to information about art, architecture, and material culture. Through rich metadata and links, it is hoped that the Getty vocabularies will provide a powerful conduit for research and discovery for digital art history and related disciplines.

relatedItems.label: Ancient Place-Name Extractor for Turkish Excavation Reports
relatedItems.description: This open‑source toolkit automatically extracts ancient place‑names from the annual proceedings of [“Kazı Sonuçları Toplantısı”](https://ukaas.ktb.gov.tr/TR-389973/kazi-sonuclari-toplantisi.html) that are the excavation reports published as PDFs on the Turkish Ministry of Culture website. It uses the Pleiades gazetteer (filtered to modern‐Turkey coordinates), page‑by‑page text extraction (with a PyPDF2→PyMuPDF fallback), and Turkish lemmatization via Zemberek.  The final output is a single JSON file listing every detected place‑name along with its Pleiades ID, coordinates, source PDF, page number, and surrounding snippet.

relatedItems.label: GeoNames Excel Mapper (GEM)
relatedItems.description: This Python script is a functional batch geocoding tool designed to efficiently find geographic coordinates for a large number of locations. It reads place names directly from a specified column in a Microsoft Excel file, queries the GeoNames API to fetch their latitude and longitude, and writes the enriched data (name, country, coordinates, and a direct link) for each location to a new Excel file. The tool handles ambiguous place names by allowing the user to configure the maximum number of results. It eliminates the need for manual searchs.

relatedItems.label: VIAF: The Virtual International Authority File
relatedItems.description: The VIAF (Virtual International Authority File) service provides libraries and library users with convenient access to the world's major name authority files. VIAF Contributors regularly supply authority data that VIAF matches, links, and groups. All descriptions for a given entity are merged into a cluster that brings together the different names for that entity. This service allows researchers to identify names, locations, works, and expressions while preserving regional preferences for language, spelling, and script.

relatedItems.label: GeoNames
relatedItems.description:
A global geographical database that may be used to identify and tag all references to location. The database contains over 8 million entries, each of which possesses a geographic name (in various languages), latitude, longitude, elevation, population, administrative subdivision and postal codes and information on unique features.

Features:

Built upon web service, enabling transparent look-up and use of content through third-party tools and sites

Browse by geographic location, country name, size of geographic region and other categories.

Full text search support





Extensible, enabling users to expand existing information or contribute new content

Support for the World Geodetic System 1984 (WGS84) co-ordinate system

relatedItems.label: Gallica
relatedItems.description:
Gallica is the online library of the Bibliothèque nationale de France and its partners. Online since 1997, thousands of new documents each week and offers access to many millions of digitized documents. Gallica is one of the major digital libraries available for free via the Internet. It provides access to any type of document: printed documents (books, press and magazines) in image and text mode, manuscripts, sound and iconographic documents, maps and plans.

Most of Gallica's collections have been converted into text format using optical character recognition (OCR-processing), which allows full-text search in the library materials. Users can access high quality zoom via IIIF. 

Each document has a digital identifier, the so-called ARK (Archival Resource Key) of the National Library of France and is accompanied by a bibliographic description. 

Gallica is intended to all readers, whether users just having a look, booklovers, students or academics.

relatedItems.label: GETTY Art & Architecture Thesaurus (AAT)
relatedItems.description: The Getty Thesaurus of Geographic Names ® (TGN), The Art & Architecture Thesaurus ® (AAT), the Union List of Artist Names ® (ULAN), the Cultural Objects Name Authority ® (CONA), and the Iconography Authority (IA) are structured resources that can be used to improve access to information about art, architecture, and material culture. Through rich metadata and links, it is hoped that the Getty vocabularies will provide a powerful conduit for research and discovery for digital art history and related disciplines.

relatedItems.label: Pleiades: A community-built gazetteer and graph of ancient places
relatedItems.description: Pleiades gives scholars, students, and enthusiasts worldwide the ability to use, create, and share historical geographic information about the ancient world in digital form.

relatedItems.label: Bibracte_Thesaurus
relatedItems.description:
Bibracte_Thesaurus is a specialised thesaurus developed for the archaeological research and documentation of Bibracte. It provides a structured vocabulary reflecting the terminology used by the scientific partners involved in research at the site, covering areas such as archaeological excavation and prospection, artefacts, chronology, research methods, conservation-restoration and dissemination. Managed through Opentheso, it supports the standardised description, organisation and interoperability of archaeological data.

FR:

Bibracte_Thesaurus est un thésaurus spécialisé développé pour la recherche et la documentation archéologiques de Bibracte. Il propose un vocabulaire structuré reflétant la terminologie utilisée par les partenaires scientifiques impliqués dans les recherches sur le site, couvrant notamment la prospection et la fouille archéologiques, les artefacts, la chronologie, les méthodes de recherche, la conservation-restauration et la valorisation. Géré avec Opentheso, il favorise la description et l'organisation normalisées des données archéologiques ainsi que leur interopérabilité.

relatedItems.label: Wikimedia Commons
relatedItems.description:
Wikimedia Commons is a free, multilingual media repository that provides access to a large collection of freely licensed and public-domain images, audio, video and other multimedia files. The repository includes structured metadata describing media files, their creators, subjects, locations and other entities. It supports the discovery, reuse and linking of digital cultural heritage resources across Wikimedia projects and other platforms.

FR:

Wikimedia Commons est une médiathèque libre et multilingue qui donne accès à une vaste collection d’images, de fichiers audio, de vidéos et d’autres contenus multimédias sous licence libre ou dans le domaine public. Le dépôt fournit des métadonnées structurées décrivant les fichiers, leurs créateurs, leurs sujets, leurs lieux et d’autres entités. Il facilite la découverte, la réutilisation et la mise en relation de ressources numériques, notamment dans le domaine du patrimoine culturel.

relatedItems.label: IdRef
relatedItems.description:
IdRef is a controlled vocabulary and authority reference system for describing and identifying people, places, organisations, conferences, and other entities in France. It supports consistent metadata creation, entity disambiguation, and interoperability across bibliographic, research, and cultural heritage information systems.

FR:

IdRef est un vocabulaire contrôlé et un référentiel d’autorité permettant de décrire et d’identifier des personnes, des lieux, des organisations, des conférences et d’autres entités en France. Il favorise la production de métadonnées cohérentes, la désambiguïsation des entités et l’interopérabilité entre les systèmes d’information bibliographiques, scientifiques et patrimoniaux.

relatedItems.label: Les vocabulaires du Ministère de la Culture
relatedItems.description:
The Vocabularies of the French Ministry of Culture are a set of controlled vocabularies, thesauri, authority lists, classifications and other scientific and technical reference resources developed or coordinated by the French Ministry of Culture. They are designed to support the standardised description, indexing and management of cultural heritage data.

These vocabularies provide a common terminology for describing cultural heritage objects, works, architectural elements, materials, techniques, periods, iconography and other relevant concepts. Their use helps to harmonise metadata, improve the consistency and quality of data, facilitate information retrieval, and enable interoperability between different cultural heritage databases and institutions.

FR: 

Les Vocabulaires du ministère de la Culture constituent un ensemble de référentiels scientifiques et techniques destinés à faciliter la description, l’indexation et la recherche des ressources et collections patrimoniales. Ils regroupent notamment des thésaurus, listes d’autorité, nomenclatures et autres vocabulaires contrôlés, élaborés par le ministère de la Culture et ses partenaires. Leur utilisation permet d’employer un langage commun et normalisé pour décrire les objets, les œuvres, les lieux, les techniques, les matériaux, les périodes ou encore les acteurs du patrimoine.

Ces vocabulaires jouent ainsi un rôle important dans l’harmonisation et l’interopérabilité des données patrimoniales : ils facilitent la cohérence de l’indexation, améliorent les possibilités de recherche et permettent de rapprocher des données provenant de différentes institutions ou bases documentaires. Certains sont notamment utilisés pour l’alimentation et l’interrogation de bases nationales telles que Joconde et sont diffusés dans des formats permettant leur réutilisation et leur intégration dans des environnements numériques.

relatedItems.label: INSEE – Official Geographical Code (Code officiel géographique, COG)
relatedItems.description:
The INSEE Geographical Nomenclature (Code officiel géographique, COG) is an official reference resource providing standardised names and identifiers for geographical and administrative entities in France, including municipalities. It supports the consistent identification and description of places, geographical referencing, and interoperability of data across information systems.
Français

FR: 

La nomenclature géographique de l’INSEE (Code officiel géographique, COG) est une ressource de référence officielle fournissant des noms et des identifiants normalisés pour les entités géographiques et administratives en France, notamment les communes. Elle permet l’identification et la description cohérentes des lieux, le référencement géographique et l’interopérabilité des données entre différents systèmes d’information.

relatedItems.label: Tutoriel alignement de vocabulaire : GeoNames
relatedItems.description:
Ce tutoriel a pour objectif d’expliquer comment effectuer un alignement de vocabulaire vers le référentiel de données géographiques GeoNames, à l’aide du logiciel libre OpenRefine. Le but de cet alignement est de relier un jeu de données archéologiques contenant des lieux (généralement des sites) à leur localisation et référentiel GeoNames afin de pouvoir utiliser le web sémantique et en particulier l’outil OpenArchaeo. Ce document est établi à l’aide des données provenant du fond “Jean Perrot. Du village à l’État au Proche- et Moyen-Orient” conservé à la MSH Mondes et d’un export de la base “Cruches gallo-romaines” depuis la plateforme de SIG en ligne ArkeoGIS.

French language tutorial from Consortium-HN MASA detailing how to align a vocabulary with GeoNames using OpenRefine.

relatedItems.label: Tutoriel alignement de vocabulaire : Getty AAT
relatedItems.description:
Ce tutoriel a pour objectif d’expliquer comment effectuer un alignement de vocabulaire vers le référentiel Art & Architecture Thesaurus créé par le Getty Research Institute, à l’aide du logiciel  libre OpenRefine. Le but de cet alignement est de créer un document d’équivalences permettant ensuite l’appareillement des données concernées avec la plateforme ARIADNEplus. Il ne s’applique que pour des jeux de données déjà alignés avec le référentiel PACTOLS de Frantiq2. Ce document est établi à l’aide des données provenant de la base Atlas des établissements ruraux de la Beauce antique (AERBA) qui se présente au format xml.

French language tutorial on aligning vocabulary with Getty AAT using OpenRefine, produced by the Consortium-HN MASA Plus.

relatedItems.label: Tutoriel alignement de vocabulaire : VIAF
relatedItems.description:
Ce tutoriel a pour objectif d’expliquer comment effectuer un alignement de vocabulaire vers le référentiel VIAF(Virtual International Authority File), à l’aide du logiciel libre OpenRefine. Le but de cet alignement est de relier un jeu de données archéologiques contenant des acteurs au VIAF afin de pouvoir utiliser le web sémantique et en particulier l’outil OpenArchaeo. Ce document  est établi à l’aide des données provenant de la base RITA qui se présente au format csv.

French language tutorial on aligning vocabulary with VIAF using OpenRefine, produced by the Consortium-HN MASA Plus.

composedOf.label: Échanger (si besoin) avec les gestionnaires du thésaurus
composedOf.description:
Chaque semaine, les gestionnaires du thésaurus Pactols examinent les candidats proposés. Ils évaluent chaque demande dans leur fond et dans leur forme. Le critère principal pour une validation est la pertinence du concept vis-à-vis de la thématique du thésaurus. La qualité des métadonnées, notamment une définition non conforme aux règles et l'absence de traduction surtout pour des mots-clés de spécialité, pourra amener les gestionnaires à vous demander des compléments d'information préalablement à une prise de décision.

En tant que demandeur, vous recevrez une notification à chaque intervention sur le candidat proposé (la fonction de notification doit être activée dans votre compte). Vous êtes invité à répondre dans le bloc de discussion. 

Cette étape est itérative tant que les éléments nécessaires à la prise de décision ne sont pas rassemblés.

composedOf.label: Répondre à la proposition d’ajout
composedOf.description:
En fin de parcours, après avoir examiné la proposition, en avoir débattu et éventuellement corrigé ou complété certaines métadonnées, les gestionnaires décident de refuser ou de valider l’ajout du nouveau candidat.

Si la proposition est refusée, elle est stockée dans les “Concepts refusés”. Le terme reste inscrit dans l’index de Pactols. Sa demande de création peut être réactivée et le candidat peut alors suivre un nouvel examen.

Si la proposition est acceptée, le candidat est inscrit dans la liste des « Concepts insérés » et vient se positionner dans l’arbre. Le nouveau mot-clé est alors disponible pour l’indexation.

Dans tous les cas, en tant que demandeur, vous êtes informé par mail (notification avec un possible message personnalisé) de la décision des gestionnaires.

label: PyMotifs: a workflow designed to detect significant lexico-grammatical patterns for automatic stylistic analysis in French
description:
This project, lead by Antoine Silvestre de Sacy and Dominique Legallois (CNRS, Université Paris III - Sorbonne-Nouvelle), was supported by the European infrastructure DARIAH via a bi-annual thematic funding call on the theme of Workflows.

**The aim of the workflow PyMotifs is to model French texts in the form of lexico-grammatical patterns, also known as "motifs".** For a long time, the objectives of stylometry were authorship verification, or the dating of texts, the similarity (generally lexical) between several texts. From now on, with the development of the possibilities offered by computer science, and the advent of corpus linguistics or Digital Humanities, more qualitative analyses (based on quantitative results) are no longer only envisaged, but actually carried out in order to characterize the properties of a text (or of a textual genre, or the textual production of an author). A corpus stylistics can thus be developed: it retains the rigor and the degree of precision of traditional stylistics, while relying on large quantified data.

PyMotifs is situated at the frontier of stylometric and stylistic questions and is intended to be used by both disciplines: as a complement to stylometry, whose orientations are essentially quantitative, seeking to answer questions such as: what are the subjects addressed by a given text? By whom was it written? When was it written? But also as a complement to stylistics, whose orientations are essentially qualitative, focusing on particular and specific facts of language: is this form significant for this author or this text? How can we interpret this form as a style of this author, text, genre or corpus?
Contrary to many approaches in digital humanities and in big data which stick to distant reading, but also in contrast to stylistics which sticks to singular facts of language, PyMotifs proposes a mixed method, relying on statistical methods but nevertheless enabling a systematic return to the texts to interpret the results. PyMotifs thus allows for both inductive approaches (data-driven and bottom-up approaches) and deductive approaches (top-down, qualitative stylistics).

All functionalities have been coded in such a way as to be usable by non-computer users with some notion of programming. Each module is presented in the form of a documented Jupyter notebook, enabling the corpus to be labeled in the form of patterns and a series of functions to be used to analyze and compare texts. More advanced machine learning functionalities integrating the scikit-learn framework have also been developed.

relatedItems.label: UDPipe: tool for lemmatization, morphological analysis, POS tagging and dependency parsing in multiple languages
relatedItems.description: UDPipe is a software tool and service that analyzes (plain) text in about 100 different natural languages up to the dependency syntax level. Users specify the desired function (tokenization, segmentation, morphological analysis, lemmatization, POS tagging, dependency parsing), output format, and input text (file(s)). The resulting analysis can be used to index and search documents by lemmas instead of multiple word forms, extract syntactic dependencies with POS information to get relations between words or lemmas, or get grammatical information for every word in the text. While in many cases the results can be used directly (statistical analysis on part of speech, lemmas and words), in many other applications the results of UDPipe serve as intermediate input to more sophisticated analysis, such as information extraction, knowledge representation, term extraction etc. UDPipe software allow to train on any language for which a treebank is available in the CoNLL-U format, such as all the Universal Dependencies corpora.

composedOf.label: Installation
composedOf.description:
### Create a virtual environment

With conda: `conda create -n pymotifs python=3.11`

### To use the last stable version of the package

- Clone the `main` branch.
- Activate your environment: `conda activate pymotifs`.
- Install with `pip install .` at the source

### Install development branch

- Install with `pip install ."[dev]"` at the source
- Install pre-commit hooks with `pre-commit install`
- Start to code

### Notebooks

You must install the package in your ipython kernel. For example, you can
create a new kernel corresponding to your environement with: `install
ipython kernel install --name "pymotifs" --user`

### Notes

- Careful about **scipy** and **joblib** versions. There are issues with
  joblib when performing tasks in multiprocessing. The package was tested
  with **joblib==1.3.2** and **scipy==1.11.4**.

composedOf.label: Text preprocessing
composedOf.description:
The [first notebook](https://github.com/Malichot/PyMotifs/blob/main/notebooks/0_Pipeline_Motifs.ipynb) shows how to use the Motif Pipeline. The Motif pipeline transforms a corpus to motif-based features, or other UDPipe tokens, such as POS, lemma, etc. It consists of 4 steps:

- UDPipe tokenization of the corpus.
- Tokens preprocessing with n-gram transformation.
- n-grams featurization, for example: TFIDF or TF.
- Visualization, for example: PCA analysis, distributional plots, specificity analysis.

Then, you can return to the texts at different scales :

- Corpus level.
- Document level.
- Motif level.

composedOf.label: Document prediction based on motifs
composedOf.description:
## Description

The [second notebook](https://github.com/Malichot/PyMotifs/blob/main/notebooks/1_Predict_doc.ipynb) aims at finding the defining motifs of a work within the same corpus. It uses a linear classification technique in order to select the most relevant motifs to predict a document inside a corpus. 

## Pre-selection of features

Since we know that a token which as a tf-idf of 0 corresponds to non-informative tokens, we propose a simple solution based on the sparsity of feature: the more sparse the token is in the corpus, the less informative it is, since it is more common to all documents. Then, we simply select the  less sparse features.

## Estimation

To fit the model, we simply minimize the Mean Squarred Error as in a classical multinomial logistic regression framework. However, in order to select the most important motifs, we apply the L1 regularization which forces non-informative features to have a 0 coefficient.

## Evaluation

To evaluate the model, we split the data in train/test samples where the observations in the test sample come from documents that are not in the train sample. Finally, we use the accuracy metric on the test set.

composedOf.label: Canonical label prediction based on motifs
composedOf.description:
## Description

The [third notebook](https://github.com/Malichot/PyMotifs/blob/main/notebooks/2_Predict_Canon.ipynb) aims at explaining the canonical label of a work by the motifs within a corpus.

## Methodology

We use a linear classification technique in order to find the motifs that explain the canonical aspect of a writing independently from the author, gender and publication date, focusing only on linguistic features of the writing.

## Pre-selection of features

In this notebook, we introduce a criterion for feature selection before estimating the parameters. Since we know that a token which as a tfidf of 0 corresponds to non-informative tokens, we propose a simple solution solution based on the sparsity of feature . We define the sparsity level as the proportion of 0 in a vector. The more sparse the token is in the corpus, the less informative it is, since it is more common to all documents. Then, we simply select the  less sparse features.

## Estimation

We apply the pipeline in order to obtain the motif annotations (or any other token). Then, we compute  the TFIDF scores of each motif within each document in the corpus, where a document represents a window of motifs, as stated above.

To fit the model, we simply minimize the Mean Squarred Error as in a classical logistic regression framework. However, in order to select the most important motifs, we apply the L1 regularization which forces non-informative features to have a 0 coefficient.

## Evaluation

To evaluate the model, we split the data in train/test samples where the observations in the test sample come from documents that are not in the train sample. We keep the class distributions in the train and test equal a Finally, we use the accuracy metric on the test set (as classes are balanced).

composedOf.label: Corpus clustering based on motifs features
composedOf.description:
## Description

The goal of the [fourth notebook](https://github.com/Malichot/PyMotifs/blob/main/notebooks/3_Clustering.ipynb) is to find natural and interpretable clusters in a corpus based on motifs.

## Methodology

Our feature space is very large (more than 200K) and on top TFIDF features are not Gaussian. Thus, we can expect KMeans to perform very badly on the raw table. We thus propose to use a manifold learning teaching, TSNE, to reduce the dimension of the feature spaces. TSNE helps use to visualize potential clusters in the dataset. We then apply a clustering algorithm, DBSCAN, to find the cluster in the embedding space.

label: Raman spectrometry for the analysis and          identification of pigments on cultural heritage objects
description: Raman spectrometry is a widely used technique for examining various types of cultural heritage objects, with significant contributions in studies concentrating on pigment identification. The Raman effect provides a quick and relatively straightforward molecular identification of a material under examination due to the fact that the Raman spectrum can be considered as a fingerprint that is used for compound identification. The method is considered significantly versatile therefore different types of equipment are commercially available such as bench top and laboratory instruments, probes/portable and handheld instruments. These advantages including the simplicity, accuracy and speed of the analysis has made Raman spectroscopy very successful in the field of cultural heritage. The current scenario presents a methodology for Raman analysis directly on cultural heritage object (no sampling).

It also describes some common approaches to avoid interferences and side-effects such as absorption, fluorescence, thermal effects, photodecomposition, and laser ablation. The selection of an appropriate laser wavelength may be crucial to avoid such interferences. Apart from interferences caused by interaction of the laser light with the sample, background radiation or ambient light may interfere with the measurements.

relatedItems.label: Raman spectroscopy as a means for the identification of plattnerite (PbO2), of lead pigments and of their degradation products
relatedItems.description: The Raman spectra of plattnerite \[lead(IV) oxide, PbO2\] and of the lead pigments red lead (Pb3O4), lead monoxide \[PbO, litharge (tetragonal) and massicot (orthorhombic)\], lead white \[basic lead carbonate, 2PbCO3·Pb(OH)2\] and of their laser-induced degradation products were recorded using a range of different excitation lines, spectrometer systems and experimental conditions. The degradation of PbO2 is more extensive along the pathway PbO2 → Pb3O4 → PbO (litharge) → PbO (massicot) the shorter the wavelength of the excitation line and the higher its power. The Raman spectrum of PbO2, which is black and of the rutile structure, is particularly difficult to obtain but three bands, at 653, 515 and 424 cm−1, were identified as arising from the b2g, a1g and eg modes respectively, by analogy with the corresponding modes of isostructural SnO2 (776, 634 and 475 cm−1). A further oxide was identified, PbO1.55, the Raman spectrum of which does not correspond to that of any of the laser-induced degradation products of PbO2 at any of the wavelengths used. The Raman results are critical to the future use of Raman microscopy for the identification of lead pigments on artworks.

relatedItems.label: Mitigation strategies for radiation damage in the analysis of ancient materials
relatedItems.description: The study of materials in cultural heritage artifacts and micro-samples benefits from diagnostic techniques based on intense radiation sources, such as synchrotrons, ion-beam accelerators and lasers. While most of the corresponding techniques are classified as non-destructive, investigation with photons or charged particles entails a number of fundamental processes that may induce changes in materials. These changes depend on irradiation parameters, properties of materials and environmental factors. In some cases, radiation-induced damage may be detected by visual inspection. When it is not, irradiation may still lead to atomic and molecular changes resulting in immediate or delayed alteration and bias of future analyses. Here we review the effects of radiation reported on a variety of cultural heritage materials and describe the usual practice for assessing short-term and long-term effects. This review aims to raise awareness and encourage subsequent research activities to limit radiation side effects.

concept.label: ASCII
concept.definition: ASCII abbreviated from American Standard Code for Information Interchange, is a character encoding standard for electronic communication. ASCII codes represent text in computers, telecommunications equipment, and other devices. Most modern character-encoding schemes are based on ASCII, although they support many additional characters. ASCII is the traditional name for the encoding system.

concept.label: CSV
concept.definition: A comma-separated values (CSV) file is a delimited text file that uses a comma to separate values. A CSV file stores tabular data (numbers and text) in plain text. Each line of the file is a data record. Each record consists of one or more fields, separated by commas. The use of the comma as a field separator is the source of the name for this file format. RFC 4180 formalized CSV. It defines the MIME type "text/csv", and CSV files that follow its rules should be very widely portable

concept.label: JCAMP-DX
concept.definition: CAMP-DX is a standard file form for exchange of infrared spectra and related chemical and physical information between spectrometer data systems of different manufacture, main-frame time-sharing systems, general purpose lab computers, and personal computers. It is compatible with all media: telephone, magnetic and optical disk, magnetic tape, and even the printed page (via optical reader). All data are stored as labeled fields of variable length using printable ASCII characters. A JCAMP-DX spectrum is a text file which can be viewed, corrected, and annotated with a text editor. The present focus is on infrared spectra, but JCAMP-DX can easily accommodate Raman, UV, NMR, mass, and other types of spectra, x-ray powder patterns, chromatograms, thermograms, and other plots which require the capability of representing contours as well as peak position and intensity. JCAMP-DX also provides for combining adequate information about the sample and method of observation with its spectrum.

relatedItems.label: Fluorescence and Raman spectra on painting materials:reconstruction of spectra with mathematical methods
relatedItems.description: SERDS (shift excitation difference spectroscopy) and SSRS (subtracted shifted Raman spectroscopy) methods were applied for fluorescence-background rejection in the Raman spectra of colored materials. These techniques are based on the assumption that the fluorescence contribution can be completely eliminated by subtracting two Raman spectra acquired at two shifted laser excitation frequencies. For the SERDS method a micro-Raman experimental apparatus coupled with a tunable diode laser (central emission at 684 nm) was set up. SSRS measurements were made on a commercial micro-Raman instrument; in this case the shifted spectrum was obtained by moving the spectrometer grating. Raman spectra were then reconstructed by applying the difference deconvolution method that automatically converts the difference signals in Raman peaks through a deconvolution operation. These techniques were tested on two reference colors (ultramarine and 6,6′-dibromoindigotine) and two colored samples of unknown composition (a Pompeian pink powder and a blue paint from a XVII century painting). Fluorescence-background subtraction and the following operation of spectra reconstruction took place successfully with no errors in Raman peaks, width and wavenumber position. In addition, even weak spectral details were revealed favoring the comparison with reference data for a molecular identification

relatedItems.label: Subtracted shifted Raman spectroscopy of organic dyes and lakes
relatedItems.description: Resonance Raman spectroscopy has been utilized to identify vegetal and animal dyes and lakes. These compounds have been used by artists since antiquity, and their identification has important implications in art history and conservation. The resonance condition is useful when working with real ancient objects so as to enhance the Raman scattering of chromophores with respect to the strong signal of the matrix, such as the textile or parchment over which the colorant is supported. The strong fluorescence that generally characterizes the resonance Raman spectra was eliminated by using subtracted shifted Raman spectroscopy (SSRS). A systematic study on reference organic dyes was primarily carried out to evaluate the suitability of the method and to estimate the strengths and limitations of the spectrum reconstruction process. The method was then applied to the noninvasive identification of madder on ancient dyed silk textiles such as an altar table cloth and a manutergium attributed to the Egyptian artistic textile production of the 10th--11th Century A.D

It provides a convenient command line interface for solving linear and nonlinear problems numerically, and for performing other numerical experiments using a language that is mostly compatible with Matlab. It may also be used as a batch-oriented language. Octave has extensive tools for solving common numerical linear algebra problems, finding the roots of nonlinear equations, integrating ordinary functions, manipulating polynomials, and integrating ordinary differential and differential-algebraic equations. relatedItems.label: Analytical study of 20th century paint
relatedItems.description: About the project The introduction of synthetic organic pigments and binders mainly during the 20th century has caused a revolution within the art of painting. The choice of pigments has increased enormously and also polymeric binders -most notably acrylic, alkyd and polyvinyl acetate- have claimed their place in the artistic world. Even more than for traditional paintings, the knowledge of the constituents of modern materials is essential prior to any conservation treatment and to develop long-term preventive conservation strategies. Technical studies concerning the painting technique of modern paintings also require the identification of the materials used. Material identification can also provide information on the restoration history of an art object, or can be useful to answer questions regarding authenticity issues. label: Research Data Integration in Text+ (corpora and text collections)
description:
Text+ is a distributed infrastructure for text- and language-based research data. Its resources include contemporary and historical literary and media texts, deeply annotated material, transcriptions of spoken and signed language, as well as audio and video data. Text+ makes these resources accessible in accordance with the FAIR principles: findable thanks to standards-compliant metadata, accessible via single sign-on authentication, interoperable via open data formats, and reusable through web services and comprehensive documentation. The more than 30 partner institutions in Text+ include archives, libraries, universities and other research organisations. The partners operate autonomously and vary in terms of data volume and processing and provision capacities.

In this workflow, we describe the steps for users to contribute their research data to the Text+ infrastructure and make it available for reuse by other users via a centralised and FAIR-compliant access point.

For this purpose, research data published in another suitable repository will also be indexed in perspectivia.net. For sensitive and copyright-protected research data that is not suitable for publication, the metadata is published on perspectivia.net. DOI assignment and bibliographic references are provided regardless of this.

The services are primarily aimed at researchers within the worldwide MWS network, whether at the institutes or at the numerous partner institutions. In addition, the scientific advisory board of perspectivia.net decides on the inclusion of data from the Text+ community according to content and organisational criteria.

label: Research Sustainability Workflow for the Humanities
description:
This workflow was developed with the generous input of researchers, arts professionals, data stewards, cultural heritage practitioners and HSS repository managers across Ireland to help Humanities researchers think through the problem of designing and maintaining reusable datasets for long-term sustainability. Humanities data may include research materials collected from many different sources including: research notes, archival collections, interviews, websites, performances, design processes, etc.

We consider that sustainable research data are data which: 
- Have been created and shared as openly as possible in alignment with the [FAIR principles](https://www.go-fair.org/fair-principles/), 
- Demonstrate appreciable ongoing value for an audience, and
- Benefit from responsible stewardship, often managed through agreements with established organisations capable of ensuring the appropriate continuity of resources. 

Sustainability is complementary to shareability, and even preservability, in that it is not an end goal in and of itself. Things which are sustainable are those which are maintained, through effort, investment, and reuse. This workflow therefore considers functionality, audience engagement, stewardship, and environment in addition to more technical considerations such as open file formats and appropriate documentation. We anticipate that this workflow will be revisited during the research lifecycle as part of an iterative process. It should be used in combination with a data management plan (DMP) and other guidance on the preparation and documentation of FAIR (findable, accessible, interoperable, and reusable) research outputs.

composedOf.label: Set up a research project for sustainability
composedOf.description:
The question of how to sustain resources developed in the course of a research project is often left to the ‘evaluate and archive’ phase of a research lifecycle, which typically occurs after data collection, analysis, and collaboration, but before publication and dissemination of results. By deciding at the start of a project which outputs need effort to support their continued reuse you can increase your ability to effectively manage your resources and expectations.

We recommend utilising this research sustainability workflow in combination with a Data Management Plan (DMP). A DMP is a document created at the outset of your project, often as part of a funding proposal, which asks a series of questions about how you will gather, manage, store, and ultimately share, preserve, or dispose of data at the end of a project. When answering these questions, consider that some outputs may be most valuable in the short-term while others might need to be sustained through repositories, partnerships, or other collaborative agreements for much longer.

There are many resources and guides available to follow in setting up a DMP and your funder might have a specific template that they want you to use if preparing a plan to accompany a grant application. [DMPOnline](https://dmponline.dcc.ac.uk) provides templates and examples tailored to various funders in the EU and UK and their requirements. There are also example DMPs tailored to Humanities research at the [Digital Curation Centre](https://www.dcc.ac.uk/resources/data-management-plans/guidance-examples) and from the [DARIAH Working Group on Research Data Management](https://www.zotero.org/groups/2427138/data_management_best_practices_in_the_humanities/collections/3Q44QWAH).

We suggest also looking at already-published Humanities datasets available through resources such as the [Social Sciences and Humanities Open Marketplace](https://marketplace.sshopencloud.eu/search?categories=dataset) and the [Journal of Open Humanities Data](https://openhumanitiesdata.metajnl.com) to see examples of datasets and data papers which describe the creation, management, structure, and format of Humanities datasets. This will give you an idea of the kinds of data outputs that other researchers in your field have produced and shared.

composedOf.label: Document your sources
composedOf.description:
This step is concerned with mapping the provenance of the data and processes that will inform your outputs. As a Humanities researcher it is highly likely that your research draws on a variety of sources, historical or contemporary, which you intend to transform by refining, narrowing, or otherwise curating in preparation for analysis, interpretation, or display. Documenting the processes and decisions behind these transformations is a critical part of preparing your data to answer potential questions from future researchers.

Consider the following activities in this step:

1. Record the names of all contributors, both to your project directly or those found in original sources. Note contributor roles and any relevant personal or organisational identifiers (such as [ORCID](https://orcid.org/) or [ROR](https://ror.org) numbers), including students, volunteer labour, and in many cases, the subjects of research participating through shared personal experience and community knowledge. To acknowledge the rights of Indigenous communities in research that utilises Indigenous knowledge, culture, or lands, you may wish to use resources like [Traditional Knowledge (TK) labels](https://localcontexts.org/labels/traditional-knowledge-labels/). 

The [CRediT taxonomy](https://acsjournals.onlinelibrary.wiley.com/pb-assets/assets/10970142/Taxonomy-1548948207717.pdf) is a useful resource for describing a wide variety of contributor roles. It is okay if names are repeated if there are multiple roles. For example, a datasheet provided for the [Munster Women Writers Recovery Project](https://repository.dri.ie/catalog/hq388j03w) dataset in the Digital Repository of Ireland includes the following activities:
- Conceptualization | https://credit.niso.org/contributor-roles/conceptualization/: Joan Murphy
- Methodology | https://credit.niso.org/contributor-roles/methodology/: Joan Murphy
- Data Curation | https://credit.niso.org/contributor-roles/data-curation/: Joan Murphy

2. Consider how you will capture further contextual information, particularly around your research processes. There may be things you have not thought of sharing that could enhance the reusability of your resources (e.g. a data modelling decision you made, or a source that was not available). If reusing data from another person or organisation, make note of any existing licences that will need to be re-published alongside your own work. For more help, see the SSHOC Workshop on [Copyright Issues in Secondary Data Use](https://marketplace.sshopencloud.eu/training-material/bP4Txq).

3. Decide on a system of version control early on, especially if your project will involve collaboration with others. If Artificial Intelligence becomes a part of the workflow, plan ahead to record how and where it was used to make appropriate disclosure statements later if needed. A good overview of how a popular version control tool used by the software community can be applied to Humanities research was developed for The Programming Historian website, [An Introduction to Version Control Using Github Desktop](https://doi.org/10.46430/phen0051). The UK Data Service also has some helpful advice on [Organising Data](https://ukdataservice.ac.uk/learning-hub/research-data-management/format-your-data/organising/) for dissemination.

Simply recording the names of all contributors and collaborators is a powerful tool for inclusivity, accessibility, and equity in any data practice. Early career researchers, students, collaborating professionals in other fields and industries, cultural contributors or Indigenous communities may not receive credit for their intellectual labour through more traditional publishing pathways.
