relatedItems.label: RAD-on: Reports, Analysis and Data on Higher Education and Science in Poland
relatedItems.description:
The RAD-on system is a part of the Integrated Network of Information on Science and Higher Education, which is the biggest, in terms of the scope of collected data, public system in Poland supporting the Ministry of Education and Science and other state agencies in shaping the scientific policy.

The RAD-on system is intended to be used primarily by scientists, students, entrepreneurs, political decision-makers and journalists looking for reliable and up to date information on scientific institutions and on their research. The system offers the following services and functionalities:

Reports. Interactive reports on higher education institutions, students, graduates, academic staff, and research conducted in Poland and abroad. They can be used as one of the tools to create an evidence-based policy

Analyses. Reliable information on issues connected with science and higher education supplemented with extensive comments

Data. Knowledge base on scientific institutions, scientific and artistic activities, academic staff and promotion procedures may prove useful for anyone looking for up to date information and news from the science and higher education sector

User account. Users, whose data are stored in the RAD-on system and its source systems, can view, update and verify their data. To access your personal data, please log in using the login.gov.pl system.

API. RAD-on resources can be freely accessed through a dedicated uniform programming interface. This innovative feature allows users to build their own solutions and applications which require access to data on higher education

composedOf.label: Pose research questions
composedOf.description:
RAD-on’s primary objective is to provide reliable and up-to-date information on scientists, students, and institutions that operate in the science and higher education sectors in Poland. It means that it can serve as a data source for all kinds of research on science and higher education. 

Research questions may include subjects such as changes in the number of students, including PhD students, or degree progammes offered by higher education institutions. In relation to research productivity, an investigation into the numbers, but also into the metadata of research outputs may be performed. For example, in case of publications metadata about authors, title, abstract, journal, or publication year is available. Given the extensive scope of data available, an analysis of publications subjects using natural language processing methods is possible, as well as qualitative research on the societal impact of scientific projects in Poland.

composedOf.description:
The second step would be to identify a relevant dataset for your scientific inquiry. Below we list data sources with links to the system. 

##Institutions and their activities

composedOf.label: Gather data
composedOf.description:
The process of gathering data may be divided into two workflows, depending on the complexity of analysis planned by a researcher. 

##1. Basic use of data sources
The first workflow includes uploading of data in csv or excel format, which may be a preferable path for a researcher with no background in IT. 

You may investigate each data source at first by using filters section and a table preview on the RAD-on website. After narrowing down your dataset to a relevant scope, you may download it as excel, csv or pdf file (see pictures below). In order to download all data related to an item e.g. publication, scientist, or patent right, choose the "download all" option. If you are interested only in basic information from the main table choose "download records from the presented page". Beware that bigger datasets (e.g. about publications or scientists) need to be narrowed down before you will be able to download excell or csv file. For example, in order to analyse data about all scientists in Poland, it is advisable to use API tool (description of a procedure below). The alternative is to divide publications by year or type and download each dataset individually. 

##2. Advanced use of data sources (application programming interface, API)
The second workflow includes the use of [API](https://radon.nauka.gov.pl/api/katalog-udostepniania-danych) and might be more suitable for data scientists with basic programming skills. It may be preferable for research projects of an extended scope, e.g. changes in publication patterns over time. The API service has extended swagger documentation. Currently, RAD-on uses REST API and GUI APIs to share the standard categories of data that constitute the basis of RAD-on’s modules and services. Each category corresponds to one of the resources associated with higher education and science (e.g. institutions, publications, or acadamic staff), which means that the scope of data available via API mirrors the one in the [Data](https://radon.nauka.gov.pl/dane) section of the RAD-on system. Most of this data is modified frequently — scientific and higher education institutions change their names, new publications appear, and staff members change their jobs. By using API these changes in time may be tracked, which is not possible in the Data section.

media.caption: Data section of the RAD-on system. It contains datasets on various aspects of the science and higher education system in Poland. By clicking at the relevant dataset, you will be able to look through the data and perform its preliminary selection.
Filters sections may be used to narrow down datasets.
Each dataset from the Data section of RAD-on can be accessed also via API services.
Swagger documentation of API is available in Polish and English.

composedOf.label: Data check
composedOf.description:
The next step would be to check the data aggregation method. Datasets may not be tabulated in a way that provides direct answers to the research question. 

For example, in the case of the [academic staff dataset](https://radon.nauka.gov.pl/dane/nauczyciele-akademiccy-badacze-i-osoby-zaangazowane-w-dzialalnosc-naukowa), it is worth mentioning that each record includes information about academic degree obtained by a particular person. It means that there is more than one entry for each researcher, i.e. each row represents one of the career path stages: from bachelor through master or PhD education stage. In order to count the number of researchers in a particular field of study, grouping by ID attribute is preferable.

composedOf.label: Analyse data
composedOf.description:
The dataset may be further investigated using standard tools such as Python, R, spreadsheets, or specialised software like SPSS, Statistica, SAS. 

Examples of analysis can be found in the [“Analyses”](https://radon.nauka.gov.pl/analizy) section of the RAD-on system.

Elle permet de téléverser, structurer et archiver des matériaux artistiques et techniques liés à une œuvre, afin d’en garantir l’accès et la traçabilité à long terme.

Selon les types de fichiers (partition, enregistrements ou vidéo, patchs/fichiers informatique), s'assurer que le déposant a le droit (a) d'en faire le dépôt sur Antony, (b) d'en laisser l'accès au public en visualisation ou téléchargement.

composedOf.label: Create and store a local archive copy of the version on your own computer
composedOf.description:
Create a folder containing all the essential electronic files required to perform the work: the scores (including annotations), the technical sheet and stage setup diagrams, as well as audio and/or video recordings (low-resolution files or links to high-resolution files).

Include the programme booklet, programme notes, and any other relevant details concerning the performance.

Compress the folder containing all the documents into a ZIP file. In the medium term, the storage volume available per depositor will be limited.

French:

2. Fabriquer une archive de la version sur son propre ordinateur

Cette étape intervient après une représentation publique.

Créer un dossier contenant l’ensemble des fichiers électroniques essentiels à l’exécution de l’œuvre : les partitions (avec annotations), la fiche technique et les schémas d’implantation, ainsi que des captations audio et/ou vidéo (en basse résolution ou sous forme de liens vers des fichiers en haute résolution).

Y joindre le programme de salle, les notes d’intention, ainsi que tout autre élément pertinent concernant le spectacle.

Compresser l’ensemble du dossier au format ZIP. À moyen terme, le volume de stockage disponible par déposant sera limité.

composedOf.label: Create an account
composedOf.description:
Users must complete the registration form available at https://antony-archiv.org/register or click the “Register” button.

The form requires the following information: last name, first name, email address, and motivations.

Once submitted, the request is sent to the editorial committee responsible for administering and moderating the application. The applicant will then receive an email confirming the creation of their account.

French:

4. Créer un compte

Il convient de remplir le formulaire disponible à l’adresse https://antony-archiv.org/register ou en cliquant sur le bouton prévu à cet effet.

Les informations suivantes doivent être renseignées : nom, prénom, adresse e-mail et motivations.

Une fois le formulaire soumis, une notification est envoyée au comité éditorial, chargé de l’administration et de la modération de l’application. Le demandeur reçoit ensuite un courriel confirmant la création de son compte.

composedOf.label: Create a version
composedOf.description:
To deposit a version, go to the Antony website https://antony-archiv.org/ and log in to your account (button at the top right). Once logged in, the user’s initials will be displayed.

A “+” button then becomes available, allowing the user to add a version. A form titled “Add a version” opens.

This form allows users to enter the name of the version to be deposited and to link it to an existing work, or to enter the name of the work if this is the first deposited version.

The “SUBMIT” button validates the creation of the version and opens its entry page. The version is then associated with a creation date and the depositor’s name.

As a depositor, a menu is available at the top right of the version entry page:

• “Upload a new archive” opens a dialog allowing the user to select the ZIP file of the version to be deposited.

• The “SUBMIT” button uploads the ZIP archive from the local storage to Antony[1]. A progress bar is displayed during the upload. A second progress bar then appears during real-time unzipping, which extracts the full file structure[2].

[1] Only users with access rights to the files can open or download them from the interface.
[2] During this second operation, which may take some time, the user may log out without interrupting the process.

French:

5. Créer une version

Pour déposer une version, il convient de se rendre sur le site d’Antony https://antony-archiv.org/ et de se connecter à son compte (bouton en haut à droite). Une fois connecté, les initiales de l’utilisateur apparaissent.

Un bouton « + » devient alors доступible et permet d’« ajouter » une version. Un formulaire intitulé « Ajouter une version » s’ouvre.

Ce formulaire permet de renseigner le nom de la version à déposer et de la rattacher à une œuvre existante, ou de saisir le nom de l’œuvre s’il s’agit de la première version déposée.

Le bouton « SOUMETTRE » valide la création de la version et ouvre sa page de saisie. La version est alors associée à une date de création ainsi qu’au nom du déposant.

En tant que déposant, un menu est disponible en haut à droite de la page de saisie de la version :

• « Téléverser une nouvelle archive » ouvre une fenêtre permettant de sélectionner le fichier ZIP de la version à déposer.

• Le bouton « SOUMETTRE » permet d’envoyer, depuis l’espace de stockage local, le dossier ZIP de l’archive de la version à téléverser sur Antony[1]. Une barre de progression s’affiche pendant le téléversement. Une seconde barre apparaît ensuite lors du dézippage en temps réel, qui permet d’extraire l’ensemble de l’arborescence des fichiers[2].

[1] Seuls les utilisateurs disposant des droits d’accès aux fichiers peuvent les ouvrir et les télécharger depuis l’interface.
[2] Pendant cette seconde opération, qui peut prendre un certain temps, l’utilisateur peut se déconnecter du site sans interrompre le processus.

composedOf.label: Enter the details of the deposited version
Submit an archive
composedOf.description:
Depositing a version of a work consists of uploading a compressed ZIP archive of the electronic components of the work and documenting it within the Antony application.

A version deposited on Antony may have different statuses. The first status is “draft”, which keeps the version in the database inaccessible to the public (visible only to the depositor). The second status is “published”, which makes the version publicly visible.

To be published, the depositor must submit a request via the “submission” menu. The editorial committee then reviews the version and may approve its publication, possibly subject to modifications requested from the depositor.

Depositing a version is only possible when the depositor holds all necessary rights to do so (including copyright clearance for the deposited materials).

French:

7. Déposer une archive

Le dépôt d’une version d’une œuvre consiste à téléverser, dans l’application Antony, une archive compressée au format ZIP contenant les éléments électroniques de cette œuvre, ainsi qu’à la documenter.

Une version déposée sur Antony peut avoir plusieurs statuts. Le premier statut, « brouillon », rend la version inaccessible au public (elle n’est visible que par le déposant). Le second statut, « publiée », rend la version accessible à tous.

Pour être publiée, une demande doit être soumise par le déposant via le menu « soumission ». Le comité éditorial examine alors la version et peut en autoriser la publication, éventuellement sous réserve de modifications demandées au déposant.

Le dépôt d’une version n’est possible que si le déposant dispose de l’ensemble des droits nécessaires (notamment les droits d’auteur relatifs aux documents déposés).

composedOf.label: Publishing a version (from draft status)
composedOf.description:
The depositor may submit a deposited version for publication.

To change a version from “draft” status to “published” status, a request must be submitted to the editorial committee, which reviews and validates it. If the request is approved, the version is published.

The editorial committee may also request modifications before authorising publication.

French:

8. Passer d’une version brouillon à une version publiée 

Le déposant peut soumettre sa version en vue de sa publication.

Pour passer du statut « brouillon » au statut « publié », une demande doit être adressée au comité éditorial, qui en assure l’évaluation et la validation. Si la demande est approuvée, la version est publiée.

Le comité éditorial peut également demander des modifications avant d’autoriser la publication.

label: SWARM-SLR - Streamlined Workflow Automation for Machine-actionable Systematic Literature Reviews
description: Authoring survey or review articles still requires significant tedious manual effort, despite many advancements in research knowledge management having the potential to improve efficiency, reproducibility, and reuse. However, these advancements bring forth an increasing number of approaches, tools, and systems, which often cover only specific stages and lack a comprehensive workflow utilizing their task-specific strengths. We propose the Streamlined Workflow Automation for Machine-actionable Systematic Literature Reviews (SWARM-SLR) to crowdsource the improvement of SLR efficiency while maintaining scientific integrity in a state-of-the-art knowledge discovery and distribution process. The workflow aims to domain-independently support researchers in collaboratively and sustainably managing the rising scholarly knowledge corpus. By synthesizing guidelines from the literature, we have composed a set of 65 requirements, spanning from planning to reporting a review. Existing tools were assessed against these requirements and synthesized into the SWARM-SLR workflow prototype, a ready-for-operation software support tool. The SWARM-SLR was evaluated via two online surveys, which largely confirmed the validity of the 65 requirements and situated 11 tools to the different life-cycle stages. The SWARM-SLR workflow was similarly evaluated and found to be supporting almost the entire span of an SLR, excelling specifically in search and retrieval, information extraction, knowledge synthesis, and distribution. Our SWARM-SLR requirements and workflow support tool streamlines the SLR support for researchers, allowing sustainable collaboration by linking individual efficiency improvements to crowdsourced knowledge management. If these efforts are continued, we expect the increasing number of tools to be manageable and usable inside fully structured, (semi-)automated literature review workflows.

label: Task of the XML files translator supporting vocabulary and preserving input files structure
description:
ATRIUM - LINDAT XML Translation Workflow

Overview
The atrium-translator is a modular Python wrapper developed to interface seamlessly with the LINDAT Translation API. This tool is strictly optimized for processing XML documents and their direct derivatives, specifically focusing on ALTO XML documents and AMCR metadata records. It safely translates structural text while maintaining the complex schema and namespaces of the original files.

Core Translation Pipeline Logic
The translation workflow follows a structured pipeline designed to protect context, formatting, and domain terminology:

Language Detection: The text undergoes source language identification using Facebook's FastText models. If the confidence score is below 0.2, the system utilizes an intelligent fallback and defaults to Czech (cs) to prevent pipeline interruptions.

Tag-and-Protect Vocabulary Strategy: To ensure domain-specific terminology is not garbled by the Neural Machine Translation (NMT) model, users can supply a vocabulary CSV. Multi-word phrases are matched via case-insensitive substring matching (favoring the longest match first). Single-word terms are matched by their underlying lemma using the LINDAT UDPipe API. These matched terms are replaced with temporary __TERM_N__ placeholder tags prior to the API call, bypassing translation, and are restored to their specified target language equivalents afterward.

Space-Aware Chunking: When dispatching text to the LINDAT Translation API (v2), the script intelligently segments text larger than 4,000 characters at the nearest space. This protects word boundaries and prevents API truncation errors.

Specialized Operating Modes

1. ALTO XML Mode
Triggered via the --alto flag, this mode is explicitly built for OCR/ALTO transcription documents. It natively traverses down to the String level and extracts the CONTENT attributes. Instead of translating word-by-word (which loses context), it reconstructs the entire TextLine for API submission, and carefully redistributes the translated output back into the individual CONTENT attributes.

2. AMCR Metadata Mode
Designed to safely modify structured archaeological and cultural heritage metadata without breaking XML validation. Target elements are dynamically specified via a list of XPaths (e.g., amcr-fields.txt). It features deep recursive namespace extraction to navigate complex OAI-PMH XML envelopes safely. Outputs can be actively validated against a provided XSD schema (e.g., the AISCR schema) to guarantee structural integrity post-translation.

Quality Assurance & Data Provenance
To support scientific integrity and ease of review, the tool automatically generates comprehensive provenance data:

Line-by-Line CSV Logging: A supplementary QA CSV log (original_filename_log.csv) is written alongside every output file, allowing researchers to manually cross-reference the text_source_lang directly with the text_target_lang on a per-line or per-XPath basis.

Paradata JSON Logs: A ParadataLogger captures run-level provenance metadata, aggregating counts, timing, processed formats, and skipped files into a serialized JSON file within a dedicated paradata directory.

Additional Utilities
Automated Vocabulary Harvesting: The repository includes a helper script (load_vocab.py) that can programmatically download and merge Czech-to-English domain vocabularies from both the AMCR OAI-PMH API and the TEATER GraphQL API into a ready-to-use CSV format.

relatedItems.label: Semi-automated extraction of information from textual documents in a domain-specific repository
relatedItems.description:
The workflow addresses the **machine processing and enhancement of archaeological textual documents** (e.g., grey literature, excavation reports, field forms) held in a domain-specific repository. It processes both **scanned documents**, through automatic text recognition, and **born-digital documents** (PDF, DOCX) that already carry a text layer. The goal is an integrated solution for **legacy data and new uploads within the selected repository system**: better search and reuse of the documents, and fewer manual steps in archiving and annotation.

The workflow chains **independent tools available as services through APIs**. Each tool performs one step: page classification, OCR quality control, linguistic annotation and named entity recognition, keyword extraction against the domain vocabularies, and translation. Each tool can also be used on its own. The repository calls the services asynchronously and stores every result as an **alternative distribution of the original file**, with a **paradata** record describing the run that produced it (tool version, parameters, licence).

The results of all steps also accumulate in **one JSON record per document** (the ATRIUM document record). Its blocks each have one producing tool, so any step can be re-run alone. The record carries the provenance of every contribution, and the licence of the combined result is derived from the most restrictive licence among them. It can later be exported as an RO-Crate.

The enriched data support:

* full-text and faceted search by page types, named entities and vocabulary keywords,
* assessment of OCR quality before further processing,
* linking of documents to controlled vocabularies and to each other,
* international access through English translations of metadata and texts,
* corpora for natural language processing, including the training and evaluation of models.

The tools were developed in the [ATRIUM project](https://atrium-research.eu/) by the Institute of Formal and Applied Linguistics (Charles University) with the Institutes of Archaeology of the Czech Academy of Sciences in Prague and Brno. They are open source, published as container images, and are described in their own Marketplace records. Their integration into [Galaxy](https://galaxyproject.org/) is being prepared with DARIAH.

The [Archaeological Map of the Czech Republic (AMCR)](https://digiarchiv.aiscr.cz/) repository serves as the **demonstrator** of the workflow.

**Diagram caption**: *Users and data curators work with a data repository (AMCR) that stores each document with its metadata, original file, ALTO XML, document record, enrichments and paradata, and the AMCR vocabularies. A processing orchestration (step 2) passes documents between the repository, a separate automatic text recognition workflow (step 4) and the ATRIUM tool services: page classification (3), ALTO post-processing and quality control (5), NLP enrichment with UDPipe and NameTag to TEITOK (7), vocabulary keywords by LLM (8) and XML translation (10). A dashed born-digital branch (6) replaces steps 4 and 5. NLP enrichment and translation call the LINDAT services; the vocabularies feed keyword extraction and translation. Annotators and data engineers train a custom NameTag model (9). A discovery service (11) serves users and feeds the OAI-PMH and File API, which feeds the ARIADNE Portal.*

relatedItems.label: Using GoTriple data for your SSH data science tasks
relatedItems.description:
This workflow explains how to use GoTriple data on Social Sciences and Humanities (SSH) for data analytics tasks.

[GoTriple](https://gotriple.eu) is the discovery platform for the SSH: it currently indexes metadata of almost 19,5 million documents, over 25,000 projects and about 22,5 million author profiles. The extreme diversity of SSH is well represented, in its multivaried aspects, in the platform: on the one hand, GoTriple’s documents cover 27 disciplines within SSH, from History to Literature, from Management to Gender Studies. 

Moreover GoTriple is inherently multilingual, indexing documents in over 20 languages but also providing its user interface localised in 10 European languages. Finally, diversity also applies to the nature of its documents, with a high representation of textual content (articles, thesis, reports, books,...) but also a significant amount of datasets, multimedia assets and software artefacts with their number expected to increase in the coming months.

This workflow explains in practice, with code examples, how GoTriple data can be used by Digital Humanists for data analytics tasks.

There are **two ways** to do so:
- by using the data dumps created and published in Zenodo (last update May 18, 2025);
- by using GoTriple APIs, to extract data from the online platform.

**What to use:**
If you just need a subset of GoTriple publications that have a link to their PDF, the data dumps are the quickest way to get you started. Also this is the suggested way if you don’t want to write code to get GoTriple data.

On the other hand, use the APIs if:
a) you need access to the most recent version of the data; 
b) you need to include publications without a full-text; 
c) if you need access to a very specific subset of the data and you want to apply custom filtering conditions.

**Workflow Code**
A Jupyter Notebook with ready-to-use examples is available and it is the base for this workflow [go‑triple_stats‑with‑zenodo.ipynb[(https://github.com/odoma-ch/gotriple-data-utils/blob/main/gotriple_stats-with-zenodo.ipynb).
This Jupyter notebook provides hands-on examples of how to process GoTriple data dumps and integrate analytics workflows via Python or similar tooling. Familiarize yourself with its structure, required dependencies (e.g., pandas, requests), and typical processing pipelines (such as metadata loading, parsing, filtering, aggregation, and visualization).
Also, familiarize yourself with GoTriple data model, which is fully described in the TRIPLE Project deliverable D2.5: [https://zenodo.org/records/7359654](https://zenodo.org/records/7359654).

composedOf.label: Read data files, extract abstracts in specified language(s)
composedOf.description: Once the compressed data files containing the GoTriple abstracts have been obtained, the next step is to read and parse the JSONL records from the compressed file, extracting abstracts in the specified language(s) for further processing. In the [example Python notebook](https://github.com/cbinding/rematch2/blob/main/ATRIUM_T3_4_IE_gotriple_abstracts.ipynb) associated with this workflow, abstracts in English, French and Spanish are extracted from the downloaded compressed data file.

composedOf.label: Configure and apply information extraction NLP pipeline

The named periods originate from a chosen [PeriodO](https://perio.do/) authority. This workflow includes an exemplar source code demonstrator in the form of [a Jupyter notebook](https://github.com/cbinding/rematch2/blob/main/ATRIUM_T3_4_IE_gotriple_abstracts.ipynb), and the techniques are described more fully in the workflow *Vocabulary-driven Information Extraction*.

relatedItems.label: spaCy
relatedItems.description: spaCy is an open-source software library for advanced natural language processing, written in the programming languages Python and Cython. The library is published under the MIT license and currently offers statistical neural network models for English, German, Spanish, Portuguese, French, Italian, Dutch and multi-language NER, as well as tokenization for various other languages. Unlike NLTK, which is widely used for teaching and research, spaCy focuses on providing software for production usage. As of version 1.0, spaCy also supports deep learning workflows that allow connecting statistical models trained by popular machine learning libraries like TensorFlow, Keras, Scikit-learn or PyTorch. spaCy's machine learning library, Thinc, is also available as a separate open-source Python library. It features convolutional neural network models for part-of-speech tagging, dependency parsing and named entity recognition, as well as API improvements around training and updating models, and constructing custom processing pipelines.

label: TextGrid - Import Workflow for Data aka The Fluffy Import
description:
How do I import textual research data in the TextGrid Repository?

Researchers repeatedly articulate their need for well-usable tools and infrastructures for the easy creation and publication of text-based research data. This also applies to Text+ and is exemplified by the Text+ User Stories. The partners involved in Text+, including SUB Göttingen, GWDG, and TU Dresden, contribute to this—for example, with the new developments tested at the 2024 Code Sprint for Humanities Data.

Thanks to its extensive, searchable, and reusable collection of texts and images, TextGridRep is an important and relevant repository for humanities research data.

For researchers, it offers a sustainable, permanent, and secure means of citable publication of their research data and a clear description of the same through necessary and extended metadata so that the publication in TextGridRep can be presented and reused. Results were achieved on various levels, which were presented and used on the occasion of the Code Sprint. TextGridRep was further developed in terms of authentication, the presentation of unpublished projects, and data intake. A new tool was developed for generating the required TextGrid metadata files, which detects the metadata in the teiHeader elements of the input files and also allows the manual setting of values and rules for their discovery. A web-based tool enabling convenient workflow operation was implemented as a Jupyter Notebook. For easy use of this tool, the Text+ JupyterHub is available. It was also adapted on this occasion so that the mentioned tools are already installed and can be used without further ado.

This workflow describes the new fluffy import in the TextGrid Repository.

relatedItems.label: tg-model - TextGrid Import Modeller
relatedItems.description:
Whats the aim?
This project focuses on attemps for a simple import of text corpora (encoded in XML/TEI) to TextGrid Repository by modeling the required metadata file structure.

To generate the TextGrid metadata files, the tool tg-model was developed, which can be used as a Python library and on the command line. The metadata files are important for good searchability and presentation of the imported data. The more detailed and precise the metadata in these files is, the better the data can be found in the portal and search results can be faceted. Typically, TEI files already contain metadata in the teiHeader element. These can be used for the content of the metadata files. However, since TEI allows many ways to mark the same information, the automated mapping of TEI metadata to the corresponding TextGrid metadata presents a challenge. The tg-model tool supports this task in several ways: In the first step, configuration files are generated that contain settings for the TextGrid metadata and indicate what values they have or where they can be found in the teiHeader (specified as an XPath expression). As far as the same information is found in the same place in the teiHeader in several files in a corpus, the corresponding XPath expression is written into the configuration files. The configuration files can then be adjusted. Subsequently, based on the configuration files and the input data, the metadata files are generated. Now everything necessary is available to import data into TextGridRep.

relatedItems.label: tgadmin - TextGrid repository administration cli tool, based on tgclients
relatedItems.description:
What is the aim?
A command line tool for managing your projects in the TextGrid repository without TextGridLab.

The actual data import is finally carried out by the Python tools tgadmin and tgclients, which in turn communicate with the TextGrid backend via the various TextGridRep APIs. Altogether, this forms the foundation for the new, simple way to comfortably import and ultimately publish data in TextGridRep. The tools, libraries, and also the TextGridRep API were expanded and revised on the occasion of the Code Sprint.

relatedItems.label: TextGrid Repository & Laboratory
relatedItems.description:
TextGrid is a virtual research environment for text-based humanities scholarship. It offers a variety of tools and services for collaboratively creating, analyzing, editing, and publishing texts. The TextGrid environment is split into two components, the Laboratory housing the tools and services, and the Repository for preserving reserach data and making it available to other scholars.

The [TextGrid Laboratory](https://textgrid.de/werkzeuge/) : Open source tools and services support Humanities scholars during the entire process of research, especially in digital scholarly editing.

The [TextGrid Repository](https://textgridrep.org/?lang=en) : The long-term research data archive offers safe storing, publishing and researching versatile digital material (XML/TEI formatted text and images), e.g., in the Digital Library of TextGrid. Certified with the Core Trust Seal.

The TextGrid Community: An online help, tutorials, mailing lists, a bug tracker and the source code enable users and developers to quickly start working with TextGrid.

This resource is supported by Text+. In case of questions you may get in touch with the Text+ helpdesk at textplus-support@gwdg.de.

label: The Sound-Text Archive of Muslim Women of West Africa (STAMWWA)
description:
The Sound-Text Archive of Muslim Women of West Africa (STAMWWA) is a multilingual, intermedial auditory platform that conveys the audible accounts of a group of Muslim women from West Africa and its diaspora. This archive, which originated from a teaching module, a conference, and a questionnaire sent through WhatsApp, amalgamates narratives addressing contemporary issues surrounding faith and practice while promoting the use of African languages.

The primary objectives of STAMWWA are:

To explore community archives and practices within the field of digital sound/humanities
To investigate how these practices intersect with digital infrastructures, addressing protocols and ethical concerns
To reveal nuanced dynamics of meaning versus textual dominance in the pedagogy of monotheistic epistemologies
To showcase a factual digital practice originating from West Africa centered on sound and its association with or independence from a post/decolonial perspective

composedOf.label: Step One: Adapting the topic and the research rationale to the itinerary and standards of a workflow
composedOf.description: Built and inspired from real life, the significance of the workflow centres on conveying the auditory narratives of Muslim women across West Africa and its diaspora. It also centres on questioning and addressing the predominance of textual sources versus sound sources in Islamic epistemology (ʿilm) and exploring new intermedial multimodal modes of knowledge transmission and technology

composedOf.label: Step Two: Checking and browsing existing materials and resources
composedOf.description: I checked existing materials and resources (data sets, audio collections, tools services, training materials, publications and datasets, workflows) in the Virtual Language Observatory (VLO) and Social Sciences and Humanities Open Cloud Marketplace (SSHOC). Browsing in these infrastructures and choosing broad terms such has “Islam”, “Women”, “Muslim”, “West Africa”, did not bring significant if not any results.

composedOf.label: Step Three: Categorising audio data
composedOf.description: Regarding the reception of audio data, three different types of audio can be catalogued. Firstly, audios as voice recordings; secondly, WhatsApp messages; thirdly, handwritten responses. Handwritten responses can also be catalogued as captured images of written responses to the questionnaire and responses written over the printed questionnaire.

composedOf.label: Step Four: Addressing Non-Fluid Audio-Data Flows: The Tangibility of Data in West Africa
composedOf.description: One of the main challenges in this initiative was the significant technical limitation that affected (and affects) any kind of practical digital research within the context of West Africa. Power cuts are frequent and an unstable electrical supply does not allow a fluid audio reception. Additionally, data access still heavily depends on the physical top-up of SIM cards for 3G connectivity. This reflects infrastructural gaps related to broadband access but mostly fibre-optic cables.  The Submarine Cable Map,  developed by TeleGeography is a powerful resource that shows the extensive network of submarine fibre optic cables. As cables form the backbone of global internet connectivity, it was essential to bring to the STAMWWA, Dr Jess Auerbach Jahajeeah’s extensive research fieldwork on fibre cables, especially those that surround Africa and spurs (the equivalent of off-ramps on the road).

composedOf.label: Step Five: Storage, Access And New Ethical And Technological Assessment
composedOf.description: Initially, I decided to store audios on my personal website to provide a non-academic, non-institutional environment that offered an unmediated space for participants. However, this approach presented many challenges: the digital security risks and potential vulnerabilities. Anonymity protocols require constant revision to prevent obsolescence.  In search of ethical, reproducible, and sustainable workflows, I was introduced to Dr Charlotte Bosseaux. Her project, Whose Voice Is it Anyway?,  explores the ethical complexities of translating gender-based violence and has led to a collaborative series of annual events with academics and professional translators, organized alongside the European Commission. Additionally, I consulted with Dr Tanya Clement and the team at Brumfield Labs—Ben Brumfield, Sara Brumfield, and colleagues at the University of Texas— who have developed the tool AudiAnnotate. As an interoperable framework for annotation, it allowed the annotation of the audios. It comes associated with an IIIF-compliant manifest that points directly to audio files. At present, audio files are stored on a personal drive, and full recordings are available upon request.

label: Tracking the dissemination of a specific work
description: In medieval studies, the dissemination of a work can give important information on life and movements of the author; plus, it can influence local history and everyday activities: i.e. some medical practices were performed just in places where the work carrying information about them was spread. Moreover, it can be useful also to understand if the work was disseminated alone or together with other works, and why: for instance, in medieval universities the essential works for the study of a discipline were often gathered in the same manuscript. Therefore, scholars may have interest in the itinerary made by a given work, and may want to track it.

relatedItems.label: CERL Portal
relatedItems.description: The CERL Portal provides access to distributed databases containing manuscript materials, printed works, photographic material and other special materials. label: Transcribing conversation in ELAN
description:
This workflow outlines the main steps involved in the transcription of conversational data using ELAN, a software environment designed for the annotation and synchronisation of audio and video recordings. ELAN is particularly suitable for multimodal transcription, as it allows the annotation of both verbal and non-verbal phenomena — such as gaze, gestures, pauses, and interactional dynamics — through multiple time-aligned annotation tiers.

The workflow includes the preliminary design of the transcription scheme and annotation hierarchy, the configuration of tiers and segmentation units, the automatic or manual transcription and annotation process, and the exportation of the final transcript in EAF or other formats. 

This workflow is based on Letizia Cirillo’s chapter “Trascrivere la conversazione” (pp. 181–188), part of the "Vademecum per il trattamento delle fonti orali" (Tavolo permanente per le fonti orali, 2020).

Rather than replacing the recording with a transcription, this process structures the resource into titled, synopsised, and keyworded segments, enabling users to navigate directly to specific points in the interview and locate content by person, place, or institution. By preserving the double voice of interviewer and interviewee at segment level and by using indexing — rather than transcription — as the primary access tool, the workflow supports listening to the original recording as the main mode of engagement with the source, in line with the stated aim of guiding and educating listening. This kind of indexing can be carried out either through OHMS (Oral History Metadata Synchronizer) or without the support of any dedicated application. The output is a reviewed, structured index suitable for publication.

relatedItems.label: ELAN
relatedItems.description:
ELAN is a tool for creating annotations on multiple layers on audio and video resources. The textual content of annotations is in Unicode and the transcription is stored in XML.

With ELAN a user can add an unlimited number of textual annotations to audio and/or video recordings. An annotation can be a sentence, word or gloss, a comment, translation or a description of any feature observed in the media. Annotations can be created on multiple layers, called tiers. Tiers can be hierarchically interconnected. An annotation can either be time-aligned to the media or it can refer to other existing annotations. The content of annotations consists of Unicode text and annotation documents are stored in an XML format (EAF).

Main features and characteristics of ELAN:
* provides several ways to view the annotations, each view is connected to and synchronized with the media timeline
* supports creation of multiple tiers and tier hierarchies
* supports Controlled Vocabularies
* allows linking of up to 4 video files with an annotation document
* media support
   * builds on existing, native media frameworks, like Windows Media Player, QuickTime or VLC
   * support for audio and video formats depends on operating system, high performance media playback can usually be achieved
* technical
   * written in the Java programming language
   * distributions available for Windows, macOS and Linux
   * open source, the sources are available under a GPL 3 license 

The solution was developed by the Language Archive of the Max Planck Institute for Psycholinguistics.

relatedItems.label: Annotating Proxemic Features in Audiovisual Document Using ELAN

This workflow describes how to annotate proxemic features in audiovisual corpora using ELAN. It integrates multimodal annotation principles from linguistic and semiotic research, with particular reference to gesture classification frameworks (Kendon, McNeill) and facial annotation protocols (FACS, Ekman & Friesen).

This process is grounded on Meluzzi’s approach to annotation ("Annotare una trascrizione", in "Vademecum per il trattamento delle fonti orali", pp. 227-229).

relatedItems.label: Treating Oral Sources in SSH Research
relatedItems.description:
This workflow, developed in Italy, guides SSH researchers, archivists, and institutions through the full lifecycle of oral sources: from initial legal and ethical preparation, through fieldwork and documentation, to long-term preservation, archival transfer, access, and valorisation, including responsible online publication. It covers the production of audio or audiovisual recordings, their contextual documentation, and their integration into archival systems.

The workflow applies equally to newly initiated oral data gathering campaigns and to the retrospective treatment of pre-existing collections. It draws on the "Vademecum per il trattamento delle fonti orali" (Ministero della Cultura, Direzione Generale Archivi, 2023), a multidisciplinary reference document developed by specialists from different domains, including oral historians, linguists, ethnologists, librarians and archivists.

While it integrates European data protection requirements (GDPR) and established professional standards, it also refers at certain points to the Italian legal framework. Researchers operating in other national contexts should therefore consult the relevant legislation and guidelines applicable in their own country.

relatedItems.label: Vademecum per il trattamento delle fonti orali
relatedItems.description: Starting from a broader definition of oral sources and from the assumption of the unity of the communicative event that generates the source—and, consequently, the archive of oral sources—this Vademecum provides a coherent theoretical framework, not merely prescriptive, to which methods and practices for the treatment of oral documentation can be anchored.

composedOf.label: Determine what you need to transcribe
composedOf.description:
Transcription is always the result of choices. Its adequacy depends on the type of data and the research questions being addressed. The first step is therefore to delimit the field: what aspects of the interaction are relevant to your analysis, and at what level of detail do you need to capture them? A highly granular transcription — one that captures speech, prosody, gaze, gesture, posture, and object manipulation simultaneously — makes the data reusable for many purposes, but produces a transcript that is considerably more complex to read. A more selective transcription is easier to follow but may omit features that turn out to be analytically relevant later.

This tension between comprehensiveness and specialisation is one of the central methodological considerations in CA transcription practice. A useful guiding principle: if in doubt, transcribe more rather than less — it is easier to omit tiers at the reading stage than to re-transcribe a corpus from scratch.

composedOf.label: Configure ELAN
composedOf.description:
A. Decide on the tiers you will create in ELAN

In ELAN, different dimensions of the interaction are organised into tiers — separate annotation layers that run in parallel and are aligned to the same time axis. Tiers can be given names, associated with specific participants, and arranged into hierarchies (a gloss tier may depend on a speech tier, for instance). It is also possible to add a transcriber comments tier for observations that should not be confused with the primary data.

B. Create the project and import media
Open ELAN and create a new annotation file (.eaf). Link your audio and/or video file(s) to the project. It is possible to link multiple media streams simultaneously, which is particularly useful for multi-party interaction data. The media files are not embedded in the .eaf file but referenced by path, so keep your folder structure stable throughout the project. PLEASE NOTE: to handle media files with different zero points or start times use synchonisation or adjust time offsets for secondary media files.

C. Define the tier hierarchy
Create your tiers according to the plan established in A. For each tier, specify: its name, the participant it is associated with (if applicable), its type (time-alignable, or dependent on a parent tier), and any linguistic type or vocabulary constraint you wish to apply. ELAN supports hierarchical relationships between tiers.

Assign clear, consistent names to your tiers from the outset. Renaming tiers later is possible but can create complications if tier names are referenced in templates or export settings.

composedOf.label: Import a transcription or transcribe
composedOf.description:
Annotate speech, prosody, non-verbal behaviour, and paralinguistic features. 

A. Transcribe speech using Jefferson conventions
Enter the verbal transcription in the speech tiers, one turn at a time, following the Jefferson system (G. Jefferson, Glossary of 'Transcript Symbols with an Introduction', in G.H. Lerner (ed.), "Conversation Analysis. Studies from the First Generation", Amsterdam/Philadelphia, John Benjamins, 2004, pp. 13-31.). The transcript is laid out vertically according to turn sequence; each turn is associated with a speaker identifier and, in ELAN, aligned to a time interval in the recording. Overlapping talk is marked with square brackets [ ] at the point where it begins and ends across the relevant tiers. It should be noted, however, that these brackets are not automatically generated by ELAN but are added manually. This point is important because conversation analysts working within the Jeffersonian transcription tradition—where the alignment of overlapping speech is visually reproduced on the page using vertically synchronized square brackets—may expect a comparable output. In ELAN, overlap is instead primarily represented through separate tiers and synchronized timestamps. Reproducing the conventional Jefferson-style layout therefore requires exporting the transcript (for instance into Word), using a monospaced font such as Courier, and often manually adjusting the alignment of the strings. 
Prosodic and voice quality features are noted inline using the standard symbols.

ELAN allows you to play short loops, slow down the audio, and zoom into the waveform display while annotating, which considerably aids the transcription of rapid, overlapping, or unclear speech.

B. Transcribe non-verbal behaviour
For audio-visual data, annotate non-verbal actions — gesture, gaze, posture, object manipulation — in the corresponding tiers, following the Mondada conventions. Each embodied action is described in plain language within angle-bracket-delimited strings, synchronised with the speech tier via time codes and shared symbols. The symbols mark the preparation, apex, and retraction phases of a movement, and indicate whether the action begins before the extract, continues beyond it, or is captured at a precise moment by a video frame reference (#).

Non-verbal actions often do not map neatly onto turn boundaries: a gesture may begin several syllables before the relevant word, or continue after the turn has ended. ELAN's multi-tier, time-aligned interface is designed precisely to capture this temporal complexity.

C. Add a working translation if needed
For multilingual data, or when the corpus will be shared with readers unfamiliar with the language of the interaction, it is useful to add a translation tier aligned to each speech tier. This working translation is not part of the primary transcription data but serves as an access tool. It should be clearly labelled as a gloss and not confused with the transcription itself.

relatedItems.label: Multiple Temporalities of Language and Body in Interaction: Challenges for Transcribing Multimodality
relatedItems.description:
The article focuses on the principles of multimodal CA, the way they can be operationalized in a transcription system, and the analytical and conceptual consequences of transcription choices. Elaborating on the foundations of multimodal CA and on the basis of video recordings of French and Swiss German encounters, as well as animal interactions, the article discusses classic and contemporary challenges for transcription and analysis, such as beyond gesture and gaze, body arrangements in interactional spaces, larger groups, material environments, mobile settings, silent activities, and animal encounters. It also highlights the diversity of multimodal practices involved: mobilizing occasioned
material resources, movements not only of the upper (head, gesture) but also the lower (feet, legs, posterior) parts of the body, haptic contacts touching objects and coparticipants, and camera movements. The precise transcription of relevant details reveals complex arrangements of multimodal resources and
gestalts. Their fine-grained, distinct, multiple temporalities constitute the basis of their sequential order—for sequentiality as a fundamental organizational principle of action. Data are in French and Swiss German.

composedOf.label: Review and normalise
composedOf.description:
A. Review the transcription against the recording
Once a first version of the transcription is complete, go through it systematically against the recording. Check the accuracy of verbal transcription, the alignment of time codes, the placement of overlap brackets, and the descriptions of non-verbal actions. Transcription is an iterative process: it is normal to revise notation choices as familiarity with the data deepens and analytical hypotheses take shape.

B. Ensure internal consistency
A well-formed transcription requires a one-to-one correspondence between symbol and phenomenon: the same symbol should always represent the same feature, and the same feature should always be represented by the same symbol. Review your transcription for inconsistencies — particularly in the notation of overlaps, pauses, prosodic features, and non-verbal descriptions — and harmonise them. Any residual inconsistency should be noted in the transcriber comments tier.

label: Transcribing Documents of Ethnomusicological Interest
description:
This workflow describes a structured process for transcribing sound and audiovisual documents of ethnomusicological interest — recordings that may contain musical performances, ritual and festive events, ethnographic interviews, or informal conversations from oral tradition contexts. It is designed for researchers, archivists, and cultural heritage professionals working with collections held in ethnomusicological archives (such as those of national and regional sound heritage institutions) or with field recordings produced by researchers or local cultural actors.

The workflow allows practitioners to determine, case by case, whether a verbal utterance embedded in a sound document should be transcribed as ordinary speech, as sung text, or as musical notation — and to combine these approaches when the material requires it. It is particularly useful when working with oral-tradition repertoires, where melodic, rhythmic, and textual elements interact in complex and sometimes idiosyncratic ways, and where a purely textual or purely musical transcription alone would fail to capture the full technical, formal, and cultural dimension of the performance.

The process was elaborated by Claudio Rizzoni (Soprintendenza ABAP di Genova e La Spezia and ICBSA), drawing on established ethnomusicological transcription methodologies developed over the course of the twentieth century, and is intended to be applied flexibly according to the research context, the purpose of the transcription, and the specific musical culture and repertoire concerned.

composedOf.label: Identify the Type of Content in the Document
composedOf.description: Begin by reviewing the sound or audiovisual document to identify what kind of verbal content it contains. Ethnomusicological documents are highly varied: alongside musical performances, they may record festive or ritual events, ethnographic interviews, or informal conversations. Each of these may contain verbal utterances that function as oral sources — whether exchanged in interviews and informal talk, or recited, declaimed, or sung. At this stage, the goal is simply to map out what is present in the document before deciding how each part should be handled. This initial inventory determines which later steps of the workflow apply: non-sung verbal content will follow standard ethnographic or historical transcription practice, while sung content requires the specific considerations described in the steps below. Where the document includes instrumental music, or vocal music without linguistic content, this should also be noted, since it remains equally relevant to musical transcription even though it falls outside the scope of textual transcription.

composedOf.label: Separate Non-Sung and Sung Verbal Utterances
composedOf.description: Once the content has been mapped, distinguish clearly between verbal utterances that are spoken (as in interviews or informal conversation) and those that are sung. This distinction matters because the two categories do not pose the same transcription challenges. Spoken utterances can generally be transcribed following the same conventions used for other ethnographic or historical sources, without requiring special methodological adjustments. Sung utterances, by contrast, combine a verbal text with a musical performance, and this dual nature calls for specific care in how they are rendered in writing. Making this separation explicit at an early stage avoids applying unnecessarily complex methods to material that does not require them, while ensuring that sung passages are flagged for the more elaborate treatment described in the following steps.

composedOf.label: Transcribe Non-Sung Utterances Using Standard Conventions
composedOf.description: For verbal content identified as spoken rather than sung, proceed with transcription using the same methodological and conventional choices applied to other ethnographic or historical sources. No additional ethnomusicological considerations are needed at this stage, since the complexity introduced by musical performance does not apply here. The specific conventions to adopt (level of detail, treatment of hesitations, dialect features, etc.) should be chosen according to the aims of the broader research project, consistent with general practice for oral source transcription.

composedOf.label: Decide Between Textual, Musical, or Combined Transcription for Sung Content
composedOf.description: For sung utterances, determine which transcription approach — or combination of approaches — best serves the purpose of the work. Textual transcription renders the verbal text alone, offering greater readability and a clearer sense of the text's metrical structure, but omits all information about its musical character. Musical transcription instead treats the sung text as a component of a musical performance, allowing formal features such as melodic profile, rhythm, and vocal timbre to be captured with a precision that depends on the methodology used. Where the aim is to convey both the verbal and musical dimensions of the sung passage as precisely as possible, combining both types of transcription is the only approach capable of doing so; this is especially recommended whenever the material has genuine ethnomusicological relevance, even in research where ethnomusicology is not the central focus. In such cases, the transcription should be entrusted to a specialist with prior experience in the musical culture and repertoire concerned.

composedOf.label: Take Into Account the Oral-Tradition Context of the Performance
composedOf.description: Before transcribing sung material, consider the conditions under which such performances are typically produced. Ethnomusicological musical performances belong predominantly to oral-tradition contexts, where reference models are learned by memory and subject to variation, and where performers may generate new forms spontaneously from implicit generative rules. This is especially visible in the many forms of improvisation found in oral musical traditions, which can affect both the sung verbal text and other, more specifically musical elements. Recognizing this variability in advance helps the transcriber anticipate and accurately represent idiosyncratic features of the performance rather than normalizing them away.

composedOf.label: Assess the Relationship Between Musical Form and Sung Text
composedOf.description: Examine how the musical form and the sung text condition one another in the specific performance being transcribed, since this relationship follows different logics depending on the musical genre. It should not be assumed that the metrical patterns of the "textual component" always take precedence over the metrical-rhythmic patterns of the "musical component." In many cases, identifiable metrical models of the sung text are manipulated or overturned in performance by rhythmic and broader musical logic. Understanding this interplay before transcribing helps determine how much weight to give textual versus musical structure in the final transcription, and flags cases where the sung text's apparent metre may not correspond to what is actually performed.

composedOf.label: Produce the Textual Transcription of Sung Utterances
composedOf.description: When producing a textual transcription of sung content, aim to restitute all idiosyncratic elements that characterize the specific execution of the piece, not just a normalized version of the text. This includes accounting for redundancies, pauses, the decomposition or aggregation of verse lines, and any performance errors. The textual transcription of sung utterances follows the same conventional and methodological options used for other types of utterance, and the choice of convention should be evaluated according to the specific case and the aims of the research.

composedOf.label: Produce the Musical Transcription of Sung Utterances
composedOf.description: For the musical transcription, apply established ethnomusicological methodologies, most of which have been consolidated over decades of disciplinary practice. For vocal music from Italian and European oral-tradition repertoires in particular, the most suitable methods rely on standard Western musical notation, supplemented with appropriate diacritical signs capable of highlighting formal elements not accounted for in the Western art-music system — for instance, intervals that fall outside the tempered system. As with textual transcription, the musical transcription should capture the idiosyncratic features of the actual execution, since this reflects the technical, formal, and cultural dimension of the singing.

composedOf.label: Complement Transcription with Acoustic Analysis Tools
composedOf.description: Recognize that musical transcription functions as one tool among several for representing and analyzing musical sound, and has historically been used alongside other methods. Where appropriate, make use of specific acoustic analysis software capable of extracting data and generating graphic representations of the sound parameters relevant to musicological and ethnomusicological analysis — for example, tools such as Sonic Visualizer or Praat. These tools can complement written transcription by providing additional layers of analysis for the same performance.

relatedItems.description:
Praat es una herramienta para el análisis fonético del habla desarrollada por Paul Boersma y David Weenink en el Instituto de Ciencias Fonéticas de la Universidad de Ámsterdam. En este material se tratan los siguientes aspectos:

Introducción a Praat: operaciones básicas

Análisis acústico del habla

Segmentación y etiquetado

Manipulación del habla natural

Creación de estímulos sintetizados

Pruebas de identificación y de discriminación

Uso de scripts

Documentación

relatedItems.label: Praat
relatedItems.description: Praat is software for the phonetic analysis of speech, including support for articulatory and speech synthesis. It is also a computer program with which you can analyse, synthesize, and manipulate speech, and create high-quality pictures.

composedOf.label: Ensure Specialist Oversight for Sung Material
composedOf.description: Throughout the process, and particularly whenever combined textual and musical transcription of sung utterances is undertaken, ensure that the work is carried out or reviewed by a specialist with prior experience in the study of musical cultures and in the specific repertoire to which the sung utterances belong. This safeguard applies even in research projects where the ethnomusicological perspective is not the predominant focus, since accurately capturing sung material still requires this specific expertise.

label: Transcription de données de langage oral
description:
French language workflow on how one can approach the task of transcribing oral recordings, produced by the Consortium Huma-Num Corli2. The French text is followed by its English translation.

Les données de langage oral enregistrées avec un magnétophone ou une caméra vidéo peuvent être transcrites de manière orthographique (pour les langues ayant une écriture) ou phonétique. Ces transcriptions se font en alignant le résultat de la transcription et du son (ou des gestes).  Le résultat des transcriptions est largement utilisé dans la recherche en sciences du langage.

English translation

The oral language data recorded with a tape recorder or video camera can be transcribed either orthographically (for languages that have a writing system) or phonetically. These transcriptions are produced by aligning the transcription output with the sound (or gestures). The resulting transcriptions are widely used in linguistic research.

concept.label: Consortium-HN
concept.definition: The Consortiums-HN are networks of experts financed for 4 years by the IR* Huma-Num (HN), bringing together staff from French SSH research units and teams, with a variety of professions (researchers, engineers, archivists, documentalists, etc.) around common themes and/or objects for which they define shared digital procedures and standards (methods, tools, sharing of experiences). In connection with HN, they aim to create synergies within the SSH research communities to encourage their appropriation of digital tools and their insertion in Open Science, while responding to the FAIR principles.
